San Juan de los Lagos also hosted the 2018 World Cup, where Angola won their first title by beating Türkiye in the final. Türkiye are the defending champions from the 2022 tournament in Istanbul. Ghana won the African title in Egypt in 2024 and arrived in Mexico as the continent's best side. Coach Stephen Richard Obeng has said the team willcome home as world champions. The winners of Wednesday's tie go through to the quarter-finals on Thursday. The final is set for Sunday, November 22, at the San Martin field.

Title: 2026 Amputee World Cup: Ghana thrash Iraq 6-0 to book Round of 16 spot
Content: The convincing victory saw the African champions finish second in their group with four points, securing a place in the knockout stage of the competition. Hamza Mohammed and Yussif Yahaya were the stars of the encounter, scoring two goals each, while Richard Ekwam and Mohammed Mubarik also found the back of the net to complete the rout. The result marked an impressive turnaround for theBlack Challenge, who began their World Cup campaign with a disappointing 2-0 defeat to Angola. Ghanasubsequently recovered to earn a point against Colombia before producing their best performance of the group stage against Iraq. Heading into their final group fixture, the Black Challenge needed a positive result to strengthen their chances of progressing to the knockout stage. They responded emphatically, putting six goals past the Iraqis to secure their first victory of the tournament. Elsewhere in the group, Angola defeated Colombia 2-0 to finish ahead of Ghana, with the Black Challenge taking second place on four points. The qualification keeps Ghana's hopes of making a significant impact at the global tournament alive as they seek to build on their continental success. The Black Challenge entered the competition as reigning African champions, having won the 2024 African Amputee Football Cup of Nations in Egypt. Having overcome a difficult start to their campaign, Ghana will now turn their attention to the Round of 16, where they will face USA on Wednesday at 5pm Mexican time (11pm Ghana time).

Title: Maxwell Woledzi is MLS Defender of the Year after Nashville's record season
Content: Ghanaian centre-back Maxwell Woledzi is the 2026 MLS Defender of the Year, after a record-breaking debut season with Nashville SC. MLSannounced the awardon Monday, capping a debut campaign in which the 25-year-old played all 34 regular-season matches after joining from Norwegian side Fredrikstad FK. His career had earlier taken him to Portugal, where hejoined Vitoria SC in 2022. He anchored a back line that set league records for the fewest goals conceded in a 34-game season, with 25, and the most clean sheets, with 17. Nashville also lifted the Supporters' Shield with single-season records of 77 points and 23 wins against only three defeats, matching the second-best goal difference at plus 46. The club greeted the news on X with a pun on his nationality. The Ghanaian added two goals and one assist. He led all Nashville players with 44 clearances and 2,100 completed passes, and won 80 aerial duels, the third most at the club. He was the only player in the league to complete more than 2,000 passes while keeping his accuracy at 94 per cent or better. Woledzi took 33.17 per cent of the overall vote, which is decided by club technical staffs, the media and current players. He won 41.58 per cent of the media vote and 45.16 per cent of the club vote. The players could not separate the three finalists: each polled 12.77 per cent of theirs. All three finalists were Nashville players: Jeisson Palacios was second on 14.72 per cent and Andy Najar third on 9.74 per cent. He is the third Nashville player to win the prize, following Walker Zimmerman's back-to-back triumphs in 2020 and 2021, and the second African winner after Cape Verde's Steven Moreira in 2024. He succeeds Vancouver Whitecaps defender Tristan Blackmon, who won the award in 2025. Woledzi's triumph adds to Ghana's growing presence in the league, where Osman Bukariscored his first Austin goal in a victory over Nashville. Fellow defender Alhassan "Lalas" Abubakar isanother Ghanaian to have made his mark in MLS.

Title: AFCON 2027 Q: There's nothing like competition between Benjamin Asare and I - Ati-Zigi
Content: Black Starsgoalkeeper Lawrence Ati-Zigi says there's no competition between himself and Benjamin Asare following Ghana's 1-0 win over Somalia on Monday at the Essipong Sports Stadium in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. Ati-Zigi was one of five changes made by Interim Black Stars head coach Kim Lars Bjorkegren prior to kick off. The 29-year-old replaced Benjamin Asare in goal, keeping a clean sheet in his first appearance for the Black Stars since the September international window. Since Benjamin Asare's Ghana debut in March 2025, the goalkeeping mandate has been shared amongst the two goalkeepers. At the 2026 World Cup, Zigi started the game against Panama before he was replaced by Asare in the second half due to an injury. Asare kept a clean sheet against England and conceded twice before the return of Zigi in Ghana's last 32 defeat to Colombia. "Asare played the last game and I played today's game. There's nothing like competition. We all want to help the national team," Zigi told the press. The win for Ghana has given the Black Stars a huge lifeline in their bid to secure qualification to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. Ivory Coast lead the way in Group C with nine points - with a game in hand - while Gambia follow closely in second place with six points.

Title: INTERPOL RULING: OSP failed to update “minimal” facts on Ofori-Atta’s Red Notice despite filing 78 charges
Content: Even after the Office of the Special Prosecutor filed 78 criminal charges against former Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta and seven others in the SML, the INTERPOL Red Notice issued against Mr Ofori-Atta was still based on an older warrant with “minimal factual information” that listed only one offence. This is revealed in the ruling by the Commission for the Control of INTERPOL’s Files on Ken Ofori-Atta’s Red Notice, which was deleted in February this year. The full ruling, exclusively obtained by Pledge Against Corruption, appears to fault the OSP, which filed the case through Ghana’s National Central Bureau (NCB) of INTERPOL, for not doing enough to meet the requirements to keep Ken Ofori-Atta’s name on the INTERPOL wanted persons list. When the OSP issued a statement on the INTERPOL Commission’s decision early this year on why the Red Notice on Ken Ofori-Atta was deleted by INTERPOL, it quoted the “polarized political statements from members of the current and former administrations about the conduct of the investigation” from the ruling. That point is contained in paragraph 36 of the ruling: “The Commission notes that this case, relating to a former Minister of Finance from the inner circle of the former president, additionally generated important media coverage in Ghana and prompted polarized political statements from members of the current and former administrations about the conduct of the investigation by the OSP, including some directly disputing the reality of the Applicant’s medical situation or attempting to litigate the case.” The Commission's 40-paragraph decision, however, points to a much bigger failure on the part of the OSP (through the NCB) to convince INTERPOL to keep Ken Ofori-Atta’s name on the wanted list. The Commission said the NCB had not updated the Red Notice “to reflect the updated charges, nor to provide reference to the new arrest warrant, raising issues in relation to the quality and accuracy of the data under Article 12 of the RPD.” “In the present case, the minimal factual information transmitted by the NCB of Ghana does not properly illustrate how the actions described could not constitute standard use of ministerial powers by the office holder, or how they represented more than simple non-compliance with administrative procedures without fraudulent intent,” the Commission stated. The INTERPOL Commission said the circumstances of the case highlighted a “rather premature stage at which a Red Notice was requested by the authorities of Ghana in June 2025, even before the Applicant was formally charged with any crime…” The INTERPOL Commission noted that the OSP’s completion of the investigation and subsequent charging of Ken Ofori-Atta in court could have made the resolved the “premature” trigger of the Red Notice, but the records were still not updated. “While this situation has now been de facto remedied with the passage of time and the occurrence of new procedural developments, the Commission notes nevertheless, that the necessary updates have still not been undertaken by the NCB of Ghana to reflect the current state of the proceedings in the Red Notice,” the ruling said. The Commission reached its decision after examining Ken Ofori-Atta’s request to delete information about him from INTERPOL’s files. In reviewing the case, the Commission considered submissions from Ken Ofori-Atta, the OSP, through Ghana’s NCB, and the United States NCB, as well as information from INTERPOL’s General Secretariat. The Red Notice against Ofori-Atta was issued on June 5, 2025, at the request of Ghana’s NCB. The notice was based on an arrest warrant obtained by the OSP from the Circuit Court in Accra on February 12, 2025. It listed “Using Public Office for Profit” as the offence for which the former minister was wanted. The allegations in the original notice related to transactions undertaken between 2017 and 2024, when Ofori-Atta served as Ghana’s Finance Minister. They covered contracts involving Strategic Mobilisation Ghana Limited (SML), procurement and payments relating to the National Cathedral project, payments connected to the termination of the Electricity Company of Ghana’s contract with Beijing Xiao Cheng Technology, payments from the Ghana Revenue Authority’s Tax Refund Account, and the procurement of 307 Mercedes-Benz ambulances by the Ministry of Health. The OSP had not finished its investigation into any of the cases at the time the INTERPOL Red Notice in respect of Ken Ofori-Atta was requested. On November 18, 2025, the OSP filed 78 criminal charges against Ofori-Atta and seven others before the Criminal Division of the High Court in Accra for their roles in the SML scandal, which investigative journalists unearthed in 2023. Though the OSP was petitioned on the matter in 2023, there is documented evidence that it only commenced an investigation into the SML scandal in January 2025, after Ken Ofori-Atta had travelled out of Ghana allegedly to seek treatment. The charges in the SML case included conspiracy to influence procurement processes to obtain an unfair advantage in the award of procurement contracts, conspiracy to cause financial loss to the Republic, using public office for profit, conspiracy to commit wilful oppression, and entering into government financial commitments extending beyond one financial year without prior parliamentary approval. The INTERPOL Commission drew attention to the 78 charges filed in November and the fresh warrant issued in December, before concluding that the NCB had not updated the notice. That aspect of the matter was considered under Article 12 of INTERPOL’s Rules on the Processing of Data, which sets requirements for the quality and accuracy of information recorded in the organisation’s files. The Commission said the information provided by the OSP through Ghana’s NCB “has remained limited to the summary of facts and a few sentences” describing the allegations. It further said “the information did not properly illustrate how the actions attributed to Ofori-Atta went beyond the standard exercise of ministerial powers or amounted to more than simple non-compliance with administrative procedures without fraudulent intent.” The Commission also found that the information “fails to highlight any specific personal benefit for the Applicant himself,” adding that it focused instead on alleged financial damage to the national budget arising from what it described as the “suboptimal selection of contractors.” The decision also considered the circumstances surrounding the issuance of the Red Notice, including the fact that it was issued in June 2025, more than five months before the OSP filed the 78 charges. The Commission noted that, under INTERPOL’s rules, Red Notices are intended for people who have been charged and are wanted for prosecution or to serve a sentence, rather than individuals who are still only investigative suspects. The commission said it observed that the suspension of the Red Notice in November 2025 “did not prevent Ghana from pursuing other channels to secure Ofori-Atta’s return.” The decision records that “Ghana engaged in bilateral communications with United States authorities, transmitted an extradition request through diplomatic channels in December 2025 and pursued the issuance of a fresh arrest warrant.” The Commission added that the “failure to update the notice left INTERPOL with outdated information” on the case.

Title: Ghana’s public debt has jumped from $49bn to $65bn, says Amin Adam
Content: Former Finance Minister Dr Mohammed Amin Adam says Ghana’s public debt has risen from $49 billion at the end of 2024 to $65 billion in October 2026. He accused Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson of heavy borrowing, but the minister denied it. Speaking to Evans Mensah in an interview on Monday, Dr Amin Adam challenged the minister’s account of government borrowing. He argued that exchange rate movements alone could not explain the increase in debt. “Our debt stock has moved from $49 billion at the end of 2024, when we were leaving government. As of October this year, 2026, the dollar value of our debt is now $65 billion.” He put the increase at almost $16 billion and said the Minority had a responsibility to scrutinise the figures. Dr Amin Adam said the debt-to-GDP ratio rose from 44% at the end of 2025 to 47.5% in October 2026. According to him, the debt stock rose 18% over those 10 months. “If the minister is not borrowing, how can your debt stock increase by 18%?” He acknowledged that debt restructuring and the cedi’s appreciation helped reduce the debt stock in 2025. However, he disputed any suggestion that currency depreciation accounted for the subsequent increase. Dr Amin Adam said the minister had added GH¢118 billion to the debt stock between the end of 2025 and October 2026. He attributed about GH¢30 billion of that increase to the cedi’s depreciation. “A quarter of that, about Gh¢30 billion, is what you can attribute to the depreciation of the cedi. The rest, what do you attribute it to? He borrowed.” He also questioned the scale of projected interest payments, citing a GH¢61 billion provision in the 2027 budget. “This minister is borrowing heavily, and this is why interest payment for 2027 is projected to be GH¢61 billion.” Dr Amin Adam said that amount exceeded the combined allocations for the new economy and Big Push programmes. He further compared the interest bill with allocations to the agriculture, energy, tourism, and trade and industry ministries. Those allocations totalled GH¢34 billion, he said. He argued that the comparison showed the burden of interest payments on public finances, with less money allocated to those sectors, which he described as job-creating areas.

Title: Konongo traffic gridlock: Motorists lose hours as authorities promise relief in 3 weeks
Content: Motorists and commuters travelling along the Konongo-Kumasi-Accra highway are spending more than two hours navigating severe traffic congestion, with authorities promising relief within three weeks. The persistent gridlock has reduced movement to a crawl, leaving vehicles bumper-to-bumper as frustrated commuters struggle to get through the busy stretch. The congestion has disrupted journeys along the major highway, affecting commercial drivers, private motorists and passengers who rely on the route for travel between Kumasi and Accra. Authorities have attributed the situation to roadside trading activities by market women who have refused to relocate to a newly constructed market, as well as a pothole along a critical section of the road. The continued presence of traders along the roadside has reportedly restricted available space for vehicles, while the damaged section has further slowed traffic movement. The situation is compounded by the volume of vehicles using Konongo as a major transit point, including commercial vehicles travelling from neighbouring countries such as Togo and Burkina Faso. Beyond the delays, motorists have raised concerns about road safety, citing narrow sections of the highway, poorly managed intersections, numerous potholes and the absence of adequate road signs. One motorist described the area as dangerous, warning that the combination of heavy traffic and inadequate road infrastructure was exposing road users to accidents. "The intersections at the station create congestion. It's dangerous to be around this road. Konongo Road is always busy," the motorist said. The motorist also pointed to the frequent movement of drivers from Togo and Burkina Faso, saying their use of the route added to the congestion. "Togo and Burkina drivers all ply this area, creating the congestion and the road is too narrow. We are witnessing too many accidents, so many potholes and there are no road signs. Every day Konongo is busy," the motorist added. The concerns reflect the growing frustration among road users, many of whom face lengthy delays on a highway that serves as an important link for passenger and commercial transportation. Authorities have, however, assured motorists that measures are expected to ease the congestion within three weeks. The promised intervention is expected to address the immediate challenges contributing to the gridlock, particularly roadside trading activities and the damaged section of the road. For commuters and commercial drivers who depend on the Konongo-Kumasi-Accra highway, the hope is that the intervention will restore smoother traffic movement, reduce travel delays and improve safety along the route.

Title: Timothy Bentum announces five-year anti-drug tour targeting 252 SHSs across Ghana
Content: Media personality and Lead Pastor of Grace Avenue Ministry, Timothy Bentum, has announced a five-year anti-drug abuse campaign targeting 252 senior high schools across Ghana's 16 regions to educate students on substance abuse, peer pressure and the dangers of addiction. The initiative, which will involve sustained engagements with students and teachers, is aimed at preventing young people from experimenting with drugs and helping those already facing challenges to access counselling and support. Mr Bentum said the campaign would focus particularly on peer influence, noting that many people who develop drug-related problems are first introduced to substances by friends. He said schools provided an important platform for addressing the problem because they brought young people and their friends together, making them suitable environments for conversations about responsible friendships and the consequences of peer pressure. He urged students to be careful about the company they keep, warning that the desire to improve academic performance or gain confidence must not drive them towards substance abuse. "There is no drug that can make you study better or give you confidence without the clap back of getting addicted and then totally throwing away your whole destiny," he cautioned. Mr Bentum stressed that the campaign would not be a one-off awareness exercise but a sustained intervention spanning five years and covering all 16 regions. As part of the programme, organisers intend to identify three to four teachers in each participating school and equip them with basic counselling skills to support students experiencing personal difficulties. The selected teachers will serve as the first point of contact for students who need guidance, emotional support or someone to talk to, helping to create a more accessible support system within schools. He also appealed to parents to become more actively involved in their children's lives, stressing that their responsibilities must go beyond providing financial support. "I want every parent out there to be more present in their children's lives beyond just trying to support with money. I really want the biggest support you can give as a nation and as individuals is to be part of your children's lives," he said. He called for collective support from parents, individuals and society to protect young people from substance abuse and its long-term consequences. The anti-drug high school tour will be officially launched on Saturday, November 21, at 3:00 p.m. at Christ the King Church in Accra. The launch event will be strictly by invitation.

Title: Timothy Bentum urges parents to be actively involved in children’s lives to prevent drug abuse
Content: Media personality and Lead Pastor of Grace Avenue Ministry, Timothy Bentum, has urged parents to become more actively involved in their children's lives beyond providing financial support, warning that peer pressure and drug abuse continue to threaten the future of young people. He said many young people were introduced to drugs through friends, making schools and peer groups important spaces for sustained education and intervention. Speaking ahead of the launch of a five-year senior high school drug prevention initiative, Mr Bentum stressed the importance of helping students make informed decisions about friendships and resist pressure to experiment with substances. He cautioned that no drug could genuinely improve academic performance or give users lasting confidence without the risk of addiction and its damaging consequences. "There is no drug that can make you study better or give you confidence without the clap back of getting addicted and then totally throwing away your whole destiny," he said. Mr Bentum disclosed that the initiative would involve a sustained tour of senior high schools across Ghana's 16 regions, targeting 252 schools over five years. He explained that the programme would go beyond one-off awareness campaigns by establishing support structures within participating schools to help students struggling with personal challenges, peer pressure and substance abuse. As part of the intervention, organisers would identify three to four teachers in each school and take them through a short counselling programme to equip them to serve as the first point of contact for students who need guidance or someone to talk to. He said the approach was intended to ensure that students could access support within their schools rather than struggle with their challenges without assistance. The pastor also appealed to parents to pay closer attention to their children's emotional and social well-being, arguing that parenting must extend beyond meeting their financial needs. He said parents needed to be present, build stronger relationships with their children and create an environment in which young people felt comfortable discussing their difficulties. Mr Bentum emphasised that preventing drug abuse required collective responsibility, urging individuals and the wider society to support efforts aimed at protecting young people. The initiative is scheduled to be officially launched on Saturday, November 21, at 3:00 p.m. at Christ the King Church. The launch will be strictly by invitation.

Title: “Invest in Ghana, produce here and grow” – Ato Forson Urges Investors
Content: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has called on local and international investors to commit resources to businesses in Ghana, stressing the need to translate investment opportunities into actual projects that will expand production and create jobs. He has also challenged banks and development finance institutions to move beyond investment discussions and work directly with businesses and investors to secure funding for viable projects. Dr Forson made the appeal at the maiden Invest Ghana Summit, organised by the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), where he urged participants to use the gathering to establish concrete business partnerships and financing arrangements. He said the summit should produce tangible outcomes, with investors identifying projects they could pursue and making arrangements for further engagements before leaving Accra. The Finance Minister encouraged Ghanaian businesses to present their expansion proposals, assuring them of the government's willingness to support credible ventures seeking financing. "To the Ghanaian businesses, bring the expansion plan you have been waiting for to finance and government will work with you," he said. He also urged foreign investors to partner local enterprises rather than approach the Ghanaian market independently. According to him, Ghanaian businesses possess valuable knowledge of the local operating environment and can provide the necessary support for international investors seeking to establish and expand operations in the country. "To the international investor, meet the Ghanaian companies that know this market and that can help you build an industry," he stated. Dr Forson directed a particular appeal to banks and development finance institutions, urging them to engage businesses and international investors to determine the financial requirements of viable investment proposals. He said financial institutions must play a more active role in turning business opportunities into funded projects instead of allowing investment plans to remain at the discussion stage. "To our banks and development finance departments, use this summit to sit down with both and work through what it will take to finance viable projects," he urged. The Finance Minister's call places access to funding and private-sector investment at the centre of efforts to stimulate economic activity, expand industrial capacity and strengthen domestic production. He further challenged participants to make the summit a starting point for sustained business engagements rather than treating it as a one-off networking event. "I would like you to leave Ghana here in Accra a project you can examine and a meeting in your diary," he said. Dr Forson concluded by urged investors to establish businesses, produce goods and expand their operations within Ghana, emphasising the importance of building productive enterprises in the country. The maiden Invest Ghana Summit brings together local businesses, international investors and financial institutions to explore investment opportunities and develop partnerships to support Ghana's economic growth.

Title: 2027 interest bill exceeds allocations to four job-creating ministries, says Amin Adam
Content: Former Finance Minister Dr Mohammed Amin Adam says Ghana’s projected GH¢61 billion interest bill for 2027 exceeds the combined allocations to four ministries he identified as key to job creation. Speaking to Evans Mensah in an interview on Monday, he put the total allocation to the Agriculture, Energy, Tourism, and Trade and Industry ministries at GH¢34 billion. He challenged Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson over government borrowing. He argued that the rising debt stock and projected interest bill contradicted claims that the minister was not borrowing. “This minister is borrowing heavily, and this is why interest payments for 2027 are projected to be GH¢61 billion. That's what he's put in the budget for 2027.” Dr Amin Adam said the interest bill also exceeded the combined allocations for the new economy and Big Push initiatives. “GH¢61 billion is more than the combined allocation of the new economy allocation and big push allocation.” He used the comparison to question the scale of borrowing and its implications for spending on job-creating sectors. According to him, Ghana’s debt-to-GDP ratio rose from 44% at the end of 2025 to 47.5% by October 2026. He said the debt stock rose 18% in those 10 months. “If the minister is not borrowing, how can your debt stock increase by 18%?” Dr Amin Adam said GH¢118 billion had been added to the debt stock over that period. He attributed about GH¢30 billion of the increase to cedi depreciation and argued that borrowing accounted for the rest. He acknowledged that debt restructuring and cedi appreciation had helped reduce the debt stock in 2025. However, he rejected exchange rate movements as a sufficient explanation for the subsequent increase. “The rest, what do you attribute them to? He borrowed,” he stated. He also said the dollar value of Ghana’s debt had risen from $49 billion at the end of 2024 to $65 billion by October 2026. Dr Amin Adam maintained that the minority had a responsibility to scrutinise those figures and challenge the government’s account of its borrowing.

Title: Amin Adam accuses Finance Minister of heavy borrowing as debt rises GH¢118bn
Content: Former Finance Minister in the Akufo-Addo administration, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam, has accused Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson of heavy borrowing. He says Ghana’s debt stock rose by GH¢118 billion between the end of 2025 and October 2026. Speaking in an interview with Evans Mensah on Monday, Dr Amin Adam challenged suggestions that the minister was not borrowing. He argued that cedi depreciation accounted for only a quarter of the increase. “Within 10 months, our debt stock increased by 18%. If the minister is not borrowing, how can your debt stock increase by 18%?” According to Dr Amin Adam, Ghana’s debt-to-GDP ratio fell to 44% at the end of 2025 before rising to 47.5% by October 2026. He attributed the earlier decline in the debt stock largely to debt restructuring and the cedi's appreciation. But he rejected exchange rate movements as the main explanation for the subsequent increase. He said the cedi had depreciated by about 10.1% in 2026. He argued this accounted for roughly GH¢30 billion of the GH¢118 billion added to the debt stock. “A quarter of that, about Gh¢30 billion, is what you can attribute to the depreciation of the cedi. The rest, what do you attribute it to? He borrowed.” Dr Amin Adam also cited an increase in the dollar value of Ghana’s debt. He said it had risen from $49 billion at the end of 2024, when his government left office, to $65 billion by October 2026. He maintained that the figures contradicted the minister’s position on borrowing. He said the minority had a responsibility to scrutinise the data. Turning to the cost of servicing the debt, Dr Amin Adam linked what he described as heavy borrowing to projected interest payments of GH¢61 billion in 2027. “This minister is borrowing heavily, and this is why interest payments for 2027 are projected to be GH¢61 billion.” He said that amount exceeded the combined allocations for the new economy and Big Push initiatives. Dr Amin Adam further argued that the combined allocations to the agriculture, energy, tourism, and trade and industry ministries amounted to GH¢34 billion. He described these as job-creating sectors and contrasted their funding with the projected interest bill.

Title: You cannot claim restructuring gains and fault repayments – Amin Adam challenges Forson
Content: Former Finance Minister Dr Mohammed Amin Adam has challenged Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson over his criticism of Ghana’s debt repayment schedule. He accused him of taking credit for the gains from debt restructuring while questioning the obligations that came with it. Speaking in an interview with Evans Mensah on Monday, Dr Amin Adam rejected the claim that the previous government deliberately deferred payments to 2027 and 2028 to set up the current administration for another default. “What struck me, as far as that [DDEP] is concerned, was the minister standing in Parliament and saying that we deliberately deferred the payment to 2027-2028 in order for them to default; that was very, very unfortunate for me to hear from the minister.” He argued that the restructuring had delivered debt relief and created fiscal space for the current government. He questioned why the Finance Minister would celebrate those benefits while suggesting the repayment terms were politically calculated. “And so you are happy to take credit for the benefits, and when it is time for repayment, you are complaining.” Dr Amin Adam said 98% of the restructuring had been completed before the election. He maintained that his government could not have known the NDC would be in office when the deferred payments became due. “And so, how on earth could we know that the NDC was going to be in government at the time the repayment will be done in 2027 and 2028?” He said the NPP had campaigned to remain in government and had already begun servicing some debts before leaving office. Defending the restructuring, Dr Amin Adam said it secured $11 billion in debt relief. He put outright cancellations by external creditors at $5 billion, with another $6 billion in debt service savings. He attributed the reduction in Ghana’s debt-to-GDP ratio and the government’s increased fiscal room to that exercise. “This minister is taking credit for the benefits from the restructuring.”

Title: Nigeria says US intelligence support helping target militants, secure 2027 election
Content: Nigeria's military is receiving real-time US intelligence and satellite support to target militant leaders and degrade insurgent networks ahead of the January elections, its defence minister said on Monday. Defence Minister General Christopher Musa said Nigerian troops killed several terrorist and bandit leaders in overnight operations in the northwest and northeast and were conducting near-daily missions aided by improved intelligence. "We took out a lot of the bandit leaders ​and the terrorists themselves," Musa told reporters during a briefing, adding that US satellite imagery, intelligence sharing and ​training had improved the military's ability to track and strike targets. Musa said Abuja and Washington ⁠have continued to expand security cooperation as Nigeria battles Islamist insurgencies in the northeast, armed banditry in the northwest ​and kidnapping gangs across the country. Nigeria is also expecting additional helicopters from the US and Italy, adding to recently commissioned ​air assets, he said. In May, Nigerian and US forces killed Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, whom US PresidentDonald Trumpdescribed as the global second-in-command of ISIS,during operationsin northeastern Nigeria. The operation followed aUS strikeon Christmas Day ordered by Trump against militants he said were targeting Christians ​in Nigeria. Musa said security agencies are intensifying preparations ahead of elections in January in which President Bola Tinubu is ​vying for a second four-year term, using intelligence-led operations to prevent violence before, during and after the vote. Authorities are monitoring militant groups' ‌use ⁠of Starlink, cryptocurrencies and commercial drones, and they are working with US authorities to disrupt financing networks, Musa said. The US embassy in Abuja did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Attacks on military positions by Islamist groups Boko Haram and its splinter Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) have surged inrecent weeksdespite years of military operations aimed at ​containing the 17-year insurgency in ​northeastern Nigeria. Musa said Nigeria has ⁠agreed a 5-kilometre (3-mile) cross-border "right of pursuit" arrangement with neighbouring Cameroon, Niger and Chad, allowing troops to pursue militants and bandits across border areas. He also warned that Islamic State Sahel ​is seeking to recruit criminal gangs in northwestern Nigeria, raising fears that largely profit-driven ​bandit groups could ⁠evolve into ideologically driven insurgents similar to ISWAP in the northeast. Musa said militants and bandits were exploiting dense forests and porous borders with Niger and Benin to evade security forces after carrying out attacks. But he said advances in surveillance had ⁠improved the ​military's ability to track through difficult terrain, restricting militants' freedom of movement. Nigeria ​is working with neighbouring countries to block cross-border movement, logistics and recruitment networks linking militants across the Sahel. "We don't want them to develop that ​capacity," Musa said. "We're blocking the logistics and taking them out from within Nigeria."

Title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
Content: Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals. Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements. The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin. Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said. The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations - unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by theincoming Labour government in 2024. Downing Street has not ruled out the UK joining the scheme, saying they will watch it "with interest". Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said the plan to open a centre in Rwanda had no "future or humanity", according to AFP news agency. "I don't see any future or humanity in that. It's not the solution," Sanchez told the Spanish broadcaster Telecinco, AFP reported. The five countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights. The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc. In a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean. In a written statement, the Dutch government said the five countries will "only return single men" as part of the first phase of the deal, adding that the focus for the Netherlands "will be on persons from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda". Once in Rwanda, people will be able to integrate into society, which means they will have the right of residence, as well as access to education, healthcare, the labour market and the legal system. Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta said the country is commmited to working with European partners to provide a "safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants". He added that they would also work on "correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities", which he called a "key driver of irregular migration".
