He added that they would also work on "correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities", which he called a "key driver of irregular migration". The United Nations' International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role. "IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms". With elections approaching in several EU nations, administrations have been under pressure to show they can control migration. Concerns around security, struggling economies and disillusionment with governing parties have all had amajor role in shaping attitudes towards people leaving their home countries. Human Rights Watch's senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said the choice of Rwanda would bea cause of concern as it had a "well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention" and support for armed rebels in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo. "Paying Kigali to host a deportation programme would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad." The independent EU Agency for Fundamental Rights argued any third country hosting a return hub should "respect fundamental rights", including that people should not be sent to a country where they face serious risk of persecution. The agency added that unaccompanied children should not be sent to a return hub, which the Dutch government has confirmed will not take place. According to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, there were almost 110,000 irregular border crossings into the EU in the first 10 months of 2026, which represents a 29% decrease compared to the previous year. In October, about 18,100 crossings were detected, which is about 6% less than October 2025 but 22% more than in September "largely because of a sharp rise in arrivals on the Western African route to the Canary Islands".

Title: Methane cuts offer cheap, fast route to tackling global warming – UN climate chief
Content: UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell has urged governments to accelerate efforts to cut methane and other super-polluting greenhouse gases, describing the measures as among the fastest, cheapest and most effective ways to slow global warming in the near term. Addressing the Leaders-Level Non-CO₂ Greenhouse Gases Summit at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, on November 12, 2026, Mr Stiell said reducing methane emissions could deliver immediate climate benefits while improving public health, boosting agricultural production and generating significant economic returns. He said climate-related disasters were already destroying lives, disrupting livelihoods and contributing to inflation, warning that the consequences would worsen as global temperatures continue to rise. “In a world of suffocating disasters, action on methane offers breathing space,” he said. Mr Stiell said reducing methane and other super pollutants was essential to limiting near-term temperature increases and ensuring that any overshoot of the 1.5°C global warming threshold remained as short and limited as possible. He, however, stressed that methane reductions must be accompanied by rapid cuts in carbon dioxide emissions to prevent further increases in global temperatures.Existing technologies can deliver significant methane cutsMr Stiell identified the oil and gas, solid waste and agricultural sectors as major sources of methane emissions, noting that existing technologies could significantly reduce their contribution to global warming. He said approximately 70 per cent of methane emissions from the oil and gas sector could be eliminated using existing technologies, with much of the reduction achievable at low or no net cost. In the solid waste sector, he said, 75 per cent of methane reduction measures could generate financial savings, with the economic value of captured methane potentially exceeding the investment required to implement the solutions. He argued that accelerating the deployment of these technologies would deliver benefits beyond climate mitigation, including improved energy efficiency, cleaner air, better agricultural yields, lower costs and fewer deaths. Citing findings by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the Climate and Clean Air Coalition, Mr Stiell said every dollar invested in key super-pollutant solutions could generate $15 in economic gains alone. “The business case is absolutely clear,” he said. He also highlighted the economic losses associated with gas flaring, revealing that approximately 167 billion cubic metres of gas were flared annually during oil and gas production, representing an estimated $54 billion in lost energy value. “And that’s money going up in smoke,” he said.Countries urged to translate climate commitments into actionMr Stiell said international recognition of the importance of methane reduction was growing, with more than 90 per cent of parties, representing approximately three-quarters of global methane emissions, having included measures to cut methane in their new Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). He said the priority must now shift from making commitments to implementing them. “The task now is to turn those plans into action,” he said. He identified COP31 as an opportunity to advance practical solutions and strengthen international momentum, including through methane and waste targets being pursued by the COP31 Presidency. He also highlighted the Super Pollutant Country Action Accelerator as an initiative designed to provide countries with the support needed to advance their emissions-reduction efforts.Stiell outlines four priorities for governmentsThe UN Climate Change Executive Secretary called on governments and other stakeholders to take four key steps to accelerate reductions in methane and other super pollutants. First, he urged countries to prioritise methane and other super pollutants in their national climate plans by establishing clear targets, introducing supportive policies for key sectors and encouraging industries to invest in available technologies and solutions. Second, he called for increased public and private financing, particularly through development banks and climate funds. He expressed concern about the limited financing currently directed towards super-pollutant reductions, revealing that only 0.5 per cent of climate finance earmarked for emissions reductions went to super pollutants in 2023. Third, he urged governments to invest in institutions, technical expertise and project pipelines to strengthen their capacity to develop and implement emissions-reduction projects. Fourth, he encouraged countries to take advantage of the new UN carbon market mechanism established under Article 6.4 of the Paris Agreement, known as the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism. He said the mechanism was already operational and had identified landfill methane as one of its initial areas of focus, rewarding projects that capture methane from landfills and put it to productive use.Methane cuts could buy vulnerable countries more timeHighlighting the particular importance of methane reduction for vulnerable nations, Mr Stiell said such interventions could provide additional time to address the escalating impacts of climate change. “For small island states like mine, methane reduction buys us time,” he said. He nevertheless reiterated that methane reductions must be accompanied by rapid action on carbon dioxide emissions to limit further temperature increases. Mr Stiell described tackling super pollutants as a major opportunity for governments to advance climate protection, economic development and public health simultaneously. “Super pollutants are a supersize opportunity. And it’s low-hanging. For the climate, for economies, and for human health,” he said.

Title: US basketball player arrested with 34kg of cannabis at Nigerian airport
Content: A basketball player from the US has been arrested in Nigeria with 33.95kg (75lbs) of cannabis in his luggage at the main airport in Lagos. The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) identified the player as Greene Da'monte Khiree, 28, from the US state of Georgia, who it said had arrived from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates. According to the agency, the suspect said he had been playing professional basketball in Thailand and was visiting Nigeria to "build networks" for his career. He has not publicly commented on the allegations. The agency said an examination of the suspect's phone had pointed "to his knowledge of and involvement in the drug trafficking activity". In a statement on Sunday, the agency said he was arrested on Wednesday after airport officials noticed him abandoning his two checked-in bags and attempting to leave with his carry-on bag. The two bags, which bore his name, contained 32 packs of the drug known as "Loud", a potent strain of cannabis, the agency said. A tracking device was also recovered from the bags, the agency added. The International Basketball Federation (FIBA) lists a player by the name Damonte Greene, with the most recent appearance at the Phuket Elite Cup in Thailand, on 26 September. Nigeria, once regarded primarily as a transit hub for drug trafficking, has increasingly become a producer, consumer, and distributor of illegal drugs, according to the UN. Recent NDLEA operations have uncovered several industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratories, raising concerns about links between Nigerian drug producers and Mexican cartels seeking to manufacture and export the drug. In September, the agency said it had dismantled a meth lab and arrested a Mexican suspected drug kingpin who was allegedly attempting to flee Nigeria through Lagos. Methamphetamine, commonly known as meth, is a highly addictive synthetic drug that can cause severe psychosis, heart attacks, or stroke. In August, a social media influencer suspected of links to an international drug trafficking network was arrested after the authorities seized cocaine worth nearly $28m (£21m), which was destined for the UK.

Title: Two suspects remanded over murder of 39-year-old woman in Oti Region
Content: Two men have been remanded into prison custody by the Dambai Magistrate Court for their alleged involvement in the murder of a 39-year-old woman, Madam Rejoice Sena Akpaku, whose body was discovered in a bush near Adumadum in the Krachi East Municipality of the Oti Region. The suspects, identified as Isaac Sekyi, 36, and Reindolf Sekeni, 45, were arraigned on November 12 in a court presided over by Mr Alhassan Dramani and remanded to reappear on December 2, 2026. According to a police statement issued by Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP), Mr John Nchor, Oti Regional Public Affairs Officer, the deceased reportedly travelled from Somanya in the Eastern Region to Dormaa in the Oti Region on October 28, 2026, to retrieve GH¢19,000 allegedly owed to her by Sekyi. She, however, failed to return, prompting concerns about her whereabouts and subsequent police investigations into her disappearance. The statement said that following Sekyi’s arrest on November 10, 2026, police investigations led to the recovery of the deceased’s Infinix Smart 8 mobile phone from a chain of individuals linked to him. Investigators reportedly traced the phone to his girlfriend, Madam Seraphine Aku Koumah, who told the police that Sekyi had given it to her before she handed it over to his brother, Frank Sekyi. The mobile phone was subsequently retrieved and found to have been flashed, with its SIM card removed. A mobile phone technician, identified as Mr Mohammed Ali, was also arrested to assist with investigations. The police statement further disclosed that on November 11, 2026, Mr Sekyi allegedly confessed to the murder and implicated Mr Sekeni as an accomplice. He subsequently led police investigators to the location where the body had been concealed, where it was identified by a sibling of the deceased. A stick suspected to have been used in the attack was also retrieved from the scene and retained as an exhibit to support ongoing investigations. The police said they subsequently arraigned and remanded the two principal suspects into custody, while granting three other persons arrested in connection with the case police enquiry bail to assist with investigations. The Ghana Police Service assured the public it would investigate the matter professionally and in accordance with due process.

Title: Police detail dramatic arrest of key suspect in the Sakumono double killing in Kumasi
Content: The Ghana Police Service has been giving detailed accounts of the operation that led to the arrest of a prime suspect in the gruesome murder of a 57-year-old man and his niece at Sakumono in Tema this year. The 57-year-old George Atubiga and his 47-year-old niece, Irene Atubiga, were murdered at their residence in Tema. Police say the arrest of prime suspect Samuel Christopher Osei at his hideout in Ejisu, close to Kumasi, followed days of intensive manhunt and a public reward announcement for information regarding the whereabouts of the 72-year-old man. But police surprised the suspect at his hideout in Tikrom near Ejisu, cutting short his preparations and attempts to flee the country to the United States. “I'm told from the arresting officer; I'm told he was preparing to leave the country. I think he is based in the US also. He was preparing to leave the country," Supt. Godwin Ahianyo, who speaks for the Ashanti Regional Police Command, explained. Acting on what police say was a vital tip-off received on a Sunday, four days after the Thursday incident, personnel from Suntreso District Command and the Anti-Armed Robbery Team tracked the suspect to his personal residence at Tikrom in the Ejisu Municipality. Superintendent Ahianyo revealed that the suspect, in the company of two other individuals, whom he claimed were brothers, did not resist arrest. According to him, the suspect readily gave himself up to the arresting officers, admitting he knew exactly why law enforcement agents had arrived. Police say Mr. Osei was temporarily held in Kumasi before being transferred under strict security to the Accra Regional Police Command. Superintendent Ahianyo says the swift and coordinated operation has won the applause and widespread commendation from the Inspector-General of Police and other stakeholders. “According to the arresting officers, he told them he knew why they were there to arrest him, so he gave himself up, and then he was brought here (Regional Headquarters) and then later was sent to Accra for investigation to continue from there, because that is where the incident happened, so we handed him over to the Accra Regional Police Command. For our arresting officers, no, he was not interrogated immediately. After the police apprehended him, they called Accra, and the instruction was that he was supposed to be sent to Accra. So, then they went with him in the morning and then handed him over to the Accra Police Command,” he said. He continued: “I think it happened on Thursday. Then on Sunday, we had intel that he was hiding somewhere at Tikrom in Ejisu. So, police proceeded there. When they got there, he was there with two other gentlemen whom he claimed to be his brothers. But they didn't have any hand in whatever had happened. That is where he stays. That is his personal residence" The police added, "Whenever he comes to Kumasi, that is where he lives, and he lives there alone. So, when the police went in there, they met him, and he really gave himself up.”

Title: Two remanded over murder of woman who travelled to recover GH¢19,000 debt
Content: Two persons have been remanded into prison custody by the Dambai Magistrate Court for their alleged involvement in the murder of a 39-year-old woman, Rejoice Sena Akpaku, whose body was discovered in a bush near Adumadum in the Oti Region. The suspects, identified as 36-year-old Isaac Sekyi and 45-year-old Reindolf Sekeni, alias Okeley, were arraigned on Thursday, November 12, 2026, and are expected to reappear in court on December 2, 2026. According to the Ghana Police Service, the deceased travelled from Somanya in the Eastern Region to Dormabin on October 28, 2026, to recover GH¢19,000 allegedly owed to her by Sekyi. However, she failed to return after the trip, prompting investigations into her disappearance. Police said Sekyi was arrested on November 10, 2026, following which investigations traced the deceased’s Infinix Smart 8 mobile phone to his girlfriend, Seraphine Aku Koumah. Koumah reportedly told investigators that Sekyi had given her the phone before she handed it over to his brother, Frank Sekyi. The device was subsequently retrieved and found to have been flashed, with its SIM card removed. A mobile phone technician, Mohammed Ali, was also arrested in connection with the incident. The Police said that on November 11, Sekyi confessed to the murder and implicated Sekeni as an accomplice. He subsequently led investigators to the location where the body had been abandoned. The deceased was identified by one of her siblings. A stick allegedly used in the attack was also recovered by the Police as an exhibit. While Sekyi and Sekeni have been remanded into prison custody, the other three persons arrested in connection with the investigation have been granted Police enquiry bail to assist with further investigations. The Ghana Police Service has assured the public that investigations will be conducted professionally and in accordance with due process.

Title: Adu-Boahene’s lawyer hints at appeal, says court ruling has ‘gaping hole’
Content: Lawyer for former National Signals Bureau (NSB) Director-General, Kwabena Adu-Boahene, Samuel Atta Akyea, says the defence has sufficient grounds to challenge the court's decision ordering his client to open his defence in the GH¢49.1 million cyber-defence case. He says the ruling by the Accra High Court contains significant gaps which the defence intends to challenge at the appropriate time. Reacting to the court's decision, Mr Atta Akyea said: “The judge has given us enough raw materials for an appeal. There is a gaping hole in the ruling, and in due time, we will challenge it.” Watch his reaction below. The court on Thursday ordered Mr Adu-Boahene and his wife, Angela Adjei-Boateng, to open their defence on the remaining charges after dismissing their submission of no case to answer on those counts. However, the court acquitted and discharged Mr Adu-Boahene on two of the 11 charges brought against him. The court also directed the accused persons to file their witness statements by December 4, 2026, if they intend to testify in their defence. The case, involving Mr Adu-Boahene, his wife and their company, Advantage Solutions Limited, centres on allegations that GH¢49.1 million intended for the procurement of a US$7 million cyber-defence system was dishonestly diverted, with only US$1.75 million paid to the Israeli supplier, ISC Holdings. The accused persons have pleaded not guilty to the charges, which include stealing, conspiracy to steal, causing financial loss to the state, using public office for profit and money laundering. The trial has been adjourned to December 10, 2026, at 9:30 a.m., for continuation of proceedings.

Title: Amantia Chief urges prioritisation of rural development to combat poverty and social vices
Content: Newly enstooled Chief of Amantia in the Asante Akyem South District, Nana Kwadwo Bredu III, has expressed concern over the neglect of rural development by successive governments. H says the utter disregard for rural communities has left many of them without essential social amenities and economic opportunities, despite contributing to taxes for expected development. He has called on the government to prioritise development in rural communities as part of efforts to tackle poverty, unemployment and social vices among the youth. According to him, the lack of basic infrastructure and essential services in rural areas has contributed to poverty and exposed some young people to drug abuse and other social vices. Speaking at his official unveiling as the new chief of Amantia, Nana Kwadwo Bredu III bemoaned the inadequate provision of essential facilities, including quality schools, healthcare centres, accessible roads and potable drinking water in his community. He attributed these challenges to what he described as the government's failure to give rural communities the needed development attention. "Before I became the chief of this community, there were several challenges relating to social amenities. I used my personal resources to address some of these problems, but we still need government intervention to bring further development to the community," he said. Nana Kwadwo Bredu III also appealed to the youth to rally behind his leadership and contribute meaningfully towards the development of Amantia. "The youth are the future of this community and the country as a whole. I therefore urge you to support me through hard work, commitment and determination to build a better Amantia," he stated. Meanwhile, the Queen Mother of Amantia has cautioned individuals and those falsely claiming the title of Amantia chief to desist from such actions. Some residents who attended the ceremony were delighted over the installation, describing it as a positive development for the community. They pledged their full support for the new chief, citing his contributions to community development even before his enstoolment. According to them, Nana Kwadwo Bredu III had demonstrated commitment to improving the community and deserved their collective support to achieve greater development. The ceremony saw residents dressed in red and displaying red banners as a symbol of their solidarity and support for the newly installed chief.

Title: Breaking the raw material curse: How Techiman’s new cashew factory redefines Ghana’s export future
Content: In a significant boost to Ghana's industrialisation drive and agricultural value addition, President John Dramani Mahama has commissioned a state-of-the-art 100-metric-tonne-per-day cashew processing factory in Techiman, Bono East Region. The facility, funded by the Ghana Export-Import Bank (GEXIM) and operated by Nadkansco Processing Company Limited, represents a major leap forward in the country's quest to move from raw material exportation to value-added processing for both local and international markets. Creating Jobs and Transforming Lives The impact on the local community is expected to be transformative. According to Belinda Akorfa Adokpa, Managing Director of Nadkansco Processing Company Limited, the factory will create 1,500 direct jobs and approximately 3,000 indirect jobs in the Techiman area and beyond. "This facility will generate foreign exchange and strengthen the local economy in Techiman and beyond," Mrs. Adokpa stated during the commissioning ceremony. Beyond job creation, the company has demonstrated its commitment to community development by donating four new ambulances to four districts, including Atebubu, Wenchi, and Techiman North. Farmers in the region are set to be the highest beneficiaries, with the company committing to purchasing their cashew produce promptly, addressing a long-standing challenge of delayed payments that has plagued the agricultural sector. What This Means for the Local People For the residents of Techiman and surrounding communities, this factory represents more than just economic opportunity—it signals a new chapter of prosperity and self-sufficiency. Industry Stakeholder Reaction Samuel Amo Takyi, a respected stakeholder in the cashew industry, expressed enthusiasm about the development, describing the factory as a transformative investment for the region. "This new factory will go a long way to helping the local economy through agriculture," Mr. Takyi said. "It is a super impact for Techiman, the region, and the country at large. This is exactly the kind of investment we need to unlock the full potential of Ghana's cashew industry." Government's Commitment to Value Addition President Mahama, who was accompanied by the Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu Adjare, and other dignitaries, spoke passionately about the rationale behind his government's focus on agribusiness. "The creation of the Agribusiness Ministry was to help with the processing of our locally produced foods for export purposes," President Mahama explained. "We need to process more and consume our own foods. Export more means creating wealth and jobs. When you import, you are importing poverty." The President announced that his government is investing 10 billion dollars of Ghana's own money in eight sectors that will create jobs, with agriculture being one of the key sectors. GEXIM's Role in Financing Productive Enterprises Sylvester Adinam Mensah, Chief Executive Officer of GEXIM, expressed excitement about the opportunities this company brings to the cashew industry and the country at large. "At Ghana Exim, our commitment remains clear: to finance productive enterprises, promote value addition, and position Ghana as a competitive player in global trade," Mr. Mensah stated. Government Support and Policy Direction President Mahama assured Nadkansco of government support through GEXIM to enable the company to purchase sufficient cashew and preserve it for year-round operations. "I assure you that government will provide Nadkansco some funds through Ghana Exim to enable it buy enough cashew and preserve it so they run all year round," the President promised. In a major policy shift aimed at promoting local processing, the President announced that Ghana is adopting a method already used by Ivory Coast. Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu Adjare, who is also the Member of Parliament for Techiman North, highlighted the benefits this company brings to her constituents. She emphasized the essential role her ministry is playing in ensuring that raw materials are always available to keep the company operational and urged the company to maintain good relationships with local farmers who supply raw materials. President Mahama encouraged Ghanaians to venture into the manufacturing and agro-processing sectors rather than leaving it to foreigners. "We must not leave this to foreigners," he urged. "Ghanaians should venture into manufacturing and agro-processing. This is how we create jobs for our people and build a prosperous nation." The commissioning of the Nadkansco cashew processing factory marks a pivotal moment in Ghana's journey toward industrialisation and agricultural transformation. For the people of Techiman and the Bono East Region, it represents hope, opportunity, and a brighter future. As the factory begins operations, it stands as a testament to what is possible when government, financial institutions, and private enterprise collaborate to create sustainable economic growth. The transformation from raw cashew exporter to value-added processor is not just an economic strategy—it is a pathway to prosperity for all Ghanaians.

Title: Ejisu MP supports 410 tertiary students with scholarships for equitable education
Content: The Member of Parliament (MP) for Ejisu in the Ashanti Region, Kwabena Boateng, has extended financial support to over 400 tertiary students in the constituency as part of efforts to promote equitable education. The support is intended to help cover school fees and other educational expenses, enabling the beneficiaries to focus on their studies. Speaking at a mini-ceremony held at Kwamo, Mr. Boateng assured of continuous support as long as he remains the parliamentarian for the area, to produce more educated individuals. “This is the third time we are doing this, and we have more students benefiting this time. I am hoping to increase the number of beneficiaries beyond the initial figures,” he said. Some of the beneficiaries expressed their profound gratitude to the MP for prioritizing the welfare of students in his constituency. “We urge all the delegates to vote and maintain Lawyer Kwabena Boateng as the MP to lead the party at Ejisu in the 2028 elections so that more support can be brought to the students,” they said. One student noted that without the financial support, he would have missed lectures in school and his educational dreams. “This MP has positively supported us, the youth in the constituency, and we urge him to continue,” he said.

Title: Ghana wins two ITU seats in Doha: what the victories mean for the country’s digital future
Content: Ghana left the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha, Qatar, with two elected seats. It wasre-elected to the ITU Council for the 2027 to 2030 term, alongside 12 other African countries. Rev. Ing. Edmund Yirenkyi Fianko, Director-General of the National Communications Authority (NCA), was re-elected to the Radio Regulations Board (RRB). Hepolled 173 of a possible 177 votes, taking one of three African seats on the Board. The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, announced both results on Monday, 16 November 2026. According to the Minister, Fianko's tally was the highest among all RRB candidates across all five ITU regions. The two positions are often reported together, but they do very different work. Readers need the distinction to understand why both matter. The ITU is the United Nations agency for information and communication technologies. Its Councilruns the Union between its four-yearly Plenipotentiary Conferences. It oversees programmes, budget and finances, prepares strategic and financial plans, and considers broad telecommunication policy. Africa is ITU Region D and holds 13 Council seats. A seat at that table gives Ghana a direct voice in how the Union spends its money and sets its priorities for developing countries. Every mobile call, radio broadcast, and satellite link depends on radio frequencies, a shared and limited global resource. The RRB is a 12-member body thatapproves the rules for applying the international Radio Regulations and hears disputesbrought before it. Members sit as independent experts, not as national delegates. Their technical credibility is therefore the whole case for their election. Fianko was first elected to the Board in 2022 with126 votes. Four years later, his support has risen by 47 votes to near-unanimity among the 177 Member States that voted. That increase is a verdict on his first term. Member States who watched him work on the Board chose to return him with a stronger mandate. He is onlythe second Ghanaian to serve on the RRB, after the late Major (Rtd) John Ray K. Tandoh, elected in 1998. For Africa, the result places a Ghanaian engineer at the centre of decisions on spectrum and satellite orbits. Those decisions shape the continent's connectivity costs and reach for years. Ghana has held a seat on the ITU Councilwithout a break since 2002. The Doha result extends that record into a seventh consecutive term and to almost three decades of continuous representation by 2030. Successive governments, the NCA, and Ghana's diplomatic service built that continuity. It is also a record that can be lost: Council elections in Region D are contested, and no one is guaranteed a seat. This is where the Minister's leadership comes in. The Doha votes ended a campaign that started a year earlier. Sam George has been clear that this was a team result. In his announcement, he thanked the agencies that worked on the elections, Ghana's Ambassador to Qatar, H.E. Abdulwahab Ali Wadey, the Foreign Ministry teams in Accra and Geneva, and his own Ministry staff. "I trust the competence of the team I work with to deliver." Sam George, Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations That accurately describes how ITU seats are won. A Minister can lead, open doors and close the deal in the room. The votes still rest on years of technical work by the NCA and on the relationships Ghana's missions maintain between conferences. Ghana did not campaign on its history alone. Sam George delivered Ghana's policy statement to the Plenipotentiary Conference, and its argument was built for an audience of regulators and engineers. "A signal is not a connection, and a tower is not a transformation. Coverage must become usage. Usage must become impact." Sam George, Ghana's policy statement to PP-26 He asked for an ITU that measures success in results, not resolutions. He also called for equitable access to spectrum and satellite orbits for every nation, the very issues the Radio Regulations Board rules on. That alignment mattered. Ghana asked delegates to back a Board candidate while making the case, at the same podium, for fairer access to the resources the Board manages. The Minister also set out a domestic record and commitments that delegates could measure. He told the conference that Ghana is targetingmore than 70 per cent 5G population coverage by March 2027, timed for the country's 70th independence anniversary. He also pointed to work to complete 2,016 rural telephony sites and upgrade older 2G and 3G masts to 4G and 5G-ready networks. "Talent is everywhere, but opportunity is not." Sam George, addressing PP-26 in Doha He closed Ghana's statement with a line that sums up its position in global digital governance: "No nation is truly connected until every nation is connected." Part 2 of this series examines how far that agenda has progressed at home. Sam George summed up the next step in one sentence: "Now the focus moves to the task over the 2027-2030 cycle." Doha's real test is what Ghana does with the four-year mandate. Three questions will define that test. Will Ghana use its Council seat to push for affordable connectivity and financing for developing countries? Will it use Fianko's standing to protect African spectrum interests, including for satellite services? And will it bring the lessons of these forums home, into cheaper and more reliable service for Ghanaian users? Ghana has earned the seats. The next four years will show whether it can turn international standing into influence that Ghanaians can feel.

Title: Intel sued by investors after PC sales slump hits share price
Content: Intel, the US chip giant, faces a shareholder lawsuit accusing it of hiding the severity of a slump in personal computer (PC) sales that caused its share price to plunge almost 29% in one day. Billions of dollars was knocked off the value of the company after it forecast disappointing revenues ahead of its latest earnings report. Shareholders allege that Intel made "materially false and misleading" statements that failed to disclose the slowdown in PC sales and the impact of its data centre projects, according to a proposed class action lawsuit filed in San Jose, California. The BBC has contacted Intel for comment. In October, Intel firm announced its computer hardware sales had dropped sharply in the three months that ended in September. That report undermined earlier suggestions from the chipmaker that demand had been improving, sending Intel shares plunging, according to the lawsuit. Shareholders claimed the "depressed demand for PC sales" caused "a dramatic slowdown" in quarterly earnings – a drop of 9%, or about $800m - to $8.1bn. The lawsuit, filed by legal firm Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd on behalf of owners of Intel common shares between 23 July and 29 October this year, was filed against the chipmaker, its chief executive Tan Lip-Bu and other company leaders. Intel has poured huge investments into manufacturing to meet the enormous demand for AI computing power. As more semiconductors are channelled towards data centres, chips for PCs and other electronics have become more expensive. Intel boss Tan had told analysts that the industry was facing an "unprecedented memory crunch", resulting in a shortage of chip supplies for PCs. "We need to address these challenges with urgency," Tan said in October. Intel shares have fallen sharply 37.5% in the past month, though the share price is still up 51% overall this year.

Title: California sues OpenAI over Hugging Face attack
Content: California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI on Monday, alleging the ChatGPT-maker misled and endangered the public by developing artificial intelligence (AI) models without proper safeguards. In the lawsuit, Bonta cited the July 2026attack on the AI platform Hugging Faceby experimental OpenAI agents which accessed the internet to breach that company's internal systems. Bonta claimed OpenAI created a public nuisance and violated the state's unfair competition laws. OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri told the BBC in a statement that Bonta's lawsuit "appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that's been identified by every major AI lab". Other major AI developers including Anthropic, Meta, and Google have also said their models have staged similar attacks. But Bonta's lawsuit, filed in San Francisco, where the company is headquartered, appears to be the first such suit filed by a US state. Hundreds of OpenAI agents coordinated the Hugging Face attack over two days even though they were supposed to be contained in a safe testing environment. The incident drew added scrutiny because the agents went as far as attempting to cover their tracks. Bonta announced an investigation into the incident in September, and served an investigative subpoena on OpenAI as part of its probe. "The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it - this disregard for public safety violated California law," Bonta said in a statement on Monday. OpenAI said it has been transparent and responsive to the Attorney General's office. "We take misalignment seriously, and we have engaged - and will continue to engage - constructively with the Attorney General's office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry," the company said. The company added that, since the Hugging Face incident, it has worked to understand and address "misaligned model activity" which industry figures often refer to as rogue agents. Nathan Calvin, chief strategy officer at AI safety campaign group Encode AI, said the lawsuit "recognises something we at Encode have long raised alarms about". "OpenAI and other companies developing frontier AI systems have safety and security practices that are insufficient to protect the public from risks that could be catastrophic," he said.

Title: ArchXenus marks 15 years with more than 140 projects, launches GeneXus
Content: Architecture firm ArchXenus has marked 15 years in practice with more than 140 projects, using its anniversary celebration to launch GeneXus, a book documenting 12 of its selected works, and to introduce initiatives aimed at strengthening its contribution to Ghana’s built environment. The two-day celebration, held on 10 and 11 November 2026 at Christ Temple East in Accra, a building ArchXenus designed and whose construction it managed, featured the launch of the GeneXus book, the Xenus Impact Foundation and the African Urban Futures Conclave. It also brought architects and other stakeholders together to examine the future of cities, climate-responsive buildings, housing and investment in the built environment. The firm is led by Nana Akua Oppong-Birmeh and Agnes Ofosu-Appiah, both Partners and Principal Architects at ArchXenus E and Co-Directors of the Xenus Impact Foundation. Both said the firm’s most significant achievement over the past 15 years was not simply the number of projects it had completed, but the people it had helped develop, and the model of partnership it offered, particularly to women building careers while managing family responsibilities. “Just by virtue of our existence, so many people have found their feet, especially women. They have found the confidence to pursue their passion, to proceed into family life, and not worry about so many things, because we are modelling this and creating an opportunity for us to grow,” Nana Akua said. “Being partners and running the firm together has taught us that there’s strength in numbers. We are both married women with children, so we have life happening as well as work that is ongoing. When one person is down or out, the other steps in. We complement each other, which allows us to work, see where the gaps are in the built industry, and provide solutions for them,” Agnes said. The GeneXus book brings together 12 selected ArchXenus projects. Nana Akua said the publication was intended to strengthen the documentation of Ghanaian architecture and give students and practitioners local examples from which to draw inspiration, noting that many still relied on foreign publications despite the availability of projects designed and led by Ghanaians. “This is an opportunity for people to gather inspiration right here, in our cities, in Ghana, designed and led by Ghanaians, with familiar names. In places where you can actually pick a cab, go and experience them, and get inspired,” she said. Agnes said the African Urban Futures Conclave was conceived to address the fragmented nature of conversations in the built environment, where architects, engineers and other professionals often discussed issues within their own disciplines although the challenges facing cities required collaboration across sectors. The full Conclave will take place in April 2027 and is intended to be held biennially, bringing stakeholders from Ghana and across West Africa together to exchange ideas, plan, make business connections and agree on practical actions. Ahead of it, ArchXenus has agreed a challenge with the Ghana Institute of Architects inviting architects to showcase solutions to the problems facing cities. The Conclave is one strand of the newly launched Xenus Impact Foundation, which the partners established to give ideas room to grow beyond the firm’s commercial work and to serve communities through impact projects and corporate social responsibility. The Foundation works in four ways: publishing, through AX Press, which includes GeneXus; building, through impact projects; convening, through gatherings such as the Conclave; and showing, through exhibitions, including Time Space and Essence in Venice in 2027. Nana Akua called for stronger coordination in the planning of Ghanaian cities, arguing that architects are commonly commissioned to work within defined plots even when the impact of a building extends beyond its boundaries. “For an architect, you are usually given a defined plot of land to work with. You can think beyond it, but you can only work on that plot. Most cities that have developed have a vision for what they want to be, and that makes it easier for everyone to plug into that vision and let us have the kind of city that we all dream of,” she said. Agnes raised concerns about the gap in housing provision for middle-income earners, saying Ghana’s housing deficit, commonly put at about 1.8 million units, persisted despite a visible construction boom that did not translate into options for people in that bracket. “When you see a construction boom, it’s not for middle income. There’s a lot of luxury, and there are a lot of affordable housing schemes. But somewhere in the middle, there’s a gap. And the kayayei: when they arrive in Accra or whichever big city they go to, what buildings and what systems have we put in place for them?” she said. The Foundation’s pilot impact project, CoSpace, responds to that gap, exploring how middle-income earners can afford dignified homes in established neighbourhoods closer to work and school rather than living far from both. These concerns were among the issues explored on the second day of the celebration, 11 November, under the theme “Conversations & Connections”, a foretaste of the full Conclave. The discussions connected the role of architecture to wider questions about the kind of cities people want to live in, including lessons from architectural practice in Ethiopia and the need to move beyond plans towards implementation. Climate-responsive construction also featured prominently, with discussions on why green buildings matter and how they could be delivered at scale. A virtual address and moderated discussion on “Designing for Dignity” considered the human needs that should inform design, while conversations on moving from vision to delivery examined what is required to turn urban plans into practical outcomes. The gathering also considered what makes urban projects investable, bringing questions of capital, business connections and collaboration into discussions about the future of cities.

Title: Experience alone is no longer enough to run banks; use data and research – First Deputy Governor
Content: The First Deputy Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Zakari Mumuni, urged banking sector managers to base decisions on data and research, warning that experience alone is no longer enough to navigate the industry’s growing complexity. Speaking at the launch of the Ghana National Banking College Journal in Accra, he said financial institutions were managing a wider range of products and technologies alongside rising customer expectations and regulatory demands. He argued these pressures require managers to support their judgement with evidence. Dr Mumuni said the industry must encourage practitioners and researchers to question established approaches and share findings that could improve banking operations. He cited the examples of a risk officer identifying a weakness, a supervisor discovering a better approach and a researcher producing evidence that challenges an existing practice. “And that is something that should be encouraged going forward,” he said. According to him, the challenge is not a lack of information but the need for a sustained platform where practitioners and researchers can examine ideas and exchange knowledge. “There is no shortage of data, but rather a sustained platform where practitioners and researchers can test ideas, challenge assumptions and share lessons.” Dr Mumuni stressed that evidence-based decision-making should extend beyond commercial banks to the institutions regulating them. He said the Bank of Ghana was itself relying on data and research to inform its work. “For us at the Bank of Ghana, that is something that we are depending on to guide our decisions.”

Title: PwC urges Fiscal and Monetary Policy balance to sustain Ghana’s economic stability
Content: PwC Country Senior Partner, George Arhin, has urged government to maintain a careful balance between fiscal and monetary policies to sustain Ghana’s improving economic stability while supporting growth. He says increased government spending, payments under the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP) and private sector activity could inject more money into the economy, making effective liquidity management critical to keeping inflation under control. Speaking at PwC’s 2027 Post-Budget Forum, Mr Arhin said tighter fiscal measures would be needed to ensure that additional liquidity in the financial system does not fuel inflation. “The government is going to spend, the economy is going to expand, we know DDEP payments are going to be made, the private sector is going to come into the economy and all this will make money available into the economy. It needs to be balanced,” he said. He added that monetary policy would remain important in managing inflationary pressures, particularly where money entering the economy is not being used productively. “My anticipation is that there will be a tighter fiscal policy to put inflation in check, to make sure that we do not have excess liquidity in the system and the liquidity is being efficiently utilised,” he said. On public expenditure management, Technical Advisor at the Ministry of Finance, Dr Theo Acheampong, said the introduction of commitment authorisation had strengthened government’s control over spending and reduced the accumulation of unexpected expenditure obligations. He explained that previously, some government agencies outside the central spending system incurred expenditure that was not captured in the budget, resulting in significant bills emerging towards the end of the financial year. “In the past we did not have a firm handle on government spending. I'm happy to report that we do have significant handle on the spending at the centre,” he said. “That is no longer the case,” Dr Acheampong added. Meanwhile, Associate Director for Tax at PwC, Laura Torgbenoo Fiagome, said tax incentives for businesses operating at the ports would be tied to measurable performance commitments, including job creation and increased investment. She explained that the incentives were not intended to provide businesses with unconditional tax relief but to encourage activities that would expand economic activity and ultimately increase government revenue. “So it's not free money at all. There would be performance agreements that would be signed, and it would be monitored. The companies have to create more jobs that's employing people,” she said. Ms Fiagome added that increased employment and investment could generate higher tax revenues through Pay As You Earn (PAYE) and other tax categories. On the inflation outlook, Associate Director at Fitch Solutions, Mike Kruiniger, warned that climate-related pressures, particularly the developing El Niño weather event, could pose risks to Ghana’s inflation outlook in 2027. He said the weather phenomenon could trigger droughts in some regions and flooding in others, disrupting agricultural production and adding to price pressures. “We think El Niño will add to those pressures. As you know, some of you might know the current El Niño event is shaping up to be one of the strongest on record,” he said. Ghana’s 2027 Budget targets total expenditure of GH¢389 billion, with no new taxes announced. It also provides GH¢30 billion for the first year of the four-year, US$10 billion New Economy programme, which runs from 2027 to 2030.

Title: Ghanaian farmers losing confidence in rice farming – CSIR-CRI Chief Scientist
Content: The Chief Research Scientist and Director at the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research–Crops Research Institute (CSIR-CRI), Professor Maxwell Darko Asante, says Ghanaian farmers are losing confidence in rice farming due to difficulties in selling their produce. He attributes the situation to the influx of cheaper imported rice, which he says has made it difficult for locally produced rice to compete in the domestic market. According to him, repeated government assurances to purchase locally produced rice have yielded little or no results, leaving farmers with large quantities of unsold produce. "So for the last couple of years, farmers, especially rice farmers, have suffered a lot because there are a lot of cheap imports and they are not able to sell their rice. So announcing a policy is not enough for them to go back to the field; even if they wish to go back to the field, there is no money for them to go back," "The confidence of the farmers has really been broken," he said onJoy FM's Super Morning Showon Tuesday, November 17. Professor Asante said the situation has discouraged some farmers to the extent that they no longer want to invest in rice cultivation. He cited an interaction with some rice farmers who openly told him they had lost interest in the business because the government had failed to purchase their produce, while imported varieties continued to dominate the market. "We invited some farmers from one of the Brong areas to train in seed production. When they came, about 20 farmers told us that not a single one of them planted rice this year because they are not able to sell the previous year's harvest," he said. "So it is very important that the government does that (purchase their rice) immediately to restore confidence in rice farming," he added. He said the development poses a challenge to efforts to strengthen Ghana's domestic rice production, particularly at a time when the country is seeking to expand its industrial and agricultural capacity. His comments come amid discussions about Ghana's production capacity following reports that Africa's richest man, Aliko Dangote, has expressed interest in investing in the country's proposed super factory. Title: NADKANSCO commissions 100-tonne-per-day cashew processing factory in Bono East, boosting Ghana’s value-addition drive
Content: NADKANSCO Processing Limited has officially commissioned its modern cashew processing factory at Tuobodom in the Techiman North District of the Bono East Region, marking a significant milestone in Ghana’s efforts to expand local agro-processing, retain economic value and strengthen its position in the global cashew industry. The commissioning ceremony was attended by His Excellency John Dramani Mahama, President of the Republic of Ghana, alongside government officials, traditional authorities, financial institutions, industry stakeholders, farmers and members of the business community. With an installed processing capacity of 100 metric tonnes of raw cashew nuts per day, the facility is designed to operate continuously across three shifts, positioning it among Ghana’s largest investments in the cashew-processing sector. Speaking at the ceremony, Managing Director of NADKANSCO Processing Limited, Belinda A. Adokpa, described the commissioning as a major step in the company’s transition from raw commodity trading to value-added agro-industrial production. “NADKANSCO began in 2012 as an agro-commodity trading company. For many years, we participated in the export of raw cashew nuts. However, we recognised that the jobs, technical skills and economic value associated with processing needed to remain in Ghana. Today, we are proud to be part of the solution through this investment in local processing,” she stated. Between 2022 and 2024, the company exported approximately 39,700 metric tonnes of raw cashew nuts, primarily to India and Vietnam. The decision to invest in processing represents a strategic shift towards retaining more value within Ghana’s economy. ADVANCING VALUE ADDITION AND EXPORT GROWTH The NADKANSCO facility will process raw cashew nuts into several marketable products, including whole, split and broken cashew kernels, Cashew Nut Shell Liquid (CNSL) and cashew shell cake. The cashew kernels will be graded, hygienically processed and packaged to meet international market requirements, while CNSL will serve as an industrial raw material for products such as paints, varnishes, resins and brake linings. Cashew shell cake will also be utilised as biomass fuel, supporting the company's resource-efficiency and waste-reduction objectives. According to the company, the factory is expected to generate more than US$40 million in foreign exchange earnings annually at the initial stage of operations, with projections exceeding US$100 million annually at full operation. Its established export network covers markets in Europe, Asia, North America and the Middle East. STRENGTHENING THE CASHEW FARMING VALUE CHAIN A central component of NADKANSCO’s investment is its commitment to supporting the farmers who supply the factory. The company has established the NADKANSCO Cashew Outgrower Programme (NCOP), designed to improve farmer productivity, enhance raw material quality, strengthen market access and promote sustainable farming practices. The programme is built around a registered network of approximately 6,000 cashew farmers. Under Phase One, supported by Ghana EXIM Bank, NADKANSCO targeted the training of 1,000 farmers but successfully trained 1,247 farmers across Tain, Wenchi, Nkoranza North and Techiman North within four weeks. The training covered financial management, record keeping and good agronomic practices. Participating farmers also received agricultural tools and equipment, including pruning saws, cutlasses, knapsack sprayers, pruning scissors and Wellington boots, at no cost. Phase Two is expected to extend the programme to an additional 2,000 farmers across eight districts. Planned interventions include farmer training in grafting and post-harvest handling, the establishment of 16 community aggregation and quality centres, GPS mapping of farms for traceability, formal off-take agreements and the provision of 20 boreholes for cashew-growing communities. The company is targeting yield improvements of at least 30 per cent among participating farmers. CREATING JOBS AND IMPROVING COMMUNITY WELFARE At full operational capacity, NADKANSCO projects that the factory will create approximately 1,500 direct jobs and an additional 3,000 indirect employment opportunities across farming, aggregation, transportation, logistics and related services. The company has placed particular emphasis on employment opportunities for women and young people from Tuobodom, Techiman and surrounding communities. To support employee welfare, the facility includes an on-site crèche, a clinic providing medical services and health screenings, and free transportation for workers through four company buses. The company has also highlighted its commitment to skills transfer, with expatriate technical experts mandated to train Ghanaian employees in processing technology, quality control and machinery operations. Beyond the factory, NADKANSCO has donated four fully equipped ambulances to district hospitals in Atebubu, Wenchi, Kintampo and Techiman North. It has also committed five per cent of its proceeds to community development initiatives in Techiman and the communities supplying its raw cashew. GHANA EXIM BANK’S ROLE IN THE INVESTMENT Ghana EXIM Bank played a significant financing and developmental role in the establishment of the factory, supporting the acquisition of plant and machinery, working capital for raw cashew procurement and the first phase of the company's outgrower programme. The partnership reflects the importance of development finance in supporting Ghanaian businesses to move beyond raw commodity exports towards local manufacturing and value-added production. NADKANSCO has acknowledged the Bank’s support and reaffirmed its commitment to meeting its financial obligations while expanding the company’s contribution to Ghana’s export economy. SUPPORTING GHANA’S INDUSTRIALISATION AGENDA The commissioning of the factory aligns with Ghana’s broader industrialisation and economic transformation priorities, including the 24-Hour Economy, the Feed the Industries agenda and the national ambition to increase local processing of tree crops. The company believes that increased investment in domestic cashew processing will strengthen the agricultural value chain, create sustainable employment, improve farmer incomes, increase non-traditional export earnings and position Ghana as a more competitive participant in the international cashew market. In her closing remarks, Managing Director Belinda A. Adokpa expressed appreciation to the Government of Ghana, Ghana EXIM Bank, the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, the Tree Crops Development Authority, the Ghana Free Zones Authority, traditional authorities, financial partners, farmers and employees for their contributions to the project. She reaffirmed NADKANSCO’s commitment to building a competitive and sustainable cashew processing enterprise that creates lasting value for Ghana. NADKANSCO Processing Limited — From Ghanaian Cashew to Global Markets. ABOUT NADKANSCO PROCESSING LIMITED NADKANSCO Processing Limited is a Ghanaian agro-industrial company established in 2012, with roots in agro-commodity trading and a strategic focus on cashew processing and value addition. Through its modern processing facility in Tuobodom, Bono East Region, the company seeks to transform Ghanaian raw cashew nuts into quality products for domestic and international markets while supporting farmers, creating employment and contributing to sustainable economic development.

Title: NADKANSCO to create 1,500 direct jobs and over 3,000 indirect jobs – MD
Content: The Managing Director of NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited, Belinda Akorfa Adokpa, says the company is expected to create 1,500 direct jobs and more than 3,000 indirect jobs as it expands its cashew processing operations. In her welcome address at the commissioning of the facility by President John Dramani Mahama in Techiman on Monday, November 16, 2026, Ms Adokpa said Ghana EXIM Bank's intervention had provided a major boost to the company's operations. She said the factory received major financial support from the bank. She said the company would also train cashew farmers to improve production and ensure a consistent supply of raw materials to sustain the factory throughout the year. The training programme, she explained, forms part of efforts to strengthen the relationship between the company and farmers while addressing the challenge of seasonal supply shortages. "Your Excellency, this factory will create 1,500 direct jobs together with some 3,000 indirect jobs for farmers, transporters, aggregators and traders," she said. "The majority of our workers are women," she added. She said securing adequate quantities of raw cashew nuts was critical to keeping the factory operational throughout the year and sustaining the jobs expected to be created.

Title: NADKANSCO targets export market with cashew kernels, shell liquid and briquettes
Content: NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited in Techiman is preparing to supply international markets with processed cashew products, including cashew kernels, cashew nut shell liquid and briquettes, as Ghana intensifies efforts to add value to its agricultural produce. The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Export-Import Bank (Ghana EXIM Bank), Sylvester Adinam Mensah, disclosed this during the commissioning of the factory by President John Dramani Mahama in Techiman on Monday, November 16, 2026. He said the facility would also produce cashew-based products for the domestic market as part of efforts to expand the range of goods manufactured locally. “Today, NADKANSCO is ready to export the following: cashew nuts of all grades, cashew nut shell liquid, briquettes, all for the foreign market,” he said. “For the local market, NADKANSCO is ready to sell cashew cakes, briquettes and roasted kernels,” the CEO added. Mr Mensah said the factory represented a major step towards retaining more economic value from Ghana's cashew production instead of exporting the nuts in their raw state for processing elsewhere. He noted that Ghana produced more than 262,000 metric tonnes of raw cashew nuts last year, but only 17,000 metric tonnes were processed locally. According to him, the NADKANSCO facility has an installed capacity to process up to 33,000 metric tonnes of raw cashew annually, creating opportunities for increased production, employment and export earnings. The Ghana EXIM Bank CEO said the bank had committed approximately $12 million to support the project, including funding for automated processing equipment, working capital and workforce training. The factory has already created nearly 1,000 direct jobs and supports an additional 3,000 livelihoods across the cashew value chain. Mr Mensah said the investment would help create jobs, strengthen local industries and support farmers by providing a ready market for their produce. He urged the company's management to scale up operations and utilise the facility's full production capacity, assuring them of the bank's continued commitment to the project.

Title: Mahama calls on local and foreign investors to tap into US$10bn New Economy Programme
Content: President John Mahama has urged local and international investors to take advantage of Ghana's US$10 billion New Economy Programme, which is expected to mobilise investments across eight priority sectors between 2027 and 2030. He made the appeal at the maiden Invest Ghana Summit 2026 in Accra on Monday, November 16, where he highlighted the private sector's role in driving manufacturing, creating jobs and transforming the economy. The programme is expected to attract investment into strategic sectors of the economy as part of efforts to accelerate industrialisation and expand economic opportunities. At the summit, the Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, outlined six key government commitments aimed at creating a favourable environment for investors and accelerating industrial development. She highlighted investment opportunities in garment manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, automotive components, sugar production and oil palm processing. On garment manufacturing, the Minister disclosed that four projected factories are expected to generate approximately 36,000 direct jobs when operating at full capacity. Founder and Chief Executive Officer of the Dangote Group, Aliko Dangote, also called on African countries to strengthen domestic investment and develop industries capable of processing their own raw materials. He stressed the importance of building local industrial capacity to create more value within African economies.

Title: Achievements of ‘New Economy’ must be measured by sustained improvements in economic growth, employment and productivity – Dr. Nsafoah
Content: A US-based Assistant Professor of Economics at Niagara University, Dr. Dennis Nsafoah, wants the success of the New Economy measured by sustained improvements in economic growth, employment, and productivity. According to him, the New Economy cannot ultimately be judged by the size of its capital budget. Before the 2027 Budget, he raised three questions: How much of the additional fiscal space would be devoted to new public investment? How would the government finance the programme? And how would it reconcile an ambitious reserve-accumulation agenda with urgent investment needs? According to him, the budget offers satisfactory answers to all three. In his commentary on the budget titled “Ghana's 2027 Budget: From Macroeconomic Stability to Prioritising Public Investment”, Dr. Nsafoah said the 2027 Budget identifies a markedly larger public investment envelope, communicates a mainly domestic financing strategy and offers a measured formal reserve-adequacy benchmark. “These are reasons for a constructive assessment, not a guarantee of success”. Dr. Nsafoah, who is also a member of the Board of Tesah Capital also said the most consequential risk is the capacity to finance new investments while repeatedly refinancing the inherited stock of domestic obligations at sustainable cost. “That risk deserves monitoring, but not alarmism”, he pointed out. “Ultimately, I will judge the New Economy by whether Ghana produces more per worker, attracts additional private investment, creates durable jobs and achieves sustained growth—not by how large the capital budget appears on presentation day. The government has made a promising allocation choice. The economic verdict must follow the results”, he explained. Financing the New Economy: Domestic Borrowing and Its Implications The government in the 2027 Budget clearly identified how it intends to finance the New Economy programme. The 2027 cash deficit is budgeted at GH¢65.8 billion (3.6% of Gross Domestic Product), with GH¢85.0 billion in net domestic financing and GH¢17.7 billion in net external repayments. In effect, Dr. Nsafoah said the domestic markets will fund both the fiscal deficit and the net repayment to foreign creditors, highlighting that the budget projects GH¢59.0 billion in net financing from commercial banks and GH¢25.9 billion from non-bank investors. He stressed that limited new external borrowing reduces exposure to new foreign-currency debt, but places greater demands on domestic financial intermediation. He added that the more important concern is the government's gross financing requirement and the associated refinancing risk, rather than the GH¢85 billion in net domestic borrowing alone. “Beyond financing new expenditure, the government must also repay or refinance maturing Treasury bills and other domestic debt obligations. Ghana's substantial stock of short-term government securities, together with significant debt maturities scheduled for 2027 and 2028, creates additional pressure on domestic financial markets”, he warned. Consequently, he said the government's ability to sustain its investment programme will depend partly on its capacity to manage these refinancing obligations while maintaining favourable borrowing conditions.

Title: Ecobank Joy Business SME Fair offers businesses platform to expand market reach
Content: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are using the Ecobank Joy Business SME Fair to showcase their products, attract new customers and explore opportunities to expand their market reach. At the three-day exhibition, which ended on November 15 at the Ghud Park, Accra Mall, businesses across fashion, footwear, personal care, healthcare and childcare showcased products and services to consumers. Participating exhibitors say the fair provides an opportunity to introduce their brands to potential customers while creating awareness about products that may otherwise have limited market visibility. For footwear retailer Shoe Tse, the exhibition is an opportunity to reach consumers with different needs and purchasing preferences. The business says its product range covers footwear for children and adults, including sandals, flats, heels, slippers and football boots. "I have shoes for every occasion. Shoes for kids, adults, males, you can even get a shoe for yourself. Anything footwear I have, slippers I have," a representative of the business said. Beyond direct sales, some exhibitors are using the platform to highlight opportunities for wholesale distribution and wider commercial partnerships. Black Shea, a personal care products business specialising in African-inspired skincare and haircare, says it offers wholesale supplies to businesses interested in stocking its products. Its representative, Dora, said the company uses ingredients including shea butter, coconut oil and cocoa powder in some of its products. She explained that the business packages its liquid products in boxes of 12 and its bar soaps in boxes of 15 for wholesale distribution. "We do wholesale distribution. The liquid ones like these that you're seeing here, it's 12 in the box for wholesale. And the bar ones are 15 in the box for wholesale," she said. The exhibition also provided an opportunity for businesses to promote their distribution arrangements as a means of reaching customers beyond their immediate locations. Adele of Sonia Enterprise, which deals in clothing, shoes and bags for men, women and children, said the business accepts orders through WhatsApp and provides delivery services. Prestige Children's Palace is similarly using the fair to showcase a broader range of products, including children's clothing, footwear, baby food, feeding accessories and other household essentials. Its representative, Nanava, said the business seeks to serve different consumer needs through its range of mother and childcare products. Healthcare products also featured at the exhibition, with BB Chemist showcasing its Relax and Bedisol brands. Representative Peniel said Relax is marketed for digestive discomfort, while Bedisol is a topical pain relief balm. The diversity of products on display reflects the range of consumer markets SMEs are targeting as they seek to grow their businesses and build stronger customer relationships. With the exhibition now over, participating businesses will be looking to convert the visibility and customer connections gained at the fair into sustained sales and longer-term growth.

Title: Customers report service outages at major US banks
Content: Thousands of customers at major US banks, including JP Morgan Chase, Wells Fargo and Bank of America, have reported trouble accessing services. Chase Bank - the largest banking institution in the US - said a "software bug" in its hardware systems may have been behind the glitch and noted the impacts may have affected other banks. It added the issue was "temporary" and not "systemic" or "cyber-related". Problems appeared to be easing for many customers by early Monday evening. The issue comes after a string of unrelated technical problems last week, including a massive Microsoft outage, as well as a telecommunications issue and network failure that grounded all US flights. Problems started throughout the afternoon on Monday. There were almost 5,000 reports of Chase Bank's services being down, according to the Downdetector website. Chase Bank told it's customers that "some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete" but they still had "access to their accounts and funds". The bank, a subsidiary of JP Morgan Chase, serves more than 86m customers at 5,000 branches across the US, as well as 7.4m small businesses, according to the company's webpage. It is also the top credit card issuer in the US. The exact nature of the bug was unclear. The BBC has contacted Chase Bank. Another institution, US Bank, said some its systems were not directly affected but clients using the Zelle, a digital payment platform, received error messages saying their payments could not be sent. Zelle has said its service is "operating as it should" and issues at other banks could be affecting payments. Customers also reported issues with Truist, PNC and Capital One but all these companies told the BBC they have not been impacted. As of 1800 ET (2300G), Chase, Bank of America and US Bank had seen a fall in the number of reported outages.

Title: Fidelity Bank Atta Gyan calls for greater investment in Ghana’s productive sectors to drive industrial growth
Content: Fidelity Bank Ghana has called for greater mobilisation of domestic capital, investment in technology, and targeted policy interventions to accelerate industrialisation and turn Ghana’s economic recovery into sustainable growth. Atta Yeboah Gyan, Deputy Managing Director, Operations and Support Functions, Fidelity Bank Ghana, made the call at the 2026 Ghana Economic Forum, where the Bank served as Lead Sponsor. The Forum was themed “From Stabilisation to Scale: Mobilising Capital, Technology, and Policy for Ghana’s Next Industrial Wave.” Addressing business leaders, policymakers, investors, and other stakeholders, he acknowledged Ghana’s progress in restoring macroeconomic stability but stressed that the next challenge was converting those gains into stronger businesses, increased production, jobs, and sustainable growth. “Stabilisation is not the final destination. The real test is whether we can turn that stability into investment, stronger businesses, increased production, more jobs and sustainable growth,” he said. Atta Yeboah Gyan pointed to Ghana’s growing dependence on gold exports as a vulnerability that must be addressed. In 2025, gold accounted for approximately US$20 billion of the country’s US$31.1 billion merchandise exports, representing almost two-thirds of total export earnings. By August 2026, its share had risen to 66%. While acknowledging gold’s importance to the economy, he argued that Ghana must leverage its natural resource earnings to build a more diversified productive economy, with greater emphasis on manufacturing, local processing and value addition. “The concern is that too much of our external stability now depends on a single commodity whose price is determined beyond our borders,” he noted. Drawing lessons from Malaysia’s cocoa-processing industry and Switzerland’s chocolate industry, Mr Gyan highlighted the importance of moving beyond raw material production to capture greater value through processing, branding, quality standards and global distribution. He also identified the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) as an opportunity for Ghanaian manufacturers to access a continental market of more than one billion consumers. On financing, Mr Gyan said Ghana has significant domestic resources to support industrial expansion, citing pension funds holding more than GH¢100 billion and growing insurance investments. He called for investment instruments that better reflect industry needs, including longer-term bonds for factories and financing structures aligned with agricultural production cycles. He also highlighted Fidelity Bank’s ambition to list on the Ghana Stock Exchange, describing it as part of the Bank’s conviction in developing Ghana’s capital market. “If Ghana’s savings are to fund Ghana’s industry, then Ghanaian companies, our own included, must be ready to open our books, meet the market’s standards and earn that capital,” he said. Sharing Fidelity Bank’s technology experience, Mr Gyan noted that more than 90% of the Bank’s transactions now take place through digital channels. Its automation programme saves more than 18,000 staff hours annually and has delivered approximately GH¢5 million in measured benefits. Service level adherence also improved from 84% to 97% within 12 months. He stressed that technology investments must deliver measurable improvements in productivity and service, supported by clean data, reliable digital processes and effective systems. On policy, he emphasised the importance of reliable, affordable electricity for industrial expansion, calling for collaboration among government, financial institutions, and private investors to develop sustainable energy solutions. He also highlighted the need to reduce agricultural financing risks through partnerships among government, banks and development partners, ensuring that financing reaches the entire value chain, from farmers and aggregators to processors. In conclusion, Mr Gyan said Ghana’s next phase of growth requires collective responsibility from government, investors, businesses, and financial institutions. “Stabilisation has largely been the work of government and the central bank. They have done their part. Scale is everyone’s work,” he said. He reaffirmed Fidelity Bank’s commitment to supporting Ghana’s economic development as a lender and partner to businesses, and to contributing to a stronger financial system that can finance the country’s next phase of industrial growth.

Title: BoG flags renewed inflationary pressures as rate rises to 5.5% in October
Content: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) is closely monitoring emerging inflationary pressures following an increase in headline inflation to 5.5% in October 2026, from 5.2% in September. Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Asiama, says the latest increase requires a closer examination to determine whether the movement reflects temporary price adjustments or a more persistent shift in underlying inflation trends. Speaking at the opening of the 133rd Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, the Governor said although inflation remains in single digits and below the Bank's medium-term target band, the central bank cannot afford to be complacent. He said the committee would examine the contributions of food, non-food and services inflation, alongside developments in inflation expectations. The assessment will also consider the potential impact of movements in fuel prices, transport fares and administered prices on the inflation outlook. "While inflation remains below our medium-term target band, the recent uptick warrants careful examination," Dr Asiama said.
