Equity-linked structures depend on the performance of the referenced shares or indices, while Credit-Linked Deposits expose investors to the credit risk of the reference entity. Both also create exposure to the institution providing the investment solution. The development of these products will require engagement among investors, financial institutions and regulators. Investors need sufficient expertise and governance arrangements to evaluate the structures, while providers must ensure that the products are transparent, suitable and properly understood. Regulators also have an important role in establishing the conditions under which innovation can take place without compromising the protection of investors or the stability of the market. Used within appropriate regulatory and investment limits, structured solutions can broaden the range of opportunities available to local institutional investors and contribute to the continued development of Ghana's financial market. Gerald Nana Kusi is the Head, Institutional Sales and Structuring, Absa Bank Ghana LTD

Title: A policy born out of sight, not sympathy: Ghana’s new dawn for persons with disabilities
Content: The launch of the Free Tertiary Education for Persons with Disabilities Initiative by His Excellency John Dramani Mahama has ignited renewed hope and pride among Ghana’s disability community. Beyond promises, this policy marks a visionary step; one that recognizes ability over disability and sets Ghana on course to become a continental model of inclusive development. A POLICY OF SIGHT: SEEING ABILITY OVER DISABILITY For many years, the refrain among persons with disabilities in Ghana has been one of hope mixed with uncertainty, hope for recognition, inclusion and empowerment, as well as uncertainty about when that hope would materialize into real systemic change. Today, that narrative is being rewritten. The announcement by His Excellency John Dramani Mahama, President of the Republic of Ghana, during the launch of the Free Tertiary Education for Persons with Disabilities Initiative, at the Accra College of Education on Friday, 24thOctober, 2025 has rekindled an unprecedented sense of optimism, dignity, and a sense of belonging among the disability community. This bold vision marks a memorable turning point in our nation’s moral and social consciousness; one that views disability not through the lens of sympathy, but through the lens of sight, fairness, and capability. A VISION ROOTED IN EMPOWERMENT AND EQUITY What makes this initiative exceptional is not merely its content, but its philosophy. For the first time in Ghana’s policy history, disability inclusion is being pursued not as an act of charity, but as a strategic national development goal. The initiative recognizes that disability should not prevent a qualified Ghanaian from pursuing a university degree, Higher National Diploma (HND) or diploma. It seeks to make tertiary education more accessible to persons with disabilities who are most often excluded as a result of financial circumstances. The policy provides for the payment of eligible beneficiary’s academic and residential fees in all public tertiary institutions as part of the support package. From the passage of the Persons with Disabilities Act 2006, Act 715, to the allocation of portions of the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF) to persons living with disabilities, and to the creation of Disability Health and Resource Centres across second-cycle and public tertiary inclusive institutions in Ghana, this is a comprehensive national vision grounded in equity, empowerment, and opportunity. The President’s directives have sent a clear message: Persons with disabilities are not liabilities to be pitied, but assets to be developed and celebrated. His emphasis on transforming our national mindset “from commiseration to partnership, from exclusion to empowerment, and from antagonism to solidarity” has resonated deeply within the hearts and minds of all Ghanaians who believe in justice and inclusion. COMPLETING THE CIRCLE OF INCLUSIVITY In the spirit of compassion, fairness, and nation-building, it is timely to make one heartfelt appeal; to extend the “Free Tertiary Education for PWDs Policy” to graduate persons with disabilities. The pursuit of higher education beyond the undergraduate level is a critical step for persons with disabilities to be fully equipped to contribute at the highest levels of governance, leadership, and national development. While free tertiary education will open doors to countless young persons with disabilities, many graduates continue to face financial and structural barriers as they pursue postgraduate degrees or professional certifications. By expanding this special intervention to covergraduate-level studies, persons with disabilities will not be left behind in policy, administration, and leadership roles where graduate qualifications are most often a requirement. Furthermore, Ghana will complete the circle of inclusivity His Excellency has so admirably begun. A further and compelling justification for extending this special initiative to postgraduate education is the employment reality confronting many persons with disabilities after graduation. Currently, too many PWDs who successfully complete tertiary education still struggle to secure employment in spite of their qualifications and capabilities. For some, an undergraduate degree does not provide a sufficient competitive advantage in an increasingly demanding labour market, where advanced qualifications, specialist knowledge, and professional credentials can influence access to meaningful employment and leadership opportunities. Without targeted support to pursue further studies, many capable graduates with disabilities risk remaining unemployed or being excluded from positions for which they could otherwise be well qualified. Extending the policy to cover postgraduate and other relevant graduate-level programmes would therefore help remove a major financial barrier and enable eligible PWDs strengthen their expertise, broaden their career prospects, and compete more effectively for employment. In the long term, this investment could also help position more persons with disabilities to contribute meaningfully to policy formulation, implementation, and evaluation, as well as to public administration, institutional leadership, research, and national development. The policy should not merely help PWDs enter tertiary institutions; it should also help create pathways for them to progress, lead, and participate in shaping the decisions that directly affect their lives and the future of Ghana. Such a move would not only enhance access but would also position Ghana as a continental leader; a nation where education becomes the ultimate tool of liberation for all citizens, regardless of physical condition. It would demonstrate that our compassion is matched by courage, and our vision by conviction. A CALL TO COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY The President has rightfully called upon the private sector, civil society, universities, and the media to join in this noble vision. Disability inclusion cannot be the work of government alone; it must be a shared national mission. Let us, therefore, as a people, take the bull by the horn and ensure that this transformative policy becomes a living and breathing testament of Ghana’s moral strength and developmental maturity. In conclusion, this new chapter in Ghana’s disability rights movement reminds us that true progress is not measured by sympathy, but by systems; not by handouts, but by opportunities; and not by rhetoric, but by results. Indeed, we are witnessing a policy born of sight, not sympathy. A sight that sees beyond physical limitations to the vast potential that lies within every Ghanaian. And as we move forward together as persons with, and those without disabilities, we reaffirm a shared truth: when inclusion becomes the norm, development becomes unstoppable. Isaac Ansah is the Ghana Gas Disability Liaison Officer, as well as the Senior Community Relations and CSR Officer for the Community Relations Division of Ghana National Gas Ltd Company, where he advocates for inclusive development and disability empowerment. His work focuses on corporate social responsibility, inclusive education, and livelihood empowerment programmes for persons with disabilities. #JohnMahamaDisabilityLegacies #InclusionIsNationBuilding#AbilityOverDisability#EducationForAll

Title: Ghana’s black gold and the quest for value
Content: The modern era of Ghana's petroleum industry began with the establishment of the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) in 1983 under the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation Act (PNDCL 64). The GNPC was mandated to lead the nation's efforts to explore oil and gas resources efficiently. For decades, the sector saw exploratory efforts that eventually culminated in major commercial discoveries, transforming Ghana into a notable player in the West African energy market and requiring a robust, multi-tiered regulatory framework to manage the newfound wealth. While exploration began in the late 19th century, the watershed moment arrived in 2007 with the discovery of the Jubilee Field deep waters off the coast of the Western Region. By December 2010, Ghana poured its "first oil," joining the ranks of African oil producers. The TEN (Tweneboa, Enyenra, Ntomme) and Sankofa Gye Nyame fields followed quickly. Ghana's oil and gas industry is structurally divided into three distinct subsectors: upstream, midstream, and downstream, each governed by specific operational parameters and regulatory bodies. The Petroleum Commission strictly regulates upstream activities (exploration and production). Petroleum Agreements (PAs) facilitate private investment, combining concession and product-sharing elements. The upstream sector involves petroleum exploration, development, and production. Operations are strictly corporate endeavours, subject to a Petroleum Agreement (PA) with the Republic of Ghana and the GNPC. The PA is a hybrid of a concession agreement and a product-sharing agreement. The Jubilee Field: The Pioneer Tullow Oil operates the Jubilee field, which remains the bedrock of Ghana's petroleum output. After its inception in 2010, production ramped up rapidly and stabilized around 100,000 kbpd by 2014. Despite technical challenges, , Jubilee has maintained resilient output. Recent infill drilling and the Jubilee South East (JSE) project have helped mitigate natural decline rates, keeping production near 74,000 kbpd in 2026. The addition of the TEN field in August 2016 and the Eni-operated Sankofa field in mid-2017 catalyzed the sharp rise in Ghana's total output. It peaked shortly after coming online but has experienced steeper-than-expected natural declines, falling from 64,000 kbpd in 2018 to an estimated 14,000 kbpd in 2026. Crucial not only for crude oil but also for non-associated gas that feeds Ghana's thermal power plants. Sankofa's oil production peaked at around 53,000 kbpd in 2018 and has declined more gradually, stabilizing at about 32,000 kbpd in 2026. Ghana's midstream sector encompassing natural gas processing, transmission, wholesale supply, and distribution is currently undergoing regulatory evolution. While historically less developed than the upstream and downstream segments, it is critical for domestic power generation. The Energy Commission (EC) is the statutory regulator and grants licenses for Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) facilities and pipeline networks. In 2015, the GNPC was designated as the Gas Sector Aggregator (GSA) to act as the sole buyer and seller of bulk natural gas, though recent administrative shifts have seen the Ghana National Gas Company Ltd (GNGC) increasingly assume this role. The downstream industry covers the importation, refining, storage, distribution and marketing of petroleum products. This sector operates under a liberalized pricing regime allowing industry players to set ex-refinery and ex-pump prices based on a prescribed formula. The ex-pump price build-up is complex incorporating the core ex-refinery price, various margins (marketers', dealers', BOST), and multiple statutory levies such as the energy debt recovery levy, road fund levy and sanitation and pollution levy.The market is highly liberalized, with numerous Petroleum Service Providers (PSPs), Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), and Bulk Distributing Companies (BDCs) operating. The Future of Oil and Gas in Ghana Ghana became a commercial oil and gas producer with the discovery of the Jubilee field in 2007 and the first oil in December 2010. The petroleum subsector quickly became a primary driver of foreign direct investment (FDI), government revenue, and GDP growth. Over the last decade and a half, the sector expanded from a single-field operation to a multi-field complex, incorporating the Tweneboa, Enyenra, Ntomme (TEN) project and the Sankofa field in the Offshore Cape Three Points (OCTP). The future of Ghana's oil and gas sector hinges on successfully integrating its traditional hydrocarbon wealth with the imperatives of the 21st-century green economy. Regulatory frameworks—from stringent local content requirements to environmental safeguards demonstrate a commitment to retaining domestic value and promoting sustainable practices.

Title: Co-Conspirators in Malfeasance: The legal case for arresting both bribe-givers and public officers
Content: Recent administrative petitions submitted to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs regarding the procurement of diplomatic passports have thrust a glaring spotlight on deep-seated administrative corruption. At the heart of these petitions lies a disturbing narrative: individuals allegedly paying off state officials to secure high-level sovereign travel documents to which they have no lawful right. When a petitioner attempts to utilize administrative channels to complain that a corrupt arrangement failed, a dangerous legal and moral fiction is exposed. The petitioner often attempts to cast themselves as an aggrieved customer cheated out of a service, but in reality, they are an active, willing participant in a corrupt enterprise. Under domestic anti-corruption frameworks, both the citizen who offers the bribe and the public official who accepts it are equally culpable. True institutional accountability demands that law enforcement agencies, including the Criminal Investigation Department, look past the self-serving framing of these petitions and arrest both parties. A cornerstone defense often floated in administrative corruption scandals is the claim of exploitation under the premise that state actors took their money. However, this argument collapses the moment legal eligibility is examined. A diplomatic passport is not a commercial commodity or a luxury item available to the highest bidder; it is a high-security instrument of state representing sovereign trust, international immunity, and official representation. By law, such credentials are strictly reserved for accredited diplomats, qualifying government officials, heads of state delegations, and designated high public officials under established administrative guidelines. If a petitioner is fundamentally ineligible for a diplomatic passport, every unit of currency handed to an official is an intentional inducement designed to subvert the law. The petitioner is not paying for a legitimate service, but rather for illegal state-sanctioned misrepresentation. By willingly participating in a scheme to bypass statutory vetting, the petitioner commits active bribery—an offence that treats the corrupt inducer with the same severity as the corrupt receiver. Conversely, the public officer who accepts money to issue or facilitate an unmerited passport commits a profound betrayal of public trust. Public servants take an oath to uphold the laws and constitution of the state, serving as custodians of national integrity. When an official monetizes administrative bottlenecks, creates artificial barriers, or sells sovereign travel credentials to unqualified applicants, they act as economic mercenaries within the civil service. This behaviour violates service regulations and degrades the international standing of the nation's travel documents. When foreign border authorities realise that diplomatic credentials can be purchased through back channels, the security value and diplomatic courtesy extended to every legitimate passport issued by the state are severely compromised. This systemic threat requires rigorous enforcement of statutory instruments, notably the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29), and the Criminal Offences (Amendment) Act, 2020 (Act 1034). Section 239 of Act 29 penalizes official corruption, wilful oppression, and extortion by public officers, while Section 252 strictly prohibits active participation in corrupting public officers through unlawful gratification. Furthermore, the legislative reforms introduced under Act 1034 reclassified corruption offenses to carry severe custodial sentences ranging from 12 to 25 years imprisonment. These stringent penalties reflect the legislative intent to eradicate corruption across both public and private sectors, ensuring that neither the bribe-giver nor the bribe-taker escapes judicial scrutiny. A half-baked anti-corruption campaign that targets only the bribe-taker while shielding the bribe-giver creates a dangerous moral hazard. It encourages citizens to treat state bribery as a viable transactional cost, operating under the assumption that if an application is rejected, they can simply pay their way through, and if caught, claim victimhood. To dismantle this cycle, the law must be applied uniformly. Without citizens willing to subvert rules with cash, corrupt networks within public offices would starve. A petition complaining that an illegal payment did not deliver the desired outcome is nothing less than a criminal confession wrapped in a grievance. When an ineligible applicant attempts to buy a diplomatic passport, both the hand that gives the bribe and the hand that takes it are tearing down the rule of law. The Criminal Investigation Department and relevant investigative bodies must treat these petitions not as civil disputes over service delivery, but as direct evidence of a criminal conspiracy. Interdicting compromised officials is a necessary administrative first step, but true justice requires the immediate arrest and prosecution of both the corrupt officers and the ineligible petitioners who sought to buy what they never deserved. The writer is Gilbert Attipoe, who can be reached at: Gilbertattipoe90@gmail.com

Title: AFCON 2027Q: Somalia wins enough ‘motivation’ for Black Stars ahead of final two games – Ati Zigi
Content: Ghana goalkeeper Lawrence Ati Zigi believes the six points against Somalia gives the team the needed motivation ahead of the their final two games of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers. Ghana recorded their first back-to-back wins in over a year following their victory over Somalia on Monday with Jordan Ayew scoring from the penalty box. For Ati Zigi, the two games against Somalia brings relief to the team following their poor start to the campaign. “I think with football, it's like a rollercoaster, and sometimes it goes up, sometimes it comes down. We didn't have a good start, but going into these games, we knew we wanted some points to be able to catch up, so that's why we came together as a team,” he said. “We spoke all together, and we had one goal, to have six points, and to work together as a team, and that's what we showed today. We can be very happy going to the next game, full of motivation, and hopefully we can make the group.” The result leaves Ghana in third place ahead of the final two games of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers campaign.

Title: Amputee World Cup: Black Challenge thrash Iraq to secure Round of 16 spot at Amputee World Cup
Content: Ghana’s Black Challenge  thrashed Iraq 6-0 in their final group game of the WAFF Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico to secure qualification for the Round of 16. Ghana headed into the encounter desperately needing a convincing victory to boost their chances of progressing to the knockout stage after suffering a 2-0 defeat to Angola and playing out a 1-1 draw with Colombia. Coach Richard Obeng’s side made their intentions clear early on, with star player Mohammed Mubarik opening the scoring with a stunning long-range strike to give Ghana the lead. Hamza Mohammed then doubled the advantage as the Black Challenge took control of the encounter, growing in confidence and piling pressure on their opponents. Ghana continued their dominance after the break, adding to their tally to complete an emphatic 6-0 victory and seal their place in the Round of 16. The result saw the Black Challenge finish second in Group D, behind Angola, who defeated Colombia 2-0 in the other group fixture. Ghana will play USA in the round of 16 on Wednesday, November 18 as they continue their quest for a maiden Amputee Football World Cup title.

Title: FIFA immortalises Caleb Yirenkyi’s torn Black Stars jersey at World Cup museum
Content:
FIFA has immortalised Caleb Yirenkyi’s torn Black Stars jersey from the 2026 FIFA World Cup, preserving a piece of Ghanaian football history at its museum in Zurich, Switzerland. The jersey was damaged during Ghana’s opening match against Panama, in which the midfielder scored a dramatic last-minute winner to secure a 1-0 victory. Yirenkyi’s match-worn shirt is expected to become part of the FIFA Museum’s permanent collection, where it will be preserved for historical purposes and future generations. The gesture recognises a memorable moment from Ghana’s campaign at the first 48-team edition of the World Cup. OFFICIAL:  FIFA Museum has immortalized Caleb Yirenkyi’s Black Stars kit which got ripped off during the World Cup in North America.

The World Football Governing body has kept the shirt in a special wardrobe for Historic reasons as it also serves as a one of the monumental factors which will remind the world about its first ever 48-team World Cup campaign. The jersey also joins other significant football memorabilia, including the shirt worn by former Black Stars captain Asamoah Gyan during Ghana’s 2010 World Cup campaign in South Africa. Gyan’s jersey documents one of the most heartbreaking moments in Ghanaian football history, when he missed a last-minute penalty against Uruguay in the quarter-finals before the Black Stars lost in the subsequent shootout. The Black Stars finished third in Group L with four points after a 1–0 win over Panama, a goalless draw with England and a defeat in their final group game. Ghana’s campaign ended on July 4 in Kansas City following a narrow 1–0 Round of 32 loss to Colombia, with Jhon Arias scoring the winner in the 14th minute. The Black Stars finished as Africa’s fifth-best team, recording one win, one draw and two defeats.

Title: Ghana’s Maxwell Woledzi named MLS Defender of the Year
Content: Nashville SC center back Maxwell Woledzi was named the 2026 Major League Soccer Defender of the ​Year on Monday. In his first season ‌in the league, the 25-year-old from Ghana helped Nashville set MLS records for clean sheets (17) and ​fewest goals allowed in a 34-game ​season (25). Woledzi contributed two goals and one assist ⁠in 34 matches to help Nashville ​win the Supporters' Shield and set additional MLS ​marks for points (77), wins (23) and fewest losses (three). He led the team in clearances (44) and completed passes (2,100) and ​was third on the squad in ​aerial duels won (80). Woledzi was the only player in the ‌league ⁠to complete more than 2,000 passes with at least 94% passing accuracy. Teammates Jeisson Palacios and Andy Najar finished second and third ​in the voting, ​respectively. ⁠The award is voted on by MLS club technical staff, media ​and current MLS players. Woledzi is the ​second ⁠player in franchise history to win Defender of the Year, joining back-to-back winner Walker ⁠Zimmerman (2020 and ​2021). He is the ​second African player to earn the honors after the ​Columbus Crew's Steven Moreira in 2024.

Title: AFCON 2027Q: We did better than first game – Kim Lars Bjorkegren
Content: Interim Black Stars coach Kim Lars Bjorkegren believes his team played much better on Monday than they did in the first game against Somalia. The Black Stars recorded their first back-to-back wins in over a year following their victory over Somalia on Monday. The Black Stars claimed all three points against the Somalis at the Essipong Stadium with a 1-0 win. Jordan Ayew scored the only goal of the game, scoring from the penalty spot to give Ghana six points from their last two games. Despite scoring one fewer than they did in the encounter last Thursday, Bjorkegren believes the return leg performance was an improvement on the first outing. “They were a little bit similar. Like I said, I think we started both games well. I think overall the first half was better today than the other day,” he said. “Of course, you can always look at the numbers and say, hey, we scored 2-0 the other day, and today only 1-0. But I don't think it's always the fact. If you look at the performance today, I think it's at least in the same level, maybe even better than in the previous game. “It's just that we need to take care of the chances a little bit better.” Ghana will now turn attention to their games against Côte d’Ivoire and Gambia in March 2027.

Title: The beacon of hope: Coach Opeele touts Andre Ayew as the man to rescue Ghana football
Content: A growing call for change at the top of Ghana football is gaining momentum, with former Black Stars captain Andre "Dede" Ayew emerging as the people's favourite to lead the Ghana Football Association (GFA) into a new era. In a Facebook post, football coach Isaac Opeele - who openly declares his affiliation with GFA President Kurt Okraku - has described Dede Ayew as the "beacon of hope" for Ghana football, arguing that the growing public clamour for the former national campyain to contest the GFA presidency, is not about hatred for the current leadership, but about a desire for change, following what he says many believe are the ills of the current administration. Why Ghanaians want change Kurt Okraku is in the final and 8th year of his second term as GFA President, and despite the GFA's controversial move to amend its constitution in the middle of Kurt's final term to enable him run for a third term, Ghanaians and some football stakeholders have said Ghana football has deteriorated under the leadership of Kurt so he must bow out at the end of his term in the interest of Ghana football. And according to Opeele, the pioneer argument for change is not personal. "The pioneer argument and reason the Ghanaian public want a change at the GFA is not because they hate Kurt Okraku but they think the association is overly corrupt; they think the GFA has ceased to care about the feeling of the masses; they think the GFA leadership is incompetent," Coach Opeele wrote on Facebook. These reasons, Opeele added, is why Ghanaians and some football stakeholders have gladly welcomed the rumour of Dede Ayew's GFA presidential ambition - as they they see him as the vehicle to drive change. "Ghanaians just want Kurt Okraku to go. It is they gladly welcomed the rumour of Dede Ayew's GFA presidential ambition. They see Dede as the kind of vehicle or a strong force to drive into the fray to unseat Kurt Okraku," he added. Dede: The unifying figure With the front of football stakeholders said to have been sharply divided in the past seven years, Opeele described Dede as a unifier, likening him to ''that palatable central in a movie that can unite factions within the GFA to recreate the Black Stars' victorious glorious days. " Strong leadership qualities Coach Opeele touted many positives he argued are leadership qualities Andre Ayew possesses. First, he compared Dede's leadership character to that of Cameroon's Samuel Eto'o, who moved from the pitch to lead his country's football federation, before highlighting other strengths he stressed wi help Ghana football. "Dede Ayew has that strong vibrant character like Cameroon's Samuel Eto'o. He is bilingual i.e dealing French speaking countries in Africa. He is a famous international brand he appeals to the Gen Z's and he has an unmatched charisma," Coach Opeele continued. As the son of the influential Abedi Pele, Coach Opeele argued that Dede inherits a legendary status that will open doors for Ghana in the oil-rich Arab nations, Europe and at FIFA. As the conversation grows, Opeele noted that Dede has been smart - keeping mute over his interest directly, but continuing to show up at major football events "He has been smart and indirectly kept mute over his interest but keeps showing up at events to get under the skin of Kurt Okraku," Opeele noted, observing that the quiet presence has only fuelled the public rallying call. Publicly, the former Black Stars captain has attracted support from key figures across all walks of life. Among them is veteran broadcaster Kwame Sefa Kayi of Peace FM, who publicly backed Dede to seize the opportunity, a backing Opeele says referenced in his article. Also, Andre Ayews support is said to be growing among football stakeholders, with many of them admiring Ayew's courage to show up and rescue the game, rather than opting for the easy option of taking an appointment with the current administration. Concluding, Coach Opeele observed that both the public and the media have lost confidence in the GFA leadership, having sold it out as as "one with zero credibility, arrogant, ineffective and a predacious leader with no achievement." "Indeed, the Kurt Okraku's brand, that am part of, is becoming the biggest loser, he noted. Coach Opeele slammed the GFA President's 'present inner circle for ''telling him what he wants to hear," which he said ''is slowly killing Ghana football of which the public cannot afford to see it decompose hence the public rallying call on Dede Ayew."

Title: Cameroon, Senegal and Benin close in on AFCON 2027 qualification
Content: Nicolas Jackson was on target again as Senegal, Cameroon and Benin moved to the brink of qualification for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) with away victories. After Aston Villa striker Jackson had opened the scoring, Senegal gave up a 2-0 lead against Sudan before two late goals sealed a 4-2 win, while five-time Afcon winners Cameroon cruised to a 3-0 triumph over Namibia. A goal in second-half stoppage time from Ede Oloko sealed a 1-0 success for Benin against Central African Republic. All three sides are on 10 points in their respective groups after four rounds of matches and will progress to next year's finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda if other results go their way on Tuesday. Elsewhere, Jordan Ayew's first-half penalty was enough for Ghana to register back-to-back victories over Somalia in Group C. The Black Stars had home advantage for what should have been an away tie, with the game played in Sekondi-Takoradi because the Ocean Stars do not have a stadium fit for international football. Ayew had a penalty saved asGhana beat Somalia 2-0 in the reverse fixturelast Thursday, but the Sheffield United forward kept his composure when he sent the goalkeeper the wrong way in the 36th minute after Brandon Thomas-Asante had been pulled down in the box. Ghana, who parted company with Carlos Queiroz after losing their opening two fixtures, move level in the table with The Gambia, with both sides on six points. The Gambians are themselves three points adrift of group leaders Ivory Coast before they host the Elephants on Tuesday. Meanwhile, Guinea moved to the top of Group D after Yakhouba Barry scored twice in their 3-1 away win over Eritrea in neutral Cairo. The West Africans lead South Africa, who travel to Kenya on Tuesday, by two points in a group with only one qualification spot available because the Kenyans are assured of a spot at the finals as co-hosts. And Zimbabwe beat Equatorial Guinea 3-0 in Harare to go two points behind Group E table toppers DR Congo. Thando Ngwenya, Tawanda Chirewa and Tawanda Maswanhise were all on target for the Warriors before Equatorial Guinea's Josete Miranda had a penalty saved and Saul Coco was sent off for the visitors late on. The National Thunder were without first choice goalkeeper Jesus Owono afterhe asked not to be selectedfollowing his involvement in a collision with Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who died the day after the incident. DR Congo, Ivory Coast, Mali and Morocco can all book their tickets to the tournament when the fourth round of fixtures culminates with 18 matches on Tuesday. The final two rounds of qualifiers will be held in March next year, with Afcon 2027 scheduled to be held in East Africa from 19 June to 17 July. Patrick Vieira'sSenegalsurvived a scare in neutral Juba after Jackson's early goal put the Teranga Lions ahead and a low strike from Brentford left-back El Hadji Malick Diouf made it 2-0 midway through the first half. Sudan hit back through Al-Gozoli Nooh and Salah Adel to level proceedings with 15 minutes to play, but Pathe Mboup's lob made it 3-2 in the 87th minute and Paul Mendy made the points safe for the West Africans in the first minute of added time. Senegal are still awaitingthe outcome of their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sportover the destination of the 2025 Afcon title. The Teranga Lions beat Morocco 1-0 after extra time in January's final, but a Confederation of African Football appeals board stripped them of the title two months later, decreeing Senegal had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them. Mahamadou Nagida opened the scoring forCameroonagainst Namibia in neutral Botswana with a stunning volley from outside the box in the 12th minute, and Ryan Fosso's deflected effort doubled the lead just before the hour mark. Saidou Alioum made it 3-0 with a fine first-time volley with 19 minutes remaining, and David Pagou's men will be assured of a place at Afcon 2027 if Congo-Brazzaville fail to beat Comoros on Tuesday. Namibia0-3Cameroon (Group G) Sudan2-4Senegal (Group J) Zimbabwe3-0Equatorial Guinea (Group E) Somalia0-1Ghana (Group C) Eritrea1-3Guinea (Group D) Central African Republic0-1Benin (Group F)

Title: Vinicius says transfer interest affected Real form
Content: Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr says he felt "truly overwhelmed" by transfer speculation in the summer, which has contributed to his mixed form at the start of the season. The Brazil international has scored just once and provided three assists in 12 appearances for Jose Mourinho's side this season. He was linked with a move to Premier League champions Arsenal this summer as he entered the final year of his contract, before signing an extension at Real. The 26-year-old also says he did not train as much as he should have following Brazil's last-16 exit at the World Cup. "I don't think I prepared as well as I could have after the World Cup, because the impact of that tournament is so significant for all Brazilians," he said. "Being knocked out so early was something we hadn't expected. So, I took advantage of my holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in previous years. "That may have affected my start to the season. "On top of that, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs showing interest last summer, I felt truly overwhelmed, as with the situation at Real Madrid. But it's a very long season." Vinicius received a red card for violent conduct in October when he pulled the hair of Villarreal midfielder Nathan Saliba, which led to a four-match suspension. In his absence,record signingYan Diomande has made the most of his opportunity on the left wing, scoring four goals. Vinicius joined Real from Brazilian side Flamengo in 2018 and has scored more than 20 club goals in each of his past five seasons. Mourinho's side are second in La Liga, three points behind rivals Barcelona, and return to league action when they host Celta Vigo on Saturday.

Title: 2027 Budget: Gov’t to complete National Sports Policy, finalise Ghana Sports Fund regulations
Content: Government has announced plans to deepen institutional and policy reforms in the sports sector, including completing the National Sports Policy and finalising regulations for the Ghana Sports Fund. The commitment was contained in the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy presented by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson to Parliament on Thursday. According to the budget, Government will prioritise the completion of the National Sports Policy and its implementation framework, alongside the finalisation of regulations under the Ghana Sports Fund Act, 2025 (Act 1159). The Government also intends to review the Sports Act, 2016 (Act 934), as part of efforts to strengthen the institutional and legislative framework governing sports development in the country. The proposed reforms come as the Ministry of Sports and Recreation continues efforts to establish a more structured and sustainable system for sports development. In September 2026, the Ministry held a national validation workshop on the draft National Sports Policy, bringing together stakeholders to review and refine the document before its finalisation. Sports Minister Kofi Iddie Adams said at the time that the Ministry was working to complete the validation process and move the document through the necessary legislative procedures for consideration by Cabinet and Parliament. The Ghana Sports Fund is another major component of the Government's planned reforms. Established under Act 1159, the Fund is intended to provide sustainable financing for sports development, including athlete welfare, grassroots sports, infrastructure development and capacity building. The 2026 Budget had indicated that Cabinet had approved the establishment of the Fund, with the enabling legislation and regulations expected to be presented to Parliament. The latest commitment to finalise the regulations represents another step towards establishing the operational framework for the Fund. Meanwhile, the proposed review of the Sports Act, 2016, is expected to form part of broader efforts to improve the administration, promotion and development of sports in Ghana. The Act established the National Sports Authority and provides the legal framework for the development, management and promotion of sports in the country. The extent of the proposed amendments and the timeline for completing the various reforms were not immediately outlined in the budget statement.

Title: OSP opens investigations into NSA World Cup visa scandal
Content: The Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) has opened investigations into suspected corruption involving some officials of the National Sports Authority (NSA) and alleged financial irregularities surrounding Ghana's participation in the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The investigations cover allegations of abuse of public office, irregularities in the selection of sponsorship beneficiaries, visa facilitation arrangements and the collection and management of money from prospective travellers. In a statement, the OSP said it had received petitions alleging corruption and corruption-related offences in the award of contracts by the NSA to various service providers. It is also examining claims that some individuals who won competitions organised under World Cup sponsorship initiatives were excluded from the final lists of beneficiaries submitted to foreign diplomatic missions. The investigation will seek to establish how beneficiaries were selected, who authorised the allocation of travel opportunities and whether public officials or private individuals improperly benefited from the arrangements. The latest development adds another layer to a controversy that has already triggered a police investigation, a presidential inquiry and the suspension of former NSA Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah. JoySports' investigations, published on MyJoyOnline on September 14, 2026, first exposed allegations that more than $623,000 had been collected from prospective travellers seeking assistance to obtain visas for the tournament in the United States and Canada. The investigation tracked about nine victims who said they had paid between $4,000 and $25,000 for visa assistance through individuals connected to the NSA. Information gathered by JoySports suggested over 170 people paid money to a chain of NSA officials for visa assistance to the USA. 46 were denied. 34 never got an appointment date. 50 were not processed at all. Of these, approximately 37 secured visas. All applicants seeking Canadian visas were unsuccessful. The investigation implicated Mr Ankrah and the NSA's former Chief Operations Officer, Yaw Gyamfi Kusi Awere, alongside Nana Boateng Gyimah, Chief Executive Officer of TRIBE Culture Fest. A petition submitted to the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service by Mr Awere alleged that Mr Ankrah received $56,000 in commission from money collected from prospective travellers. Mr Gyimah was also accused of receiving $511,000. Mr Awere, who acknowledged the allegations to JoySports, said he had been involved in collecting money from applicants and that the funds were subsequently shared among individuals connected to the arrangement. Mr Ankrah, however, has denied wrongdoing, insisting that he neither collected money from prospective travellers nor participated in any arrangement to facilitate visas. The controversy took another turn in October when JoySports reported that $26,000 had been paid to the police on behalf of Mr Ankrah. The payment, reported on October 20, was made by a friend of the suspended NSA boss, with his approval and that of his lawyers. Sources familiar with the transaction told JoySports that the amount formed part of the $56,000 Mr Awere alleged Mr Ankrah had received as commission from proceeds linked to the visa arrangements. The individual who made the payment had reportedly undertaken to settle the outstanding balance. The payment followed Mr Awere's petition to the police seeking assistance to recover the alleged commission and facilitate refunds to prospective travellers who had paid for visa assistance but were unsuccessful. When contacted by JoySports on October 15 for a response to the reported payment, Mr Ankrah did not respond. He has maintained that although he exchanged money with Mr Awere over the years, he was unaware that any of the funds represented commissions from prospective travellers. He has also challenged anyone to produce evidence that he collected money to facilitate visas. On October 1, President John Dramani Mahama suspended Mr Ankrah as Director-General of the NSA pending investigations by the CID. The decision followed a report submitted to the Presidency by Sports and Recreation Minister Kofi Adams after allegations of financial impropriety emerged. Professor Emmanuel Osei Sarpong was subsequently appointed Acting Director-General of the Authority. The suspension came after JoySports published details of the alleged visa arrangements, including claims that an office at the Accra Sports Stadium had been used by individuals connected to the operation. The NSA has denied authorising visa facilitation activities or permitting its premises to be used for collecting money from prospective travellers. The Minority in Parliament has also questioned the roles of the NSA, Ghana Tourism Authority, Ministry of Sports and Recreation and TRIBE Culture Fest in the arrangements. Vincent Ekow Assafuah, Ranking Member of Parliament's Youth and Sports Committee, has raised concerns about discrepancies in lists submitted to foreign diplomatic missions. He alleged that only 15 of 102 individuals presented as NSA personnel could be verified as employees of the Authority. The Minority has called for a broader independent investigation into the institutions and individuals involved. President Mahama has also established a committee chaired by Professor Francis Dodoo to examine the allegations. The OSP's intervention means the controversy will now face scrutiny beyond the police investigation into the alleged collection of money for visa assistance. The inclusion of NSA procurement contracts introduces a separate area of inquiry into how the Authority awarded contracts and whether public officials or private entities benefited improperly. The OSP says it will provide further information on the investigations in accordance with its disclosure policy. It has cautioned that the commencement of investigations does not establish wrongdoing and that all individuals and institutions concerned remain presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Title: LA 2028 Olympics: African Boxing Qualifiers Scheduled For August 2027
Content: The African Boxing Qualifiers for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games have been scheduled for 13th - 22nd August, 2027 in Accra. In a statement confirming the date and the fact of Ghana's successful hosting bid, the Ghana Boxing Federation (GBF) said ''It is a major milestone for Ghanaian boxing and a national assignment. We are extremely excited about this opportunity. This is not a responsibility for the Ghana Boxing Federation alone. It is a national assignment, and we need the support and commitment of all stakeholders to make it a success.'' The GBF also called on the government for assistance. ''We want to call on the Government of Ghana, the Ministry of Sports and Recreation, the Ghana Olympic Committee, corporate Ghana, the media, and all stakeholders to rally behind the Federation.'' Government support is essential because the ‘‘Host City Agreement’’ - a binding legal contract between the IOC and Ghana - places specific obligations on the Ministry of Sports and Recreation. The agreement clearly spells out all local operating expenses, including public security, police escorts, medical services, and specialized infrastructure upgrades, and who is responsible. In the past, the IOC has retained all major commercial revenues—including broadcast rights, ticket sales, and official sponsorships—while host cities receive no direct share of those earnings. For Ghana’s part, the government, through the Ministry for Sports and Recreation (and possibly the Accra Metropolitan Assembly), will assume all associated costs, including intra-and inter-city transportation, accommodation arrangements, existing boxing infrastructure requirements, etc. However, the operational support and expertise will come from the Ghana Boxing Federation. The tournament will provide a home platform for Ghana's national teams, the Black Bombers and Black Hitters, as they pursue Olympic qualification. It will also boost sports tourism, showcase Ghana's rich boxing heritage, and strengthen the country's position as a leading destination for international boxing.

Title: 2027 AFCON Qualifiers: 'We did better today than the last game'  - Interim Black Stars head coach
Content: InterimBlack Starshead coach Kim Lars Bjorkegren says the team performed better in their reverse fixture against Somalia than the home encounter. Ghana narrowly edged Somalia after skipperJordan Ayewconverted from the spot in the first half. The win moved Ghana to six points in Group C but the team remain in third place behind Gambia who have six point and play Ivory Coast on Tuesday. Despite the Black Stars creating decent openings, the team walked home with a 1-0 win, a goal short of the 2-0 win Ghana recorded in the home attire. Both games were played at the Essipong Stadium due to Somalia not having an approved ground by CAF. Reflecting on the team's performance, Interim Black Stars head coach Kim Lars Bjorkegren believes the Black Stars performed better. "You can always look at the numbers and say we scored 2-0 the last time but I can say we did better today" Ghana will return to action in 2027 when they take on Ivory Coast and Gambia. The Black Stars failed to make the AFCON in the last edition and will be eager to seal their place in the forthcoming competition.

Title: New delivery room, kindergarten block brings relief to two communities in Nadowli-Kaleo
Content: For years, women in Sampina gave birth in difficult and undignified conditions. There was no proper delivery room, no privacy, and little comfort for expectant mothers. In Biire, children aged between three and five had to walk more than three kilometres to Pala every day to attend kindergarten, navigating bush paths and often making the journey in the rain. This week, the stories of the two communities took a positive turn. In Sampina, a new delivery room has been completed at the Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) Compound, while in Biire, a new kindergarten block has been handed over to the community. The two projects are expected to improve access to essential healthcare and early childhood education in the Nadowli-Kaleo District of the Upper West Region. The new delivery room in Sampina was constructed through a partnership between Azumah Resources and the people of the community. While residents provided the labour, Azumah Resources supported the project with materials and other resources. The Member of Parliament for Nadowli-Kaleo, Anthony Mwinkara Sumah, subsequently supported the initiative and joined community members and other stakeholders for its commissioning. The midwife in charge of the Sampina CHPS Compound, who has served the community for three years, expressed relief and gratitude, describing the new facility as a major improvement in her working conditions. "I want to thank our Honourable MP for this good work, with the support of Azumah. We have had several visits from Azumah here, and today, the place is complete. I am very grateful," she said. Recalling some of the difficulties she encountered while attending to women in labour, she said the poor condition of the former delivery space sometimes made her work frightening. "I remember there are times I come in the night to do delivery, and maybe a lizard will fall, and I will take off running. So if I have a very beautiful place like this, I do not know how to express the joy," she added. She disclosed that despite the lack of a proper delivery environment, she had conducted 71 deliveries and registered more than 300 clients during her three years at the facility. The District Chief Executive for Nadowli-Kaleo, Mary Haruna, said the new structure represented more than an improvement in healthcare infrastructure, describing it as a symbol of dignity for women and the wider community. "This structure signifies dignity to the women and the men themselves. This structure is an encouragement to women and the people of this community," she said. She assured residents that the District Assembly remained committed to improving healthcare delivery across the district. "As an Assembly, we are committed to supporting the development of healthcare delivery in this community and the district as a whole. We know maternal mortality will reduce, and then our child healthcare will improve," she stated. Beyond the new delivery room, residents used the occasion to raise other development concerns, including the lack of electricity in more than 40 communities, the need for staff accommodation for health workers and the completion of their Junior High School (JHS) block. Responding to the concerns, Mr Sumah said the government had plans to extend electricity to all communities in the Upper West Region. He explained that a similar exercise had been completed in the Savannah Region, with the Upper West Region expected to be next. "There is a plan by the government to extend electricity to every community in the Upper West Region. It has happened in Savannah. All the communities in Savannah are now connected to the national grid, and the next region is the Upper West Region," he said. On the request for staff accommodation, the MP said an assessment would be conducted to determine the necessary support. Regarding the unfinished JHS block, he said the District Chief Executive had undertaken to deploy officers to assess the remaining work and establish what was required to complete the project. For years, young children aged between three and five had to travel to Pala to access kindergarten education, covering more than three kilometres daily through bush paths and often under difficult weather conditions. The Nadowli District Director of Education, Vivian B. Nyekanga, said the situation exposed the children to several risks and made access to early childhood education difficult. "Before the provision of this facility, our little children in Biire faced considerable challenges. They had to travel from Biire to Pala to attend school, exposing them to various risks, including being caught in the rain and other dangers associated with travelling through bush paths," she said. She said the new kindergarten block would bring relief to parents and provide children with a safer and more comfortable learning environment within their own community. "Today, that story has changed. Through the generosity of our Honourable Member of Parliament, these children can now access education in a safe, comfortable, and child-friendly environment within their own community," she added. Explaining how the project was initiated, Mr Sumah said it was a community-led effort in which residents provided the labour while he supplied the materials needed for construction. "The community agreed to start a community project, so that I could assist with the materials. From the commencement, it has been the community providing the labour, and then I was providing the materials," he explained. The MP urged residents to take ownership of the facility by ensuring that children were enrolled and regularly attended school. He warned that the investment would serve little purpose if parents failed to send their children to the new facility. "My plea is that the school now belongs to the community. If you do not bring the kids to school, it is a white elephant. I cannot think of a life now without education," he said. The completion of the two projects marks an important step towards addressing some of the basic development challenges facing Sampina and Biire. For women in Sampina, the new delivery room offers a more dignified environment for childbirth and improved working conditions for health workers. For children in Biire, the kindergarten block brings early childhood education closer to home, reducing the risks and difficulties associated with travelling long distances to school. Although residents continue to call for improvements in electricity, healthcare accommodation and other educational infrastructure, the two facilities represent meaningful progress in their efforts to secure better living conditions. They also demonstrate the importance of collaboration between communities, public officials and private-sector organisations in addressing local development needs.

Title: Academic City, BoG, IIPGH explore ways to secure Ghana’s digital financial ecosystem1 hour
Content: Academic City University, in partnership with the Bank of Ghana and the Institute of ICT Professionals Ghana (IIPGH), has called for stronger collaboration among financial institutions, technology companies and academia to strengthen the security of Ghana’s rapidly expanding digital financial ecosystem. The call was made at a Cybersecurity in FinTech Roundtable organised as part of Ghana’s 2026 National Cyber Security Awareness Month. The event brought together regulators, academics, fintech professionals and cybersecurity experts to examine emerging threats and explore practical measures to strengthen cybersecurity in the digital finance sector. It also sought to address how Ghana could continue scaling digital financial innovation without compromising cybersecurity, consumer protection, or the resilience of financial institutions and digital platforms. Speaking at the event, the Head of the Offensive and Defensive Unit at the Bank of Ghana, Mr Eric Afanu, said customers who lost their savings to fraud risked permanently losing confidence in digital financial services. “If a market trader loses her savings through a wallet takeover and cannot recover the money, she may lose confidence in digital finance as a whole,” he stated, adding that security, trust and institutional resilience are the foundations on which sustainable innovation is built. Mr Afanu noted that although mobile money and digital banking had expanded financial inclusion, they had also created new opportunities for fraudsters, particularly through impersonation and manipulation. He urged financial institutions to strengthen complaint-handling systems to ensure victims of fraud received timely, fair assistance. He also called for stronger oversight of third-party technology and cloud service providers, stressing that financial institutions remained responsible for protecting their customers even when services were outsourced. On artificial intelligence (AI), Mr Afanu advocated clear governance, regular testing and human oversight to prevent its misuse for sophisticated impersonation and fraud. He said sustained public education, particularly in local languages, to help vulnerable groups such as market traders, farmers and older people identify and avoid digital fraud is critical now. Dr Muhammad Suraj, Director of Graduate and Continuous Education, Academic City University, said the university’s decision to combine its annual fintech conference with the cybersecurity roundtable reflected the growing need to balance financial innovation with digital security. He said the discussions focused on strengthening cyber resilience and digital infrastructure, preventing fraud, and improving governance around emerging technologies. According to him, although digital transactions appeared seamless to consumers, complex backend systems operated continuously to ensure service availability and security, exposing both users and service providers to risks such as account takeovers, fraud, cyberattacks, system disruptions, and third-party vulnerabilities. He described artificial intelligence (AI) as a “double-edged sword”, saying although it could be exploited to facilitate sophisticated cyberattacks, it could also enhance intrusion detection, anti-malware systems and Security Operations Centre (SOC) operations. Dr Mark Tampuri, Head of the Department of Business and Entrepreneurship at Academic City University, said social engineering continues to exploit gaps in financial literacy, enabling fraudsters to manipulate victims through deceptive conversations to obtain sensitive information. He urged regulators to enforce clear policies that held financial institutions accountable, while service providers invested in robust security systems and customer education. He also encouraged consumers to remain vigilant and protect their personal and financial information. Richard Kafui Amanfu, Executive Director of IIPGH, said convenience should not replace caution, urging the public to pause and verify before clicking, sharing information, approving transactions or transferring money. According to him, every fraud case, SIM-swap attack and compromised account eroded public trust in the digital financial ecosystem. Mr Amanfu called on banks, telecommunications companies, technology firms, regulators, and industry bodies to collaborate to strengthen security, educate users, and stay ahead of emerging threats, stressing that protecting Ghanaians online is a shared responsibility.

Title: Gifty Oware trial: Private firm got GH¢30m loan meant for service personnel – Investigator1 hour
Content: A private company linked to the accused in the Gifty Oware trial received a loan of more than GH¢30 million meant to finance equipment for national service personnel, an investigator told the Accra High Court. Detective Sergeant Woode, the fourth prosecution witness, said the money was paid into Blocks of Life Consult Ltd's account on the accused person’s written instructions. He was answering questions from defence counsel Gary Nimako during cross-examination on Monday, November 16. The investigator said the accused, a former Deputy Executive Director of the National Service Authority (NSA), had signed a hire-purchase agreement with the Agricultural Development Bank. The arrangement was intended to finance equipment for national service personnel. However, he said that the company received the funds and that the names submitted as beneficiaries were fictitious. When defence counsel asked who the agreement identified as beneficiaries, the witness distinguished between those named in the document and the entity that received the money. “Even though on the master agreement it is stated as NSP being beneficiaries of the Hire Purchase Agreement, the actual beneficiary of this agreement was Blocks of Life Consult,” he told the court. He said the supposed beneficiaries never benefited because the accused person submitted fictitious names. Detective Sergeant Woode further said that investigations established connections between the accused person and the company’s directors. “During our investigation, we discovered that the accused person caused a change of directorship from the previous directors to its current directors.” He identified one director, Charles Antwi Obeng Jnr, as the accused person's errand boy. He described the second director, George Annan, as a former driver of the accused person’s mother, Kate Oware. The investigator told the court that the accused person had obtained Annan’s Ghana Card, Tax Identification Number and the residential address used in the company registration documents. He said Annan denied knowing the company or completing documents to register it. “During our investigation, George Annan indicated that he does not know of any company called Blocks of Life Consult neither has he filled a company registration document to register a company,” the witness said. Cross-examination is scheduled to continue through Thursday as the prosecution seeks to close its case.

Title: Mahama to assess the performance of all 261 MMDCEs in December1 hour
Content: All 261 Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) are to undergo a nationwide performance assessment following a directive from President John Dramani Mahama. The Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs will lead the exercise, which is expected to determine how effectively the local government appointees have delivered on their responsibilities since taking office. The assessment will begin immediately, with field evaluations scheduled to run from December 1 to 15, 2026. The ministry is expected to submit a comprehensive report to the President by December 20 for his consideration and further action. In a statement signed by the sector minister, Mahama Ayariga, the ministry said the evaluation would be independent and evidence-based, incorporating both documented performance and feedback from residents in the various districts. The exercise will measure the MMDCEs against six key performance indicators, with development, service delivery, local economic growth and poverty reduction accounting for the largest share of the assessment at 35 per cent. Revenue mobilisation and financial management will carry 20 per cent, while peace, security and chieftaincy relations will account for 15 per cent. Governance and accountability will also attract 15 per cent, citizen engagement and inclusiveness 10 per cent, and implementation of presidential directives and national programmes five per cent. Under the development indicator, the ministry will examine sanitation, road construction and maintenance, drainage systems, markets, lorry parks, schools and CHPS compounds. Job creation, support for economic activities and the implementation of social intervention programmes will also be assessed. The evaluation will further examine the assemblies’ internally generated funds and the timely submission of accounts relating to the District Assemblies Common Fund. On governance, attention will be given to General Assembly meetings, the operations of sub-committees and area councils, procurement procedures and compliance with public financial management laws. MMDCEs will also be assessed on their relationships with traditional authorities and religious leaders, their handling of chieftaincy and land disputes, and their management of District Security Council meetings. Citizen participation will be measured through town hall meetings, engagement with women, young people and persons with disabilities, live broadcasts of Assembly meetings, and responses to public complaints. The assessment will be undertaken by a team led by the ministry and the Regional Coordinating Councils, with participation from the Office of the Head of Local Government Service, the District Assemblies Common Fund office and the National Development Planning Commission. Two additional individuals from the relevant region or district may also be nominated by the minister. As part of the process, every MMDCE must submit a performance report with supporting evidence through a dedicated online portal by November 30. Evaluation teams will subsequently visit all 261 districts to verify reported achievements, inspect infrastructure and financial records, and engage Assembly Members, chiefs and residents. Citizens will also have the opportunity to rate their respective MMDCEs through a dedicated online platform. The ministry may additionally seek confidential assessments from intelligence agencies, Presiding Members and District Coordinating Directors. The final findings will be presented to President Mahama by December 20, 2026, to inform his consideration of the performance of the local government appointees.

Title: 8 seafarers rescued after months of detention in Iran welcomed to Ghana2 hours
Content:
Ghana has received eight seafarers who have regained their freedom after spending several months in detention in Iran, following diplomatic intervention by the government. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa met the returnees at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Tuesday, November 17, where they expressed their gratitude for the government's efforts in securing their release. The group had been detained after their fishing vessel was held amid the conflict in Iran. Their eventual release came after the Ghanaian government opened diplomatic discussions with Iranian authorities to resolve the situation. According to Mr Ablakwa, the Ministry's intervention followed a petition received on 7 September 2026, which prompted immediate engagement with the Iranian authorities. In a Facebook post announcing the meeting, the Minister described the occasion as a particularly emotional moment, recalling the circumstances surrounding the seafarers' detention. It was really heartwarming to receive a group of Ghanaians who were rescued in Iran after their fishing vessel was detained for several months due to the conflict. 

Following a 7th September, 2026 petition, Ghana’s Foreign Ministry immediately activated diplomatic negotiations with Iranian authorities for their release. 

We are grateful to the Iranian Embassy in Accra and our counterparts in the Islamic Republic of Iran for their impressive cooperation. 

The Foreign Ministry assures that we shall continue to assist the 8 rescued Ghanaian seafarers and ensure that they receive adequate compensation.

We will not relent in guaranteeing that Ghanaians in distress abroad receive urgent and compassionate consular support. 

May God bless them for the gratitude they came to express to staff of the Foreign Ministry. 

For God and Country 🇬🇭 🙏🏾 “It was really heartwarming to receive a group of Ghanaians who were rescued in Iran after their fishing vessel was detained for several months due to the conflict,” he wrote. He also expressed appreciation to Iranian officials for their role in the negotiations, particularly the Iranian Embassy in Accra, whose cooperation helped facilitate the release. “We are grateful to the Iranian Embassy in Accra and our counterparts in the Islamic Republic of Iran for their impressive cooperation,” Mr Ablakwa stated. The Minister further assured the eight Ghanaians that government support would continue beyond their return, adding that the Ministry would pursue appropriate compensation for the hardship they experienced while in detention.

Title: Cars you cannot import into Ghana in 2026: Full list of banned vehicles
Content: PAY ATTENTION:Mark YEN.com.gh as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! Ghanaians planning toimport vehiclesfrom countries such as theUnited States, Germany, Canada and Dubai must familiarise themselves with Ghana's vehicle importation regulations before making purchases. TheGhanaStandards Authority (GSA) introduced stricter requirements on October 1, 2026, to prevent unsafe and substandard vehicles from entering the country. The regulations cover vehicle age, structural condition, safety features and other technical requirements. Dubai bans 8 food and item categories at airports: what Ghanaian travellers should know Reason for restriction Vehicles older than 15 years Exceed permitted age limit Flood-damaged vehicles Water damage and safety concerns Fire-damaged vehicles Serious fire-related damage Vehicles with damaged chassis Compromised structural safety Vehicles with damaged safety cages Broken, bent, cracked or twisted structures Vehicles assembled from spare parts Do not meet assembly requirements Vehicles designated for scrap Not considered roadworthy imports Vehicles without km/h speedometer readings Fail speedometer requirements Right-hand-drive vehicles Generally restricted unless special approval is granted The GSA clarified in August 2026 that the age restriction applies to used vehicles exceeding 15 years, replacing an earlier proposed 10-year limit. Minor cosmetic damage does not automatically disqualify a vehicle, provided it satisfies applicable safety and roadworthiness requirements. According tothe GSA, vehicles shipped before October 1, 2026, are exempt from the new requirements, even if they arrive after the implementation date. Title: "I could lose my life": Gay Ghanaian detained in Sweden amid push for asylum
Content: PAY ATTENTION:Mark YEN.com.gh as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! A 33-year-oldGhanaian man has been held at a Swedish detention facility for six months while his asylum application remains unresolved, with the man warning that deportation to Ghana could cost him his life. Joy News reported that Samuel Asiamah, who is seeking asylum on the basis of his sexuality, has been confined at a facility in Åstorp, roughly an hour north of Malmö, according to a report by The Irish Times published on 12 September 2026. His lawyer has reportedly been unable to obtain a clear explanation from Swedish authorities regarding the basis for his continued detention, despite him holding valid asylum papers at the time he was held. Another young Ghanaian dies abroad after violent attack Asiamah told The Irish Times that trouble began at home in Ghana after his mother grew suspicious about his sexuality. PAY ATTENTION:Follow YEN's WhatsApp channel for a daily dose of breaking news on the go! Having been raised by his grandmother in a rural area, he relocated toAccraat 18 to live with his mother, who he said subjected him to repeated church blessing sessions and gradually withdrew from him. He left home at 19 and found community through a local LGBTQ+ support group called Solace. His first relationship, however, brought renewed hostility, with verbal abuse escalating into physical violence. He still carries a scar from one of those assaults. Asiamah later connected with a man referred to as "Brother Kofi", who arranged his travel toEurope. He used 60,000 Ghana cedis from his mother's savings to fund the journey, travelling through Mauritius to France before arriving in Sweden in November 2024. The facilitator allegedly abandoned him on arrival. Doris Adu Gyamfi: Javits' mother speaks as 17-year-old suspect is arrested After a week without shelter, a woman offered him accommodation but asked him to leave upon learning of his sexuality. Swedish police eventually found him on a snow-covered street and directed him towards support services. Asiamah submitted his asylum application in Malmö in February 2026. At a hearing in May, he raised Ghana's parliamentarypassage of a billthat would criminalise the promotion of LGBTQ+ activities, carrying prison sentences of up to 10 years, and a provision compellingfamilymembers to report one another. His case officer reportedly dismissed both developments as irrelevant because he had not personally been subject to the proposed law. Swedish authorities have pressed him to engage with the Ghanaian Embassy to facilitate his return, a step he has flatly refused. "There is a difference between co-operation and placing your life in jeopardy," he said. "If people in prison know you are homosexual, you will be brutalised and assaulted, and you could lose your life." His case reflects a broader tightening of Swedish migration policy. Asylum applications in Sweden fell by 96 per cent from their 2015 peak to 6,737 in 2025, and the country's approval rate stood at roughly 23 per cent, less than half the European Union average. An organiser of a Malmö-based asylum support group assisting Asiamah described the shift bluntly: "It used to be seen as a victory in Sweden to protect people here from unsafe situations, but these people have been so dehumanised now that getting rid of them quickly is the new victory." Title: Meet Dr Letitia Obeng? Scientist and Theodosia Okoh's sister whose image was allegedly used on new GHC50 note
Content: PAY ATTENTION:Mark YEN.com.gh as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! The unveiling of Ghana's new GH¢50 banknote, which features the late flag designer Theodosia Salome Okoh, has been overshadowed by a family dispute over whether the portrait on the currency actually depicts her at all. Dr Eddie Obeng, a nephew ofTheodosia Okohand son of the late Ghanaian scientist Dr Letitia Eva Obeng, raised the concern after inspecting the note. In a LinkedIn post, he said he initially felt pride upon seeing his aunt honoured, but on closer examination, he believed the portrait bore a stronger resemblance to his mother than to Okoh. Bank of Ghana finally breaks silence on Theodosia Okoh cedi note portrait controversy TheBank of Ghanaresponded through board member Beatrice Annan, who stated that three verified photographs of Theodosia Okoh were used as the basis for the engraved image, with artistic adjustments made to satisfy banknote production and security standards. PAY ATTENTION:Follow us on Instagram - get the most important news directly in your favourite app! The confusion is not without precedent. In 2020, the South African publication The Continent issued a correction after mistakenly publishing a photograph of Dr Letitia Obeng while identifying her as Theodosia Okoh. The publication acknowledged that the two sisters had on occasion been misidentified in photographs published across various media. The latest dispute has brought renewed focus on Dr Obeng, whose contributions to Ghanaian science spanned more than six decades. Dr Letitia Eva Takyibea Obeng was born on 10 January 1925, in Anum in theEastern Region. She attended Achimota College between 1939 and 1946 before receiving a government scholarship to study at the University of Birmingham in the United Kingdom, where she earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Zoology in 1952, becoming the first Ghanaian woman to do so. She followed this with a Master of Science in Parasitology in 1962 and a doctorate in Tropical Medicine in 1964 from theLiverpoolSchool of Tropical Medicine, making her the first Ghanaian woman to obtain a PhD in science. Zimbabwean influencer’s Makola Market portrait allegedly appears on Ghana’s new GH₵1 note, video On returning to Ghana, she was appointed the first female science lecturer at what is now theKwame NkrumahUniversity of Science and Technology (KNUST) in Kumasi. She subsequently joined the Ghana Academy of Sciences and the National Research Council, focusing on parasitology and aquatic biology. Between 1965 and 1974, she served as director of the Institute of Aquatic Biology under the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), conducting research into the environmental impact of the Volta Lake and studying the black fly that transmits the parasite responsible for river blindness. Her work later took her to the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), where she became its first African female senior staff member in 1974 and, in 1980, the first African woman to lead UNEP's Regional Office for Africa. She was also unanimously appointed the first female president of the Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences in 2008 and chaired the Global Water Partnership from 2008 to 2012. Theodosia Okoh’s nephew responds after Bank of Ghana rep defends portrait on new GH¢50 heritage banknote Among her honours were Ghana's Order of the Star of Ghana in 2006 and honorary doctorates from both KNUST and the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine. The CSIR named a facility, the Letitia Obeng Block, after her in recognition of her scientific legacy. Dr Obeng died on 23 March 2023, at the age of 98. Parliament has approved the reconstitution of the country's delegation to the ECOWAS Parliament, restoring Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin to the group following aprolonged disputeover the country's representation in the regional body. The resolution paves the way forGhanato resume active participation in the ECOWAS Parliament after weeks of political tension that at one point placed the country's membership in jeopardy. The controversy began when Parliament moved to replace Afenyo-Markin on the delegation. Despite that decision, the Minority Leader continued to attend and participate in ECOWAS Parliament proceedings, where he holds the position of Third Deputy Speaker.
