Title: Young man dies in Circle railway fire after going back for his motorbike
Content: A young man died on Monday night when fire swept through wooden homes and shops beside the railway at Circle–Avenor in Accra. The blaze broke out at about 22:00 near the STC yard, close to where VIP and OA Transport Services buses park,as 3News reported when it began. Fire Service officer ADO1 Isaac Adomba Kwabena Opoku said the man had gone back into the burning area for his motorbike and was overcome by smoke. “The smoke overwhelmed him, and sadly, we found him lifeless,” he said. “As it stands, we have handed the body over to the police.” Opoku said the police would send the body for an autopsy at the Police Hospital before releasing it. He added that firefighters have no power to certify a death themselves. The man has not been identified. ADO1 Alex King Nartey of the GNFS Communications Team confirmed that an adult male died. Opoku put the damage at more than 100 wooden structures, many used as both homes and businesses. Nartey described the loss as several structures. It is not the first fire there this month. Earlier in November,fire gutted the lower floor of an unfinished building used to store scrap at the Circle Railway. Monday's fire hit a settlement where people both lived and traded, Opoku said, leaving debris and damaged property across the site. The cause is also disputed. Nartey told TV3’s Ghana Tonight that a cylinder explosion started the fire, while earlier reports from the scene said it was not yet known. Several fire appliances were sent, and crews worked for hours to keep the flames from reaching nearby buildings. Smoke hung over the Kwame Nkrumah Interchange through the night. No other casualties had been reported by early Tuesday. The same night,fire also broke out at the Tema Community 1 Market.

Title: Rice Farming: Fertilizer, seeds and tractor services have all become more expensive - Bawumia
Content: Flagbearer of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has visited the Asutuare Water Users Association in the Kpone Irrigation enclave. Prior to meeting the stakeholders, he toured their farms, inspected the irrigation facility, and visited one rice mill. Dr Bawumia described what he saw as sobering. "Our rice farmers cannot sell their rice even at half the old price because cheaper foreign imports have flooded the market. Meanwhile, fertiliser, seeds, and tractor services have all become more expensive," the former Vice President wrote on Facebook after his tour. He also noted that Phase 2 of the Kpone Irrigation Scheme has stalled. "Our millers are struggling with high electricity costs and no demand for their services," he said. Dr Bawumia made the point clearly that agriculture is a national security issue. If agriculture collapses, unemployment will rise, and the livelihoods of most Ghanaians will be destroyed, he said. "We must act with urgency to:  Restore the incentives previously given to farmers; use the government's purchasing power to support our farmers," he urged. He added that "We cannot preach food security while letting our own farmers go bankrupt. Our farmers feed this nation. It is time this nation fed them back."

Title: Takoradi traders doubt GH¢200m is enough to finish their market
Content: Traders at Takoradi Market have questioned whether theGH¢200 millionvoted in the 2027 Budget will be enough to complete the Market Circle redevelopment. TV3 reports that the traders "are questioning whether the proposed funding will be sufficient to deliver the project, as they await the fulfilment of the government's promise to redevelop the market." Thereport from the marketwas published on Friday, November 13, a day after the budget presentation. Finance MinisterCassiel Ato Forsonannounced the GH¢200 million allocation in his budget address to Parliament on Thursday, November 12. It sits inside GH¢17.6 billion voted for local governance, chieftaincy and religious affairs, according to thefull budget text. The same budget lines giveGH¢685 million eachto the New Agbogbloshie market in Accra and Kejetia Market Phase 2 in Kumasi. The statement also says contractors are on site at 208 of 260 market projects awarded under the District Model Market Initiative. The Takoradi project has stalled for years. In September the tradersrejected upfront payment demands and proposed their own eight-point financing plan, asking the government to finish the market first and recover the money over time. They addressed the plan to Mr Ayariga after his September 22 visit to the site. The contractor, Contracta Costruzioni Italia S.R.L., had said work could resume within a month, with the project 62 per cent complete. The minister, Mahama Ayariga, had proposed renting out the market's roughly 4,000 trading spaces to raise completion funds. What the budget does not say is what the Takoradi job will cost in total, or when it will be finished. It gives no completion date and no detail on stall allocation or what traders will pay.

Title: 2027 budget: Close revenue leaks - ISODEC tells Finance Minister
Content: In relation to the 2027 budget statement, the Integrated Social Development Centre (ISODEC) says it has noted the commitment to introduce no new taxes, the review and modernisation of the Income Tax Act and the Revenue Administration Act, and the review of Double Taxation Agreements in line with the United Nations framework convention on international tax cooperation. However, ISODEC said the budget speech does not include a tax expenditure statement, even as it adds new exemptions and incentives for solar equipment, rice hubs, Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) hotels, and medical tourism, and says little about trade mis-invoicing and transfer pricing. It urged the government to "close revenue leaks and improve compliance before considering measures that place additional pressure on households and workers." ISODEC further said that the provisions for the National Health Insurance Scheme (GH¢10.2 billion), Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) (GH¢1.1 billion), school feeding (GH¢2.1 billion) and the District Assemblies Common Fund (GH¢10.8 billion) are noted. They welcome the US$1 billion Pwalugu Multipurpose Dam, GH¢820 million for the northern Ghana water system and GH¢3 billion for rural electrification in the northern and western regions. Headline allocations are not sufficient evidence of improved support. "The relevant test is whether allocations rise in real terms, are released on time, and reach communities with the greatest needs. "The Budget should provide regional and district breakdowns of capital expenditure per person and assess the distributional effects of tax and spending decisions by income group, gender and region," the statement said. ISODEC further said that the 2027 Budget responds to several of the central priorities that they raised earlier. They welcome the decision to lower the primary surplus target to 0.5 per cent of GDP and use the space for a GH¢30 billion New Economy investment programme in 2027, capital expenditure of GH¢100.4 billion, now larger than interest payments, and firm targets for processing cocoa, gold, manganese and bauxite at home, and local-purchase rules for food, textiles and medicines, with no new taxes. These commitments deserve recognition. However, the Budget does not yet turn this welcome shift into measurable commitments on jobs, transparency and equity, ISODEC said in a statement In their assessment, the 2027 Budget partly meets expectations, "It delivers ISODEC’s central macroeconomic asks, a lower primary surplus target and a larger share of spending for productive investment, but it does not yet translate this shift into a measurable jobs target, transparent execution and reporting, or protections for equity and revenue integrity. In several areas, the Budget states intentions without providing measurable targets, implementation timelines, or reporting arrangements. "The difference between an announcement and a funded commitment matters. Budget at a glance: primary balance target 0.5% of GDP (legal floor 0.5%; 2026 target 1.5%); capital expenditure GH¢100.4bn, or 5.6% of GDP; employment target: none stated for 2027 (unemployment below 8% by 2030); New Economy programme GH¢30bn in 2027. Against the 28 asks in ISODEC's pre-budget statement: 5 met, 15 partly met, 8 not met," the statement said. ISODEC also indicated that stabilisation must now make room for employment and production. It said that Ghana has made important progress on macroeconomic stabilisation but the question for the 2027 Budget is how that progress will be used to address persistent unemployment, weak productive capacity and the country's exposure to foreign-exchange pressures. The fiscal framework should be judged by its effects on employment, inflation and the external balance, not by the pursuit of a fiscal ratio in isolation, it said. "The announced primary surplus target of at least 0.5 percent of GDP on a commitment basis, down from 1.5 percent in 2026, needs to be considered alongside capital expenditure of GH¢100.4 billion (GH¢120.5 billion including transfers), against a record of under-execution in 2026, when primary spending ran 3.4 percent below target to October. "While the GH¢30 billion New Economy allocation is welcome, the Budget speech does not yet set an execution target or commit to quarterly reporting of releases and spending by ministry, programme and region. The execution gap remains a serious concern: government must explain how it will ensure that approved capital allocations translate into completed projects and economic activity. Employment commitments need numbers, funding and accountability," it said. They acknowledge the removal of the cap on youth employment funding (an extra GH¢1 billion), GH¢2 billion for youth employment and skills, and the job projections for rice (about 125,000), oil palm (potential for more than 250,000) and pharmaceuticals (about 20,000). However, they said that the Budget speech does not set a 2027 employment target or a consolidated jobs target across the eight pillars, nor does it explain how jobs will be counted. "Unemployment below 8 percent (from 12.8 percent in 2025) is a 2030 goal only. Without these details, it is difficult to assess whether the announced programmes are commensurate with the scale of unemployment and youth exclusion. "The absence of a public employment guarantee pilot, particularly in deprived districts in Northern Ghana, is a missed opportunity. Government should use labour-intensive public investment in climate adaptation, irrigation, feeder roads, care and community services to provide paid work while meeting urgent development needs. Skills programmes must also be linked to vacancies and the requirements of productive firms."

Title: Agyinasare demands full disclosure of National Cathedral money
Content: Archbishop Charles Agyinasare has challenged those behind the National Cathedral project to open their financial records to public scrutiny, insisting that churches must know how contributions have been handled before being asked to help complete the controversial facility. He said any attempt to revive the project without first accounting for the money raised and spent would be premature, particularly given the questions surrounding the reported cost of the construction so far. The Founder and Prelate of Perez Chapel International said the first step should be to establish how much had come into the project, how much had been expended and what remained outstanding. “Let’s see what the account says first. And then when we see what the account says then we can know, because I know churches and us contributed some monies but we don’t know what the account is,” he said. He expressed concern about the reported GH¢97 million expenditure, saying he wanted to examine the accounts before supporting any proposal for the churches to take over the project. “If it’s true that GHC97 million was spent and that’s what we have, it’s a problem. And so I would wish that I could see the accounts,” he stated in an interview on Channel One TV on Monday, November 16, 2026. Archbishop Agyinasare disclosed that some churches, including his own, had made financial contributions towards the project but had not been given sufficient information about how the funds were accounted for. He said the financial position must be made clear before churches could determine whether they were willing and able to assume responsibility for completing the facility. Archbishop Agyinasare said the political divisions surrounding the cathedral should not be allowed to prevent an objective assessment of its future. “I think that the politics of it is a problem and we should move past the politics of it and then pick it up from there,” he said. Archbishop Charles Agyinasare wants cathedral retained for national use Despite his reservations about the project's finances, the archbishop said the site should not be abandoned, arguing that the substantial work already undertaken there should be considered in deciding its future. He proposed that the facility could be developed into a venue for important national events, including presidential swearing-in ceremonies and other major indoor state functions. He said such a use would give the project a broader national purpose beyond the original personal pledge that inspired its construction. The cathedral project was initiated under former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, who proposed the construction of a national worship centre and made a personal pledge towards it. The project subsequently became the subject of intense public debate over its financing, cost and management. In July 2025, the government disclosed findings from a Deloitte and Touche audit of the National Cathedral Secretariat covering 2021 to 2023. The report identified procurement breaches, questionable payments, weaknesses in financial controls and discrepancies in consultancy fees. One finding was an unexplained difference of about GH¢4.93 million between the amount the Office of the President recorded as paid to Sir David Adjaye & Associates and the amount the firm reported receiving. The government also disclosed that the total financial commitment to the project had reached US$97 million, comprising US$58 million already paid or committed and a further US$39 million outstanding to the contractor. It subsequently ordered a forensic audit to examine the project more comprehensively. In October 2026, the Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, announced that the construction site had been handed back to the government while the Attorney-General reviewed the forensic audit. The minister also confirmed that the Board of Trustees had been dissolved and that the government would not commit further public funds to the construction. The government's position is that the next steps will be determined after the Attorney-General's advice on the audit. Archbishop Agyinasare's intervention adds to the debate over whether the project should be completed through contributions from churches, repurposed for wider national use or subjected to a different arrangement.

Title: Belgium’s Lukaku retires from internationals
Content: Romelu Lukaku has retired from international football, saying he has "enjoyed every single moment" of playing for Belgium. Fenerbahce striker Lukaku, 33, made his international debut in 2010 and is Belgium's all-time leading men's goalscorer with 94 goals in 135 appearances. He is the fifth highest men's international goalscorer of all time, behind Sunil Chhetri, Ali Daei, Lionel Messi and leader Cristiano Ronaldo, who has scored 146. Lukaku scored eight goals across four World Cups, including in the run to the quarter-finals at this summer's tournament, and a total of six goals at three European Championships. Writing on Instagram,the former Everton, Chelsea and Manchester United forward thanked his team-mates and coaches "for pushing and trusting me to help the team" during his 16 years with the national side. He missed Belgium's Nations League win over Turkey last week with a hip injury and was an unused substitute on Sunday as they qualified for the last eight of the competition bybeating Italy 4-1. "These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team... I went through every emotion possible," Lukaku wrote. "To the Belgium fans thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in four World Cups and three European Championships. "I will never forget those moments. I'm at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing. It was enjoyable. I'm grateful." In 2023, Lukaku scored 14 times in eight Euro 2024 qualifying appearances, breaking the record for goals scored by a player in a European Championship qualifying campaign. His Belgium team-mate Kevin de Bruyneposted an image of himself with Lukaku, externalon Instagram adding: "There are no words to describe what you've meant to me and our country!"

Title: Wontumi offers to pay GH¢25m if the state drops his GH¢30m EXIM Bank case
Content: Chairman Wontumihas offered to pay the state GH¢25 million if prosecutors drop the GH¢30 million EXIM Bank fraud case against him, JoyNews reported early on Tuesday. The offer, made through his lawyer Samuel Atta Akyea, would leave GH¢5 million of the alleged loss unpaid. The Attorney-General's office has not responded publicly. The report said any deal would need the court's approval. It is not the first figure his team has put on the table. In July the stateturned down an earlier offer, with Deputy Attorney-General Dr Justice Srem-Sai saying the prosecution was not satisfied with it. According to the report, the state wanted the full GH¢30 million, plus interest. The talks began in June, when thecourt allowed both sides to negotiate a plea bargain. Atta Akyeatook over as lead counselin July and asked for time to finish them. They failed. In August the Accra High Courtordered the case to go to trial. Prosecutors thenfiled a fresh charge sheetin September. Thomas Antwi-Boasiako and Wontumi Farms Limited are charged alongside the former NPP Ashanti Regional Chairman, whose real name is Bernard Antwi-Boasiako. They face five counts between them: defrauding by false pretences, uttering forged documents (two counts), money laundering, and causing financial loss to a public body. Prosecutors allege that the two men obtained about GH¢14.3 million from EXIM Bank in 2018 for a farming project by false pretences, and that the bank lost GH¢30 million between 2018 and 2022. They also allege that a forged receipt was presented to the bank to support an application for a further GH¢4 million. Wontumi has pleaded not guilty. His lawyers have alsoasked the court to treat the case as a civil matter, arguing that the collateral and insurance on the loans are enough to pay them off. He is already serving a20-year jail term for illegal mining offenceslinked to Samreboi. On Monday the High Courtrefused him bail pending his appeal, ruling that the appeal had no likelihood of success. The Economic and Organised Crime Office is separatelyseeking to confiscate his assets, including GH¢50 million in Treasury bills.

Budget at a glance: primary balance target 0.5% of GDP (legal floor 0.5%; 2026 target 1.5%); capital expenditure GH¢100.4bn, or 5.6% of GDP; employment target: none stated for 2027 (unemployment below 8% by 2030); New Economy programme GH¢30bn in 2027. Against the 28 asks in ISODEC's pre-budget statement: 5 met, 15 partly met, 8 not met," the statement said. ISODEC also indicated that stabilisation must now make room for employment and production. It said that Ghana has made important progress on macroeconomic stabilisation, but the question for the 2027 Budget is how that progress will be used to address persistent unemployment, weak productive capacity and the country's exposure to foreign-exchange pressures. The fiscal framework should be judged by its effects on employment, inflation and the external balance, not by the pursuit of a fiscal ratio in isolation, it said. "The announced primary surplus target of at least 0.5 percent of GDP on a commitment basis, down from 1.5 percent in 2026, needs to be considered alongside capital expenditure of GH¢100.4 billion (GH¢120.5 billion including transfers), against a record of under-execution in 2026, when primary spending ran 3.4 percent below target to October. "While the GH¢30 billion New Economy allocation is welcome, the Budget speech does not yet set an execution target or commit to quarterly reporting of releases and spending by ministry, programme and region. The execution gap remains a serious concern: government must explain how it will ensure that approved capital allocations translate into completed projects and economic activity. Employment commitments need numbers, funding and accountability," it said. They acknowledge the removal of the cap on youth employment funding (an extra GH¢1 billion), GH¢2 billion for youth employment and skills, and the job projections for rice (about 125,000), oil palm (potential for more than 250,000) and pharmaceuticals (about 20,000). However, they said that the Budget speech does not set a 2027 employment target or a consolidated jobs target across the eight pillars, nor does it explain how jobs will be counted. "Unemployment below 8 percent (from 12.8 percent in 2025) is a 2030 goal only. Without these details, it is difficult to assess whether the announced programmes are commensurate with the scale of unemployment and youth exclusion. "The absence of a public employment guarantee pilot, particularly in deprived districts in Northern Ghana, is a missed opportunity. Government should use labour-intensive public investment in climate adaptation, irrigation, feeder roads, care and community services to provide paid work while meeting urgent development needs. Skills programmes must also be linked to vacancies and the requirements of productive firms."

Title: Tunisia and Ghana to enhance cooperation in vocational training, higher education, digital technology, women’s empowerment
Content: The Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, has received his counterpart, H.E. Mohammed Ali Nafti, the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Migration and Tunisians Abroad of the Republic of Tunisia, for a courtesy call at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Accra. During the engagement, Ablakwa welcomed his Tunisian counterpart and expressed Ghana’s commitment to strengthening bilateral relations between the two countries. He welcomed the proposals for enhanced cooperation and emphasised the need to expedite the finalisation of pending bilateral agreements. He also called for the revival of the Joint Commission between Ghana and Tunisia to provide a structured platform for advancing cooperation. The Minister identified several areas for enhanced collaboration, including vocational training, higher education, digital technology, women’s empowerment, aviation and sports. He further proposed a review of visa waiver arrangements for holders of diplomatic and service passports to facilitate official engagements. He also expressed Ghana’s interest in strengthening diplomatic representation in both countries through the reopening of a permanent Tunisian diplomatic mission in Ghana and the establishment of a Ghanaian Diplomatic Mission in Tunisia. In his remarks, H.E. Mohammed Ali Nafti reaffirmed Tunisia’s commitment to deepening relations with Ghana and proposed the development of a comprehensive action plan to assess existing cooperation, review achievements and identify new areas of collaboration. He highlighted the need to strengthen the legal framework governing relations between the two countries, particularly through the conclusion of pending agreements. He identified trade and investment, security and military cooperation, health, education, technology and maritime as key areas for enhanced partnership. He also proposed the organisation of economic forums in both countries to promote trade and investment and encouraged Ghana’s participation in major economic events in Tunisia. To conclude, both Ministers expressed their commitment to working together to advance the proposed initiatives and strengthen the longstanding relationship between Ghana and Tunisia. The visit took place last Friday.

Title: AFCON 2027 Qualifiers: Medeama’s Etse Dogli makes Black Stars debut in Somalia win
Content: Medeama SC midfielder Etse Dogli made his seniorBlack Starsdebut as Ghana secured a second consecutive victory over Somalia in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. Dogli’s appearance marks a major milestone in his career, having earned his maiden national team call-up following his impressive performances in the Ghana Premier League. The midfielder was among the five domestic-based players named in Ghana’s squad for the double-header against Somalia. His debut came as the Black Stars continued their resurgence in the qualifiers, having recorded a 2-0 victory in the first encounter on Thursday, November 12, before returning for Monday’s second leg.With Ghana leading 1-0 in the second game, Etse came on forAlidu Seiduin the 93rd minute as he helped Ghana to get the victory. Dogli’s progress from Division Two side Banana Inn FC to Hearts of Lions and subsequently Medeama has been a remarkable journey, culminating in his first appearance for the senior national team. The midfielder will be hoping to build on this opportunity and establish himself as a regular option for Ghana in future international assignments. The victories over Somalia have given Ghana a lifeline after a disappointing start to the qualifiers. However, the real test lies ahead, with crucial encounters against Côte d’Ivoire and The Gambia set to determine whether the four-time African champions can book their place at AFCON 2027.

Title: Fitch Solutions sees Ghana's 2027 spending at a 16-year high and inflation above 10%
Content: Fitch Solutions forecasts that Ghana's capital spending will reach a 16-year high in 2027 while headlineinflationclimbs back above 10 per cent in the second half of the year. Speaking at PwC Ghana's 2027 Post-Budget Forum in Accra on Monday, November 16, Fitch Solutions director Mike Kruiniger also put the cedi at an average of GH¢12.40 against the US dollar for 2027. The projections follow Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson's2027 Budget Statement, which plans GH¢389.2 billion in total spending and GH¢98.4 billion in capital expenditure, of which theNew Economy programme's first year takes GH¢30 billion. "We expect capital expenditure to rise to around 5% of GDP next year, which would be the highest level Ghana has seen since around 2010. So quite a substantial uptake," Kruiniger said. Fitch Solutions expects the higher investment drive to widen the fiscal deficit to about 2.7 per cent of GDP in 2027, the largest since 2023, while keeping the primary budget balance in surplus. "With the debt ratio having fallen below 50%, pretty low yields on domestic treasuries, pretty robust amount of GDP growth, we think that fiscal risks stemming from the increase remain very much limited as we go into 2027," he said. On prices, Kruiniger warned that the disinflation that broughtheadline inflation to 5.5 per cent in October 2026, according to theGhana Statistical Service, will gradually reverse and breach the government's 8 ± 2 per cent target band. He pointed to global El Niño weather disruptions pushing up prices of imported staples such as wheat and rice, adding that higher food inflation will squeeze real incomes and household budgets in late 2027. Those dearer food imports, combined with domestic money supply growth, moderating gold price gains andBank of Ghana reserve accumulation, are expected to pressure the cedi to an average of GH¢12.40 per dollar next year.

Title: ECG cuts power in Tema, Eastern and Ashanti areas from today until Tuesday
Content: TheElectricity Company of Ghanahas published power cut schedules for parts of Tema, Eastern and Ashanti regions from today, Sunday, until Tuesday, November 17. The utility posted thenotices on Xon Sunday morning, covering emergency maintenance in Tema today, planned works on Tuesday, and faults its engineers are fixing in Tema and Ashanti. It is the latest in a run of November maintenance schedules from the power distributor, which earlier publishedoutage lists for Accra East and Temacovering November 8 to 13. Today, Sunday, November 15.Two emergency maintenance outages hit Tema, while three faults have cut supply elsewhere: Tuesday, November 17.Planned maintenance will cut supply in the Eastern Region from 8:00am to 1:00pm and in the Kpong enclave from 10:00am to 3:00pm, in a schedule similar toFriday's Eastern and Western outages. ECG says the maintenance works are to improve service delivery, and it has apologised for the inconvenience. Itsfault noticessay engineers are working to fix the faults and restore supply. The notices seen by 3News cover Sunday and Tuesday only, with no ECG-published schedule for Monday or Wednesday.

Title: Don't click that Microsoft 'fix': CSA and NITA warn of scams after the outage
Content: Ghana's Cyber Security Authority (CSA) and the National Information Technology Agency (NITA) are telling people not to fall for scam messages that use this week's Microsoft outage as bait. In ajoint alertdated November 13, the two agencies say criminals are pretending to be Microsoft or IT support staff, sending fake "fixes" and "restored access" links, or asking people to verify their accounts. Microsoft services, including Outlook, went down on Thursday, November 12. The CSA says they have since been restored, though some users may still see intermittent faults. Anyone who gets an unexpected message about the outage, a password reset or an account check should not click its links or open its attachments, however genuine it looks, the agencies say. It follows a similar CSA warning aboutfake speeding-fine messagessent from ordinary phone numbers to steal bank card details. The alert says no one should share passwords, one-time codes or multi-factor approval prompts. Microsoft never asks for them by email, text message or phone call. It also tells people to check the sender's full email address, treat urgent or threatening messages with suspicion, and double-check the recipient before sharing sensitive documents on messaging apps. Cyber incidents cost Ghana GH¢209.7 million in nine months,the CSA has said, withonline fraud alone making up 47 per cent of reported cases. Anyone who receives a suspicious message can report it to the CSA on short code 292 by call or text, on WhatsApp on 0501603111, or by email to report@csa.gov.gh. NITA can be reached on govdap@nita.gov.gh or 055 249 9661, according to the joint alert, which carries the reference CSA/CERT/MPA/2026-11/02.

Title: Wirtz double helps Germany thrash Netherlands
Content: Florian Wirtz scored twice as Germany thrashed the Netherlands in their final Nations League game - with both sides qualifying for the quarter-finals. Jurgen Klopp's side started the day third in Group A2 but overtook Greece and the Netherlands into top spot. All three teams ended on 11 points - with results between them being used as the tiebreaker instead of goal difference. The Netherlands would have finished top of the group had Germany only won 4-0. Greece, who beat Serbia 1-0 thanks to a Giorgos Masouras goal, placed third. Freiburg's Derry Scherhant scored his first international goal, curling a fine effort into the top corner in Berlin. Liverpool attacking midfielder Wirtz won the ball before firing in Germany's second from outside the box. Borussia Dortmund defender Nico Schlotterbeck headed in Brajan Gruda's free-kick to make it 3-0. Gruda then cut the ball back for Wirtz to lash in his second goal. And Gruda, on loan at Leipzig from Brighton, made it two goals in two caps - to go with his two assists in Berlin - as he made it 5-0. It was Germany's biggest victory against their neighbours since 1959 when they won 7-0. "We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second half," Wirtz told German broadcaster ARD. "We don't mind who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent - and I think we did that perfectly. "We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we've taken some great steps in our development as a team." The Netherlands, who beat Greece 7-0 on Friday, finished second after their first defeat under Xavi Hernandez.

Title: Mahama assures of export restrictions, levy to protect local cashew processors
Content: President John Dramani Mahama has announced a raft of measures to shield Ghana’s local cashew processors from competition for raw nuts, including a three-month export ban and a levy on raw cashew exports. Speaking at the commissioning of the Nadkansco Cashew Processing Factory in Techiman, the President reiterated his government’s commitment to strengthening the local cashew processing industry and said the state would create a more favourable environment for processors to operate. Following the Ivorian model President Mahama said Ghana would borrow from the approach of neighbouring Côte d’Ivoire, one of the world’s leading cashew producers, which has put measures in place to protect its domestic processors. “We are going to implement conditions that Ivory Coast is implementing to protect the local processors,” he said. Three-month export ban on raw nuts Under the planned arrangement, raw cashew nuts will be kept in the country for at least three months after harvest, giving local processors first access to supply before any exports are permitted. “No export from Ghana for a period of three months for the local processors to have access to the raw cashew,” the President declared. Levy on raw nut exports The President also announced that a levy will be placed on exports of raw cashew nuts once exports are allowed, with the proceeds earmarked to support local processors. “A levy will also be put on export of raw nuts and proceeds would be used to support local processors,” he said. GHS148.4 million factory The Nadkansco factory, located in Techiman in the Bono East Region, was funded at a cost of GHS148.4 million by the Ghana Export-Import Bank (GEXIM). A further GHS12 million was allocated for capacity building. The facility is designed to process about 31,000 tonnes of raw cashew nuts annually. Incentives under the 24-hour economy policy At the commissioning, Mr. Mahama also announced new business incentives under the government’s 24-hour economy policy. These include a one-year deferment of duties and levies on imported manufacturing equipment, aimed at helping firms expand their plants. The announcements signal the government’s intent to move Ghana up the cashew value chain, keeping more of the crop’s value in the country rather than exporting it in raw form.

Title: ‘Your cedi can fund terrorism’: GIS tells Ghanaians to stop giving to street beggars
Content: The Ghana Immigration Service has told the public to stop giving to street beggars, warning that “your cedi can fundterrorism.” The flyer wasposted on the Service’s verified Facebook pageon Saturday, November 14, without a caption. It carries the hashtag #StopMigrantBegging, the number 030 732 5089 and the GIS website address. “Stop giving to street beggars,” its second line reads. The flyer shows a woman handing something to people seated on a pavement, under a large red “STOP” stamp. It comes afterGIS apprehended 1,055 people, 662 of them children, in raids on begging networks in Accra and Kumasi in August. The flyer does not explain how money given to a beggar could reach terrorists, or what the phone number is for. GIS set out its thinking in June, when Deputy Comptroller-General Faisal Disu, in charge of Command Post and Operations, said “Ghana is currently attracting a lot of bad actors into the country.” He said proceeds from begging networks could potentially be used to finance terrorism. In August, Interior Minister Muntaka Mubarak Mohammed saidmore than 3,000 migrant beggars and illegal immigrants had been removed from Ghana since 2025. By early Tuesday the flyer had drawn about 11,500 reactions, 1,700 comments and 1,600 shares. The commonest question in the comments was how the beggars got into Ghana at all. Many said border control is the Service’s own job. Others called for tighter borders, with drones on unapproved routes and more patrols. Some pointed out that many areECOWAScitizens with a right to enter. Others defended giving as a religious duty or because the people are hungry; one suggested food rather than money. A few asked whether the campaign is xenophobic, and a smaller group backed it. In September,PAG presidential candidate Dr John Kpikpi criticised the planned deportation of those rounded up in August, saying Ghana should not copy xenophobic actions elsewhere in Africa. In April, GIS said the ECOWAS Free Movement Protocol guarantees visa-free travel, residence and establishment rights for citizens of member states, and that its operations target criminal exploitation and irregularities, not legitimate regional mobility. “The Ghana Immigration Service remains resolute in safeguarding Ghana’s borders and enforcing immigration laws, while upholding our obligations under the ECOWAS Protocol,” Comptroller-General Samuel Basintale Amadu said then. It followedan early-morning operation in Kumasi that rescued 606 people from begging networks. It said 381 were children, and that many of those rescued were believed to be victims of trafficking and forced begging. GIS also reminded the public that the Beggars and Destitute Act, 1969 (NLCD 392) prohibits street begging by citizens and non-citizens. Offenders face fines, up to three months in prison, or both.

Title: Ghana EXIM Bank commits $12m to NADKANSCO cashew processing factory – Sylvester Mensah
Content: The Ghana Export-Import Bank (Ghana EXIM Bank) has committed approximately $12 million to support the establishment and operations of NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited in Techiman. The Chief Executive Officer of the Bank, Sylvester Adinam Mensah, disclosed this during the commissioning of the factory by President John Dramani Mahama on Monday, November 16, 2026. He said the financing was aimed at supporting the acquisition of modern processing equipment, providing working capital and training workers to equip them with the skills needed to operate the facility. "We saw jobs created close to where our people live so that no one would leave home to earn a decent living elsewhere. And we saw an opportunity to prove that large-scale cashew processing can succeed in Ghana. That is why the Ghana Export-Import Bank committed approximately the equivalent of 12 million U.S. dollars to this project," he said. According to Mr Mensah, more than $3 million of the funding went into the acquisition of automated processing equipment, while additional financing was provided to support the factory's working capital requirements. He explained that the investment was informed by the need to retain more value from Ghana's cashew production by processing the nuts locally rather than exporting them in their raw state. "Mainly for state-of-the-art automated processing equipment, alongside working capital and training to equip the workforce with the skills that the work demands. Your Excellency, the President, the automated equipment that we find here across this factory was committed by Ex-Im Bank at a cost slightly in excess of 3 million U.S. dollars.  The working capital, which is the crux of the matter, amounted to not less than 110 million." Mr Mensah said the bank saw the project as more than a commercial venture, describing it as an opportunity to create employment, support local farmers and demonstrate that large-scale cashew processing could thrive in Ghana. He noted that Ghana produced more than 262,000 metric tonnes of raw cashew nuts last year, but only about 17,000 metric tonnes were processed locally. The remainder was exported in its raw form, depriving the country of potential jobs, skills development and additional economic value. The NADKANSCO facility has an installed capacity to process up to 33,000 metric tonnes of raw cashew nuts annually, almost twice the volume processed across the entire country last year. Mr Mensah said the factory had already employed nearly 1,000 people directly and supported an additional 3,000 livelihoods across the cashew value chain. He said the facility would produce cashew kernels, cashew nut shell liquid and briquettes for export, while supplying cashew cakes, briquettes and roasted kernels to the domestic market. He further urged the company's management to expand operations and utilise the factory's full production capacity, assuring them of the bank's continued support through affordable, long-term financing.

Title: Ghana has about 20 heart surgeons for 35 million people, specialist warns
Content: Ghana has only about 20 cardiac surgeons serving a population of about 35 million, a heart specialist has warned, leaving children with heart defects waiting too long for surgery. Dr Eugene Nana Atuahene-Ampadu, who works as a resident cardiothoracic surgeon at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital'sNational Cardiothoracic Centre(NCTC), said too few specialists and equipped centres had left children needing operations waiting for long periods. He made the remarks during the launch event for the Beating Odds Foundation, which helps children born with heart defects and supports their families as a non-governmental organisation. “Parents or guardians have to then wait. And of course, it increases their anxiety, knowing that I have my ward and my ward maybe requires surgery, but perhaps I have not been able to undergo surgery or surgery has not been done for my child yet,” he said. He said the delays increased the emotional and financial burden on families. Dr Atuahene-Ampadu called for more hospitals able to carry out heart operations nationwide to cut waiting times and widen access to specialised care. The NCTC, the heart centre at Korle Bu, says its mission covers patient care, training and research, with the aim of becoming the leading centre for cardiothoracic and vascular disease management in Sub-Saharan Africa. Korle Bu opened anew cardiac catheterisation laboratorythis year, and the Health Minister has urged accountability in how it is run. The2027 Budget also promises a mother-and-child centre at the hospital. He added that the centre relied on support from international partners, including Boston Children's Hospital, to strengthen its operations. The Beating Odds Foundation links families looking for care to donors and other backers, while campaigning on heart defects in children. Founder Phyllis Dodd urged individuals, companies and other willing supporters to back its work. Heart surgery is also performed outside Korle Bu: the University of Ghana Medical Centre this yearcarried out a life-saving heart operation on a patient with a rare tumour, supported by the MahamaCares Fund.

Title: Up to 62 tonnes of mercury enter Ghana illegally every year, researcher estimates
Content: Between 42.5 and 62 tonnes of mercury enter Ghana through illicit channels every year for use in small-scale gold mining, a researcher has estimated. Dr Sylvester Akpah, chief executive of Smart Innovation Ghana Limited, gave the estimate at a United States Embassy symposium in Accra on mercury pollution and sustainable mining, the Ghana News Agency reported. His warning followsan EU-backed study reporting excess mercury in roughly 94 per cent of soil sampled at galamsey sites in the Savannah Region. Dr Akpah said the mercury came in through unidentified routes despite port controls, and that small-scale mining supported more than 2.5 million people directly or indirectly. He said communities hosting mines in Western, Ashanti, Eastern and Central regions took a heavy hit, with Tarkwa and surrounding areas under severe environmental pressure. Anearlier assessment by Africa Pure Earth with the Environmental Protection Agencyalso pointed to high mercury levels in Ghana's water bodies. Mercury attacks the kidneys, lungs and brain, Dr Akpah said, while theWorld Health Organization sayseven small exposures can cause serious harm, especially to unborn children. Professor Daniel Nukpezah of the University of Ghana's Institute for Environment and Sanitation Studies said mercury did not break down in the environment and could turn into methylmercury in water, accumulating in fish and entering the food chain. The danger to babies is well documented:mercury crosses the placenta, leaving babies with reduced brain development. The WHO lists mercury among ten chemicals of greatest concern to public health. Dr Akpah urged tighter enforcement of current rules and uptake of lower-mercury technologies, such as gold-catching equipment he said was still little used. He said Ghana had signed up to the Minamata Convention on Mercury, yet enforcement stayed difficult, with no dedicated national directorate overseeing mercury use in mining.

Title: Agyinasare says Mahama’s second term outperforms first
Content: Founder of Perez Chapel International, Archbishop Dr Charles Agyinasare, has rated President John Dramani Mahama’s second administration ahead of his first, citing improvements in the performance of the cedi, government payments and the financing of public projects. He said the developments since Mr Mahama returned to office showed signs of progress, particularly efforts to meet outstanding financial obligations and undertake some projects without resorting to additional borrowing. Archbishop Agyinasare also cited increased flight activity between Ghana and other countries as an indication of growing commercial activity and movement of goods. He recounted that during a trip from India in September, he was informed that Emirates was operating two daily flights to Ghana, a development he considered encouraging. “They told me Emirates was coming to Ghana twice a day. So I came with the midnight flight, and there was a seven o’clock flight. Now, that should show you that people have started going out to buy things. That alone, for me, was an encouragement,” he said. The renowned preacher further pointed to the performance of the local currency and the government's efforts to clear some outstanding bills as indicators of improvement. “I see the cedi has done well. I see we’ve been able to pay some of our bills,” he stated. He also referenced the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy presented to Parliament by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson on November 12, particularly the government's account of payments made and projects being undertaken without new borrowing. “Some of the projects we are doing, we are not borrowing money for them. That, for me, I think, is progress,” Archbishop Agyinasare added. He made the assessment during an interview on Channel One TV on Monday, November 16, where he gave his views on the performance of the Mahama administration since its return to power. “I think he’s done better than the first term,” he said.

Title: Retaining the incumbent regional chairman is the surest bet for Ashanti NDC
Content: Mohammed Yakubu, the Member of Parliament (MP) for Ahafo Ano South-East, has described the re-election of Mr Andrews Nana Akwasi as Ashanti Regional Chairman of the NDC as the surest bet for maximising the party’s votes in the Election 2028. He explained that keeping the current regional leadership in place would help consolidate the gains already made and provide the party with a stable base from which to pursue its electoral ambitions in the Ashanti region. Speaking to the Ghana News Agency, after the regional executive elections, the MP said it was time for the past executives and the currently elected ones to deduce more winning strategies ahead of the 2028 general elections. He said the period offered an opportunity for both past and newly elected executives to reflect on the lessons of the previous contest and work out more effective and winning strategies that would strengthen the party’s fortunes. Mr Yakubu noted that a divided house could not progress and that the leadership must prioritise reconciliation to have a formidable force to ensure victory in the general elections. He therefore urged the party’s leadership to reach out to those who lost the elections and bring them on board so that the NDC could present a united front in the region. To him, the chairman-elect deserved the victory, acknowledging the good work he did in the 2024 general elections in ensuring that the NDC votes appreciated in the region and moved the Parliamentary seat to seven in the region. He said the outcome reflected the confidence that the party faithful had in the regional leadership and the efforts made to strengthen the NDC’s presence in the Ashanti Region. The MP enumerated some development projects in his constituency, citing the building of a 24-Hour Economy Model Market, construction of over twenty boreholes in various communities, and building new school blocks, among others. Mr Yakubu called on the Ahafo Ano South-East constituents to exercise restraint while he delivered on the mandate for which he was voted for.

Title: Oti Regional Minister highlights government development projects
Content: John Kwadwo Gyapong, Oti Regional Minister, has highlighted development projects being undertaken by the John Dramani Mahama-led government in the region, urging residents to acknowledge efforts to improve infrastructure and social services. He mentioned road projects under the government’s Big Push initiative, including the Dodo-Pepesu-Nkwanta, Nkwanta-Kpassa, Nkwanta-Dambai and Okadjakrom-Kwamekrom roads, describing them as significant interventions expected to improve transportation, connectivity and economic activities across the region. Mr Gyapong made these remarks during a media engagement on the sidelines of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) Oti Regional Executive Elections held at the Bueman Senior High School (BUSEC) in Jasikan on November 14. He also cited the proposed university at Jasikan, the Oti Regional Hospital project, the establishment of 24-Hour Economy Markets across the region, the proposed airport at Dambai and the Dambai Bridge project as other major development initiatives. He said the President was expected to cut the sod for the Oti Regional Hospital project soon, expressing optimism that its construction would improve access to healthcare services and reduce the challenges residents faced in seeking specialised medical attention. The Regional Minister said the projects demonstrated the government’s commitment to fulfilling its development promises, adding that the people of the region had reasons to appreciate the interventions. According to him, the government had moved beyond promises to implementing projects that would address critical infrastructure and development needs in the region. He further disclosed that several other interventions, including the construction of school blocks, Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) compounds and water supply facilities, were being undertaken across the region’s nine districts. Mr Gyapong therefore challenged journalists to visit the various communities to independently assess the projects and report on their implementation and impact on residents. He said media practitioners had an important responsibility to provide accurate information on development initiatives and their benefits to the people. He urged the media to give adequate attention to ongoing development projects in the region to enable residents to appreciate the interventions and hold relevant authorities accountable for their implementation.

Title: Ghana exports to China surge under zero-tariff policy3 hours
Content: Ghana’s exports to China rose sharply following the implementation of China’s zero-tariff policy, with imports from Ghana reaching US$290 million in June 2026. The initiative is expected to expand market access for Ghanaian products and create opportunities for local exporters seeking to enter the Chinese market. Mr Cong Song, Chinese Ambassador to Ghana, announced this at the 2026 Scholarship Alumni Association Reception and China-Ghana Zero-Tariff Forum in Accra. He said bilateral trade between Ghana and China reached $14.12 billion in 2025, while Ghana’s exports to China amounted to $2.67 billion, representing a 33.9 per cent increase over previous years. The forum, organised by the MOFCOM Scholars Alumni Association of Ghana (MOSAAG), formed part of a nationwide capacity-building initiative on China’s zero-tariff concession for African countries. Mr Cong said the policy would reduce the cost of African products entering the Chinese market and improve their competitiveness. He said China’s removal of tariffs on African goods would strengthen confidence in Africa’s economic prospects, support international trade and attract new investment. “The zero-tariff policy is offered unilaterally, with no requirement for African countries to open their markets reciprocally. There is no ceiling on the volume of African exports to China. “It comes with no political strings attached…For African countries, this means the door of opportunity to China’s mega-market of 1.4 billion people is wide open,” he said. The Ambassador highlighted ongoing cooperation between Ghana and China across the mining value chain, including geological exploration, local processing, value addition and skills development. He urged Chinese businesses operating in Ghana to comply with local laws and regulations and called for a conducive environment for investment. Mr Cong encouraged MOSAAG to deepen public awareness of the zero-tariff initiative, identify export opportunities and help address implementation challenges. “Let us join hands to harness the momentum of China’s zero-tariff treatment, and use the certainty of high-level bilateral opening-up and cooperation to offset the uncertainties in the global environment, injecting sustained and strong momentum into Africa’s development,” he said. In a speech read on his behalf, Mr Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Minister for Foreign Affairs, said the government remained committed to partnerships that supported industrialisation and economic transformation. “Our interest is not to only to attract investment into the country; we seek partnerships that establish local production facilities, develop domestic supply chains, strengthen the skills of our workforce and create decent and sustainable jobs,” he said. The Minister urged Ghanaian exporters to meet Chinese market requirements to fully benefit from the policy and deepen trade relations between the two countries. He said the government would continue efforts to strengthen domestic production, improve competitiveness and create a business environment conducive to enterprise growth. Mr Leonard Edem Cosmos, President of MOSAAG, said the forum sought to equip producers, agro-processors and small and medium-sized enterprises with the knowledge required to access the Chinese market. “Knowing that duties have been removed is only the first step; knowing how to navigate sanitary and phytosanitary standards, packaging regulations, rules of origin, logistics, and Chinese buyer expectations is where real trade happens,” he said. Mr Cosmos said the association would support capacity-building efforts, connect Ghanaian businesses with credible Chinese partners and promote effective implementation of the zero-tariff policy.

Title: BoG warns strong El Niño could affect food prices, cocoa and cedi3 hours
Content: Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Monday warned that an unusually strong El Niño episode could affect agricultural production across West Africa, including Ghana. He said the Pacific Ocean warming phenomenon, which disrupts global weather patterns, could persist into the first quarter of 2027, with implications for food prices, domestic agricultural output, cocoa production, export earnings, inflation and the exchange rate. He gave the warning at the opening of the final Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting for 2026 in Accra, where members are expected to review developments during the year and assess whether further adjustments to policy instruments may be necessary. Urging the Committee to consider weather-related risks in its 133rd meeting, Dr Asiama said an unusually strong El Niño episode could affect agricultural production across West Africa into the first quarter of the following year. He said the development could have implications for food prices, domestic agricultural output, Ghana’s cocoa production and export earnings, with possible effects on inflation and the exchange rate. The Governor urged the Committee to provide a comprehensive assessment of the potential transmission channels, their implications for the domestic economic outlook and measures to manage the associated risks effectively. He also highlighted the broader risks to domestic agriculture, noting that lower production could affect rural incomes, food availability and growth in the agricultural sector. Dr Asiama emphasised that cocoa, one of Ghana’s major export commodities, remained particularly exposed, as adverse weather conditions could disrupt production and reduce export volumes. Any shortfall in cocoa output could directly affect export earnings, which had been an important source of strength for the external sector and reserve accumulation, he said. Beyond the El Niño threat, the MPC, at its 133rd meeting, would consider domestic and external developments, including the global economic outlook, geopolitical developments and commodity prices. On the domestic front, the Committee would assess the recent uptick in inflation and inflation expectations, developments in the external sector and reserves, and the effectiveness of monetary policy. It would then make appropriate recommendations on the monetary policy stance as the Bank prepared for 2027. The Committee is expected to announce its decision at the end of the meeting on Wednesday, November 18. At its September meeting, the Committee maintained the policy rate at 14 per cent, marking its third consecutive hold after similar decisions in May and July. This followed reductions from 18 per cent to 15.5 per cent in January and subsequently to 14 per cent in March, amid declining inflation and improving macroeconomic stability.

Title: Opoku-Agyemang rallies collective responsibility for quality education3 hours
Content: Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has called for sustained collaboration between government and stakeholders to make quality education a shared national responsibility. She said expanding access to education must go hand in hand with improved teaching, better facilities, stronger parental support, and better learning outcomes. Prof. Opoku-Agyemang made the call at the Mfantsipim School’s 150thAnniversary celebration at Cape Coast, held on the theme: “A Legacy of Excellence, Leadership and Service to Inspire the Future.” Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, the Asantehene, attended the event, along with Osabarimba Kwesi Atta, the Paramount Chief of Oguaa, government officials, traditional and religious leaders, alumni, and education stakeholders. She congratulated the Mfantsipim community on the school’s 150 years of service, describing the institution as integral to Ghana's history of formal secondary education and praising its role in nurturing generations of young men. Prof. Opoku-Agyemang said the anniversary should not be viewed as a celebration for Mfantsipim alone, but as an opportunity for the country to reflect on the future of secondary education. She said Ghanaians needed to consider what kind of secondary education the nation required and what steps it would take to achieve it. To her, success in schools depended not only on the government, but also on teachers, school leadership, parents, alumni, and how seriously students approached their education. She said the government’s responsibility included expanding access to quality education, providing infrastructure, ensuring trained teachers were available, and maintaining standards. These measures supported Ghana’s broader ambition to build an economy that produced more of what it consumed, added value to agricultural produce, developed industry, and created meaningful jobs, she said. The Vice President said the government was taking steps to expand secondary-school capacity while improving quality and equity. She said already some senior high schools had returned to single-track operation, and that work was ongoing to complete previously stalled infrastructure projects. She also cited recent investments in the sector, including the commissioning of the Paga Senior High School E-Block and a $300 million financing agreement signed in 2026, to support secondary education, with emphasis on access, relevance, and learning outcomes. She said the 2027 budget had allocated GH¢1.3 billion to improve secondary education and eliminate the double-track system. The Vice President said these investments were meant to provide adequate school facilities, restore instructional time, and ensure expansion was matched by better-quality education. Prof. Opoku-Agyemang said Ghanaian education needed to prepare young people for a rapidly changing world shaped by technology, scientific advancement, climate change, and changing employment patterns. At the same time, she urged schools to uphold the enduring values of discipline, character, integrity, and service. She highlighted Mfantsipim’s motto, Dwen Hwe Kan – “Think and Look Ahead” – noting that choosing Fante, rather than Latin or English, reflected confidence in African identity, independence, and education as a route to self-realisation. Mr Haruna Iddrisu, the Minister for Education, strongly assured that the government would recruit 10,000 teachers in 2027, as indicated in the 2027 Budget presented to Parliament. He said 2,000 of the planned recruitments would go to non-teaching staff, creating opportunities for labourers, drivers, and other support personnel in the education sector. He commended Mfantsipim School for its contribution to Ghana’s educational history since its establishment in 1876, noting that the institution had nurtured generations of students and promoted discipline, intellectual curiosity and service. Reverend Ebenezer Aidoo, the Headmaster of Mfantsipim School, said the school’s 150th anniversary is a powerful legacy of vision, sacrifice, excellence and service. He expressed profound gratitude for inheriting a remarkable institution and said that the present generation’s duty was to preserve its values, strengthen its foundations and prepare it for an even greater future. He honoured the pioneering missionaries, educators, church leaders, benefactors, former Headmasters, teachers and staff whose sacrifices laid the foundations on which the school stands. He also urged old boys to unite in service, uphold integrity and use their time, talent, resources and influence for the good of others. He reminded the students that they had inherited a great name but must live responsibly through honesty, discipline, faith and service, adding that Mfantsipim was a living trust whose light must last forever.

Title: Ghana now Africa’s eighth-largest economy, second in West Africa – Mahama tells Investment Summit3 hours
Content: President John Dramani Mahama has hailed Ghana’s economic recovery, declaring the country as “one of Africa’s most resilient and promising economies” as he opened the Ghana Investment Summit 2026 in Accra. Addressing investors and business leaders at the 2026 Ghana Investment Summit, the President said Ghana had made significant progress after a period of economic reform, restoring stability, rebuilding confidence and putting the economy on a stronger growth path. “In 2025, Ghana’s Gross Domestic Product reached approximately $114 billion, positioning the country as the 8th largest economy in Africa and the 2nd largest in West Africa,” President Mahama said. He added that the International Monetary Fund projects Ghana’s GDP to reach $128.64 billion by the end of 2026, with the country set to maintain its current position as Africa’s eighth largest economy and second largest in West Africa. “Our economy also grew by six per cent in 2025 and is projected to grow by 5.7 per cent in 2026. This figure would have been much higher if the bombs had not started flying in Iran,” the President said. “Inflation has fallen sharply from 23.5% in January 2025 to 5.5 per cent in October 2026, bringing greater stability to the business environment,” he said. President Mahama said the nation’s external reserve position had also strengthened considerably, adding that gross International Reserves stood at $12.05 billion in September 2026, representing 4.5 months of import cover. This was supported by a strong trade surplus of $8.86 billion in the first eight months of 2026, he stated. President Mahama said the primary balance also recorded a surplus of 1.6 per cent of GDP, exceeding the fiscal target and that the country’s public debt had remained broadly stable at 45 per cent of GDP as of July 2026. He noted that poor negotiation of the debt restructuring risked drawing Ghana into a second catastrophic debt default. However, fiscal discipline and competent management of the economy had kept them on track in honouring their domestic and external debt obligations, and their aim was to achieve investment grade by the year 2030, he stated. “Our currency, the Cedi, has shown greater stability, supported by stronger foreign exchange reserves and improved external balances.” President Mahama said the nation’s currency appreciated by 40.7 per cent against the US dollar in 2025 and remained about seven per cent stronger in September 2026 than it was in September 2025. He said in August 2026, Ghana’s Business Confidence Index stood at 107.8, while the Consumer Confidence Index reached 111.9, and that the Composite Index of Economic Activity also expanded by 14.9 per cent year-on-year in July 2026. This positive outlook, the President said, was also reflected in Ghana’s sovereign credit rating. He reiterated that S&P Global affirmed Ghana’s B-/B rating with a stable outlook, while Fitch upgraded the country’s rating from B- to B with a positive outlook. Again, Moody upgraded the long-term foreign currency and local currency issuer ratings to B-3 from CAA-1 and revised the outlook to stable. Together, these indicators pointed to an economy on stronger footing, providing greater confidence and a more stable foundation for investment, production and long-term business growth. He said in addition, Ghana had enjoyed more than three decades of constitutional democracy, peaceful transitions of power, respect for the rule of law and strong institutions, which had provided the stability and predictability needed for long-term investments. “We are also distinguished by the openness of our society, the warmth of our people, the ease with which international businesses can build relationships here, and Ghana’s longstanding reputation as a welcoming place to live and do business,” the President said. He said Ghana was home to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat, giving businesses access to the wider African market of about 1.4 billion people, with a combined GDP of approximately $3.4 trillion. President Mahama said beyond Africa, businesses that establish production in Ghana benefit from preferential access to some of the world’s largest consumer markets. He said qualified Ghanaian exports enjoy duty-free and quota-free access to the United Kingdom under their Ghana-UK Interim Trade Partnership Agreement, and to the European Union under the EU-Ghana Interim Economic Partnership Agreements. He said Ghana also benefits from the China Preferential Federal Tariff Arrangements for African Countries and benefits from the African Growth and Opportunities Act (AGOA), of the United States. President Mahama said the economy they were building should be visible in the everyday lives of their people, stating that a farmer should sell more of his harvest to a nearby processor. He urged Ghanaian businesses to use the summit to find partners who could help them expand production, improve technology, and enter new markets. To the nation’s financial institutions and development partners, the President asked them to work with project sponsors to structure financing that matches the time needed to build and grow productive enterprises. He also extended invitations to investors from Africa and around the world to invest in Ghana.

Title: Governor Asiama urges vigilance as MPC holds final 2026 meeting3 hours
Content: Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), has cautioned against complacency as the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) holds its final meeting for 2026. He said although Ghana’s economy remained resilient amid global uncertainty, risks to the inflation outlook persisted, making the 133rd MPC meeting an opportunity to assess economic developments over the year. Dr Asiama said this when he opened the 133rd and final MPC meeting for 2026 in Accra on Monday. The meeting was expected to examine domestic and external economic conditions and determine the policy rate for the end of the year. He noted that the country’s macroeconomic stabilisation process remained on track, citing single-digit inflation, strong economic activity and substantial external surpluses. The gains, he said, had been supported by credible and disciplined policy implementation, effective liquidity management and reforms introduced in 2025 to the foreign exchange operations and reserve management framework. “However, we cannot afford to be complacent. We remain conscious of the risks to the inflation outlook, and the need to strengthen the economy’s resilience while responding appropriately to these risks as they evolve,” Dr Asiama said. The meeting, he noted, would assess the effectiveness of policy measures, consider whether further adjustments to policy instruments were necessary, and reflect on the priorities and challenges ahead as the Bank prepared for 2027. On the global economy, Dr Asiama said conditions had remained relatively resilient, with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) projecting global growth of about 3.1 per cent in 2026. He said growth would be supported partly by strong investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and other technology-related activities, although geopolitical fragmentation and supply chain disruptions remained significant sources of uncertainty. “The implications for global commodity prices, trade and financial conditions will need to be carefully assessed,” he said, warning that the uncertainties could affect Ghana’s economic outlook in the coming months. On domestic conditions, Dr Asiama said macroeconomic conditions remained stable and broadly positive, but noted a modest increase in headline inflation from 5.2 per cent in September to 5.5 per cent in October 2026. While inflation remained below the medium-term target band, he said the recent increase warranted careful examination, particularly the contributions of food, non-food and services inflation. He urged the Committee to monitor inflation expectations closely and determine whether the recent movements reflected temporary adjustments in fuel, transport and administered prices or signalled a more persistent shift in underlying price-setting behaviour. He also highlighted the external sector as an important source of strength to the economy, urging the Committee to look beyond headline surpluses to assess reserve accumulation and underlying vulnerabilities. Dr Asiama said the Committee would assess the appropriateness of the current monetary policy stance in light of recent macroeconomic developments and the outlook, with its decision to be announced after deliberations.

Title: Bank of Ghana maintains Monetary Policy Rate at 29% amid inflation concerns
Content: The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Ghana has maintained the policy rate at 29 percent citing recent inflation pressures and exchange rate volatility. Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr. Ernest Addison, addressing journalists in Accra on Monday, stated that while headline inflation has declined from peak levels, the pace of disinflation has slowed down considerably. The committee observed that risks to the inflation outlook remain elevated, driven primarily by upward adjustments in utility tariffs and transportation costs. Dr. Addison emphasized that the central bank remains committed to steering inflation back towards the medium-term target band of 8 plus or minus 2 percent. Economic growth continues to show resilience, supported by the services and agriculture sectors, although fiscal consolidation under the International Monetary Fund program remains critical for macroeconomic stability.

The Governor reiterated the central bank's unwavering stance to maintain a tight monetary policy posture until inflation firmly returns to the target band of 8±2 percent. Private sector credit growth remained subdued as commercial banks adopted cautious lending practices.

Title: Bank of Ghana freezes policy rate at 29% for third consecutive time
Content: The Bank of Ghana has announced that its Monetary Policy Committee decided to hold the monetary policy rate steady at 29 percent. Governor Dr. Ernest Addison told reporters during a press conference in Accra that inflationary pressures and cedi depreciation were the primary factors behind the decision. He noted that although price growth slowed earlier in the year, recent energy tariff hikes and food supply constraints pose renewed risks. The central bank plans to keep monetary policy sufficiently restrictive to achieve price stability under Ghana's ongoing three-billion-dollar IMF bailout.

Title: EC extends voter exhibition exercise by two days nationwide

Title: Supreme Court defers ruling on suits challenging Human Sexual Rights and Family Values Bill
Content: The Supreme Court of Ghana has deferred judgment on two injunction applications seeking to restrain Parliament and President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo from transmitting and assenting to the Human Sexual Rights and Family Values Bill 2024. A seven-member panel presided over by Chief Justice Gertrude Torkornoo indicated that the court will deliver its ruling alongside the substantive constitutional suits challenging the legality of the bill. The plaintiffs, broadcast journalist Richard Dela Sky and researcher Dr. Amanda Odoi, contend that Parliament breached Article 108 of the 1992 Constitution regarding private members' bills imposing financial obligations on the consolidated fund. Speaker of Parliament Alban Bagbin, through his legal team, argued that the apex court lacks jurisdiction to halt legislative processes.

Counsel for Parliament opposed the application, asserting that judicial interference with the legislative arm undermines the separation of powers.

Title: Cocobod moves to self-finance cocoa purchases after 32 years of offshore syndication loans
Content: The Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) has announced a historic shift in its financing strategy, terminating its 32-year reliance on offshore syndicated loans to finance annual cocoa bean purchases. Chief Executive Officer of COCOBOD, Joseph Boahen Aidoo, told journalists in Accra that the board will instead adopt a domestic self-financing mechanism starting in the 2024/2025 crop season. Aidoo stated that high international interest rates and conditionalities on syndicated commercial loans had made offshore borrowing unsustainable for the cocoa sector. He emphasized that the new internal financing model will save Ghana over 150 million dollars in interest payments and financial transaction charges.

The agency plans to collaborate with local banks and international chocolate manufacturers for forward sales agreements to ensure timely payment to cocoa farmers across the country without incurring hefty interest burdens.

Title: Fuel prices projected to fall by up to 4% in second pricing window of August - COPEC
Content: The Chamber of Petroleum Consumers (COPEC) has projected a reduction in pump prices of petroleum products starting August 16 for the second pricing window. Executive Secretary of COPEC, Duncan Amoah, stated that the anticipated price reduction is attributable to relative stability in the foreign exchange market and a decline in international benchmark crude prices. Petrol prices are expected to drop from an average of 14.20 cedis to 13.80 cedis per litre, while diesel is expected to average 14.50 cedis per litre. COPEC urged Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) to reflect the favorable international price changes at their retail pumps to give relief to transport operators and Ghanaian consumers.

Petrol prices are expected to drop from an average of 14.20 cedis to 13.80 cedis per litre, while diesel is expected to average 14.50 cedis per litre.

Title: Good news for drivers as COPEC announces upcoming reduction in petrol and diesel prices
Content: Petroleum consumers in Ghana are set to enjoy lower fuel prices in the second half of August according to the Chamber of Petroleum Consumers. Duncan Amoah of COPEC explained that international crude price drops coupled with cedi performance will result in a 3 to 4 percent decrease in retail pump rates across the country.

Title: Education Minister rejects calls to review Free Senior High School policy funding model
Content: Minister of Education, Dr. Yaw Osei Adutwum, has reaffirmed the government's commitment to fully funding the Free Senior High School (Free SHS) policy, dismissing calls from civil society and opposition figures to allow affluent parents to pay boarding fees. Speaking at the launch of the National STEM Education roadshow in Kumasi, Dr. Adutwum insisted that introducing cost-sharing would undermine equity and exclude vulnerable students from rural communities. He noted that secondary school enrollment has doubled since the policy's inception in 2017, with academic performance in WASSCE improving consistently across core subjects.
